pins.title: Vertical City
pins.description:
A crowded city plan is read as falling puzzle blocks and rebuilt upward in white card and coloured plastic, freeing the ground while furnished rooms show life inside the stacks.

Physical model and drawing | High-density city study | Wooden strips, museum board, plastic | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 垂直城市
zh-Hant.description:
擁擠的城市平面被解讀為落下的拼圖方塊，再以白色卡紙與彩色塑膠向上重建，釋放地面，同時以配置家具的房間呈現量體中的生活。

實體模型與繪圖｜高密度城市研究｜木條、博物館板、塑膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In very dense cities, buildings are squeezed into tight and irregular shapes. The project asked how stacking these shapes upward could release space on the ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在極度密集的城市中，建築被擠壓成緊密而不規則的形狀。這個專題探問，把這些形狀向上堆疊如何能釋放地面的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A two-dimensional plan recorded the compressed footprints of a crowded district as interlocking blocks. These blocks were compared to the falling pieces of a stacking puzzle game.
captions: A Tetris screenshot that inspired the block shapes.
A published section drawing of Kowloon Walled City, the reference for stage two.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張二維平面把擁擠街區被壓縮的基地輪廓記錄為互鎖的方塊。這些方塊被比擬為堆疊益智遊戲中落下的方塊。
captions: 啟發方塊形狀的俄羅斯方塊截圖。
第二階段參考的九龍城寨剖面圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: In three phases, the low blocks were lifted and combined into taller volumes with coloured plastic panels. Each phase opened more of the base while keeping the variety of shapes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 在三個階段中，低矮的方塊被抬升並結合為帶有彩色塑膠板的更高量體。每個階段都釋放更多底面，同時保留形狀的多樣性。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises as a cluster of towers above an open base. Small furniture models and interior rooms show how daily life could fit inside the compact units.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型如一群塔樓升起於開放的底座之上。小型家具模型與室內房間顯示日常生活如何能容納於精簡的單元之中。

sections.heading: Lifted Blocks - Returning the Ground to the City
sections.body: Extreme density turns urban space into a puzzle in which every building is pressed into whatever shape remains. This project began from that observation, recording the compressed footprints of a crowded district in a two-dimensional plan of interlocking blocks. The pattern immediately recalled the falling pieces of a stacking puzzle game, suggesting that the same shapes might be rearranged in height rather than spread across the ground. An original block model reproduced the dense plan, and three successive phases then lifted, rotated and combined its pieces into taller volumes clad with coloured plastic panels. With each phase, more of the base was released as open public ground, while the variety of forms was carefully preserved. The refined model rises as a cluster of towers whose gaps admit light and views. At a smaller scale, white furniture models and furnished interiors tested how daily life could fit inside compact units, from desks and shelves to bunk beds. The guidance encouraged moving between the scale of the city and the scale of the room.

zh-Hant.heading: 抬升的方塊-把地面還給城市
zh-Hant.body: 極度的密度把城市空間變成一道拼圖，每一棟建築都被擠進剩下的任何形狀。這個專題從這個觀察開始，把擁擠街區被壓縮的基地輪廓記錄在一張互鎖方塊的二維平面中。這個圖形立刻讓人聯想到堆疊益智遊戲中落下的方塊，暗示同樣的形狀可以在高度上重新排列，而不是攤開在地面上。原始的方塊模型重現了密集的平面，接著三個連續階段把其中的構件抬升、旋轉並結合為覆以彩色塑膠板的更高量體。每經過一個階段，就有更多底面被釋放為開放的公共地面，形式的多樣性則被小心保留。精修後的模型如一群塔樓升起，其間的縫隙引入光線與視野。在更小的尺度上，白色家具模型與配置家具的室內，測試日常生活如何容納於精簡單元之中，從書桌、層架到上下鋪。指導鼓勵在城市與房間兩種尺度之間來回思考。

pins.title: Wave Park
pins.description:
Lines drawn from tidal ripples are triangulated into a net and folded in card and wooden strips into a park of angular pavilions that shelter different activities.

Physical model and drawing | Natural pattern study | Wooden strips, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 波浪公園
zh-Hant.description:
從潮汐漣漪描繪出的線條被三角化為網，再以卡紙與木條摺成一座由角狀亭子構成、容納不同活動的公園。

實體模型與繪圖｜自然紋理研究｜木條、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The park of folded pavilions from above.
從上方看摺紙亭子構成的公園。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The ripples formed by changing tides are full of movement but have no fixed form. The project asked how their pattern could become an open space for people.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 潮汐變化所形成的漣漪充滿運動，卻沒有固定的形式。這個專題探問，它們的紋理如何能成為供人使用的開放空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Lines were drawn to follow the shades of rippling water and extended into geometric figures. Two line studies were then merged into one dense net of triangles.
captions: A photograph of tidal ripples that inspired the project.
A first line study of ripples.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 線條順著水波的明暗被描繪，並延伸為幾何圖形。兩張線條研究接著被合併為一張密集的三角網。
captions: 啟發本案的潮汐波紋照片。
漣漪的第一張線條研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The triangle structure was folded in card and braced with wooden strips into a three-dimensional concept model. Its peaks and hollows suggested small spaces for gathering.
captions: The concept model of folded triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三角結構以卡紙摺出，並以木條支撐，成為立體的概念模型。其峰與谷暗示了可供聚集的小空間。
captions: 摺疊三角形的概念模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final park spreads many angular pavilions across an open ground, each sheltering a different activity. Figures sit, climb and pass beneath the folds as if walking among frozen waves.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的公園把許多角狀亭子散布在開放的地面上，每一座庇護不同的活動。人形在摺面下坐著、攀爬與穿行，彷彿走在凝固的波浪之間。

sections.heading: Folded Tides - A Shore Made of Triangles
sections.body: Water at the edge of the sea never holds a shape for long, yet its ripples follow patterns that can be read and drawn. This project began from a lifelong affection for the coast, tracing lines along the shifting shades of rippling water and extending them into geometric figures. Two such studies were overlaid and merged into a dense net of triangles, translating fluid motion into a structure of straight edges. The net was then folded in card and braced with wooden strips, producing a concept model of sharp peaks and sheltered hollows. Read at the scale of the body, these folds suggested places to sit, gather, climb and pass through. The final park spreads many angular pavilions across an open ground, each tuned to a different activity, while single pavilion studies refine their stances and openings. Small figures moving beneath the folds appear to wander among frozen waves. The guidance valued the patient translation of natural phenomena into buildable geometry, showing how a familiar landscape can inspire a generous public space.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺起的潮汐-由三角形構成的岸
zh-Hant.body: 海邊的水從不長久維持一種形狀，它的漣漪卻遵循著可以被閱讀與描繪的紋理。這個專題源自對海岸長久的喜愛，沿著水波變換的明暗描繪線條，並把它們延伸為幾何圖形。兩張這樣的研究被疊合並合併為一張密集的三角網，把流動的運動轉譯為直線構成的結構。這張網接著以卡紙摺出，並以木條支撐，產生一個由尖峰與庇蔭凹處構成的概念模型。以身體的尺度閱讀，這些摺面暗示了可以坐下、聚集、攀爬與穿越的地方。最終的公園把許多角狀亭子散布在開放的地面上，每一座對應不同的活動，單座亭子的研究則細修其姿態與開口。在摺面下移動的小小人形，彷彿漫步於凝固的波浪之間。指導重視把自然現象耐心轉譯為可建造的幾何，顯示熟悉的地景也能啟發寬廣的公共空間。

pins.title: House of Porosity
pins.description:
A plain cube is opened into a four-by-four frame of sticks, and black-and-white grid patterns decide which cells stay solid and which stay porous, creating rooms of light, shadow and stairs.

Physical model and drawing | Density and porosity study | Wooden strips, PVC foam board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 孔隙之屋
zh-Hant.description:
一個簡單的立方體被打開為四乘四的木條框架，黑白格紋決定哪些格子保持實心、哪些保持通透，形成光、影與樓梯交織的房間。

實體模型與繪圖｜密度與孔隙研究｜木條、PVC發泡板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final cube with stairs and figures.
帶有樓梯與人形的最終立方體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Houses are essentially boxes, yet rolling, folding or cutting can turn a box into rich space. The project asked how one cube could hold many different experiences through changes in density.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 房屋本質上是盒子，但捲曲、摺疊或切割可以把盒子變成豐富的空間。這個專題探問，一個立方體如何透過密度的變化容納多種不同的體驗。
captions: 作為起點的實心立方體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sixty-three ways of colouring a four-by-four grid in black and white were drawn as a catalogue. Selected patterns were layered in observation drawings to map solid and open cells.
captions: Layered patterns mapped onto the cube.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以黑白為四乘四網格上色的六十三種方式被繪成一份目錄。選出的圖案在觀察繪圖中疊合，以標示實心與開放的格子。
captions: 六十三種黑白網格圖案。
疊合後對應到立方體的圖案。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The cube was rebuilt as an open frame of sticks, and panels were inserted where the patterns were dark. Stairs then threaded through the cells to link every room.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 立方體以木條重建為開放框架，並在圖案深色之處插入板片。樓梯接著穿過格子，把每一個房間串連起來。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model offers dark and bright, crowded and wide, quiet and lively rooms side by side. Visitors can move freely between them along a web of white stairs.
captions: The model against a dark ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型讓幽暗與明亮、擁擠與寬敞、安靜與熱鬧的房間並列。訪客可沿著白色樓梯織成的網絡在其間自由移動。

sections.heading: Measured Hollows - A Cube That Breathes Through Its Cells
sections.body: Every house can be read as a box, and this project asked what happens when a single box is made to contain contrasting worlds. Its starting point was a plain white cube, which was opened into a four-by-four frame of slender sticks so that its interior became a field of cells. A systematic catalogue of sixty-three ways to colour a small grid in black and white supplied the rules. Selected patterns were layered in observation drawings and projected onto the faces of the frame, deciding which cells would be closed with panels and which would remain open to air and light. The result was a carefully measured gradient of density and porosity. White stairs were then threaded through the openings, turning the abstract grid into a sequence of rooms to be climbed, crossed and inhabited. Moving through the finished model, one passes from darkness to brightness, from crowding to openness, and from stillness to motion. The guidance emphasised method, showing how a disciplined set of patterns can generate rich and varied spatial experience.

zh-Hant.heading: 度量的空洞-以格子呼吸的立方體
zh-Hant.body: 每一棟房屋都可以被讀作一個盒子，這個專題探問，當一個盒子被要求容納彼此對比的世界時會發生什麼。它的起點是一個簡單的白色立方體，被打開為由纖細木條構成的四乘四框架，使內部成為一片格子的場域。一份以黑白為小網格上色的六十三種方式的系統目錄提供了規則。選出的圖案在觀察繪圖中疊合，並投射到框架的各個面上，決定哪些格子以板片封閉，哪些保持向空氣與光線開放。結果是一道經過仔細度量的密度與孔隙漸層。白色樓梯接著穿過這些開口，把抽象的網格轉化為可攀登、穿越與居住的一連串房間。在完成的模型中移動，人會從幽暗走向明亮，從擁擠走向開闊，從靜止走向運動。指導強調方法，顯示一套嚴謹的圖案如何能生成豐富而多樣的空間體驗。

pins.title: Emerging Division
pins.description:
A photograph of scattered toy pieces is abstracted into shapes, lines and a triangulated net, then built in paper, swabs and wooden strips into a layered tower of sharp folded planes.

Physical model and drawing | Image-to-space study | Wooden strips, PVC foam board, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 浮現的分割
zh-Hant.description:
一張散落玩具積木的照片被抽象為形狀、線條與三角網，再以紙、棉棒與木條建成一座由尖銳摺面層疊而成的塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜圖像到空間研究｜木條、PVC發泡板、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A memory of childhood play returns as a heap of small scattered pieces, unconnected and out of order. The project asked how such a fragmented image could break out of the photograph into three-dimensional space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 童年遊戲的記憶以一堆散落的小構件重現，彼此不相連也沒有順序。這個專題探問，這樣破碎的圖像如何能從照片中突破，進入三維空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The photograph was reduced to grey blocks and split into three layers by tone. The outlines were then traced as line drawings and joined into a dense net of triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 照片被簡化為灰色方塊，並依明暗分成三層。輪廓接著被描成線條圖，並連結成一張密集的三角網。
captions: 簡化為灰色方塊的構件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cotton-swab frames tested the net as a structure, and folded paper walls tested how sharp planes could be cut and suspended. A concept drawing stacked these layers into one tower.
captions: Folded paper walls with cut planes.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 棉棒框架把三角網測試為結構，摺紙牆則測試尖銳平面如何被切割與懸掛。一張概念圖把這些層疊成一座塔。
captions: 帶有切割平面的摺紙牆。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises in three platforms linked by leaning planes and bundles of sticks. It could serve as a café, a park, a passage or a playground.
captions: The model seen from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以三層平台升起，之間由傾斜的平面與成束的木條連接。它可以是一間咖啡館、一座公園、一條通道或一處遊樂場。

sections.heading: Scattered Memory - Building Upward from Fragments
sections.body: Memories of childhood rarely arrive as a story; they surface as fragments without sequence, like a heap of small toys tipped onto the floor. This project took such an image as its material and asked how it might leave the flat photograph and become space. The picture was first reduced to grey blocks, then separated by tone into three layers, each a scattered field of rectangles. Tracing their outlines produced a series of restless line drawings, which were finally joined into a dense triangulated net. That net was tested in two directions. Frames of cotton swabs explored it as a lightweight structure, while folded paper walls with cut and suspended triangles explored it as a surface of light and shadow. A concept drawing stacked these findings into a tower of three platforms. In the final model, leaning planes and bundles of wooden strips rise between the floors, suggesting a café, a park, a passage or a playground. The guidance encouraged open interpretation, treating a fragmented memory as a generous starting point for architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 散落的記憶-從碎片向上建造
zh-Hant.body: 童年的記憶很少以故事的形式到來，它們以沒有順序的碎片浮現，像是一堆被倒在地板上的小玩具。這個專題把這樣的圖像當作材料，探問它如何離開平面的照片而成為空間。圖片首先被簡化為灰色方塊，再依明暗分成三層，每一層都是一片散落的長方形場域。描繪它們的輪廓產生一系列躁動的線條圖，最後被連結成一張密集的三角網。這張網朝兩個方向被測試。棉棒框架把它探索為輕盈的結構，而帶有切割與懸掛三角形的摺紙牆，則把它探索為光與影的表面。一張概念圖把這些發現疊成一座三層平台的塔。在最終模型中，傾斜的平面與成束的木條在樓層之間升起，暗示一間咖啡館、一座公園、一條通道或一處遊樂場。指導鼓勵開放的詮釋，把破碎的記憶視為建築一個寬廣的起點。

pins.title: Deep-Sectional Urbanism
pins.description:
Mechanical drawings are collaged into four section scenes of daily life, then built in card, tracing paper and wooden strips as a dense city where a cut-through view is always visible.

Physical model and collage | Machine city study | Wooden strips, PVC foam board, tracing paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 深度剖面都市
zh-Hant.description:
機械圖被拼貼為四幅描繪日常生活的剖面場景，再以卡紙、描圖紙與木條建成一座密集的城市，在其中總能看見剖開的景象。

實體模型與拼貼｜機械城市研究｜木條、PVC發泡板、描圖紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Machines play a growing role in every part of daily life, from cranes to intelligent software. The project asked what a city would become if its factories, buildings and homes were all made of machines.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 從起重機到智慧軟體，機器在日常生活的每一部分扮演越來越重要的角色。這個專題探問，如果工廠、建築與住宅全都由機器構成，城市會變成什麼模樣。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Mechanical elements were studied in detail and recombined into section collages. Four collages describe scenes of life inside a machine-built world.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 機械元件被仔細研究，並重新組合為剖面拼貼。四幅拼貼描繪了機器建成的世界中的生活場景。
captions: 第三與第四幅剖面拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The collages were printed on card and tracing paper and joined by a frame of wooden strips. Each face was arranged so that a section remains visible from any side.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 拼貼被印在卡紙與描圖紙上，並以木條框架連接。每一個面都經過安排，使得從任何一側都能看見剖面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model reads as a dense city of cut-open buildings linked by bridges and platforms. Walking around it reveals layer after layer of machine interiors.
captions: A close view of the layered faces.
Bridges and platforms across the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型宛如一座由剖開的建築構成、以橋與平台相連的密集城市。繞著它行走，可以看到一層又一層的機械內部。

sections.heading: Cut-Open City - Living Inside the Machine
sections.body: Urbanisation and mechanisation are often described as twin trends of the present, yet they are rarely imagined as a single fabric. This project pushed the two together, asking what life would look like if factories, buildings and even homes were entirely composed of machines. It began with close studies of mechanical parts, gears, shafts, wheels and casings, drawn with the precision of technical illustration. These elements were then cut apart and recombined into four section collages, each describing an everyday scene inside a machine-built world, from domes and towers to rooms nested within engines. The collages were printed onto card and tracing paper and assembled with a frame of wooden strips into a three-dimensional city. Its faces were arranged so that a cut-open section is always visible, whichever side one approaches. Bridges and platforms tie the fragments together, inviting the eye to travel from one interior to the next. The guidance encouraged speculative thinking grounded in careful drawing, showing how sectional representation can become an architectural world in its own right.

zh-Hant.heading: 剖開的城市-居住在機器之中
zh-Hant.body: 都市化與機械化常被描述為當代的兩股趨勢，卻很少被想像為同一片紋理。這個專題把兩者推到一起，探問如果工廠、建築甚至住宅完全由機器構成，生活會是什麼模樣。它從對機械零件的細緻研究開始，齒輪、轉軸、輪子與外殼都以技術插圖般的精確度被描繪。這些元素接著被切開並重新組合為四幅剖面拼貼，每一幅都描繪機器建成的世界中的一個日常場景，從穹頂與塔樓到嵌在引擎中的房間。拼貼被印在卡紙與描圖紙上，並以木條框架組裝成一座立體的城市。它的各個面經過安排，無論從哪一側接近，總能看到一個剖開的斷面。橋與平台把這些碎片連結起來，引導視線從一個內部移向下一個。指導鼓勵以細緻繪圖為基礎的推測性思考，顯示剖面的表現方式本身也能成為一個建築的世界。

pins.title: Dreamy Lemon Shop
pins.description:
The glowing tissue of a thin lemon slice inspires a shop of soft white floors, ramps and stems rising from a shimmering hologram ground.

Physical model and drawing | Natural form study | Hologram paper, PVC panels, super light clay, hemp rope | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 夢幻檸檬店
zh-Hant.description:
薄薄檸檬切片中發光的組織，啟發了一間由柔軟白色樓板、坡道與莖柱構成，從閃爍全息地面升起的商店。

實體模型與繪圖｜自然形態研究｜全息紙、PVC板、超輕黏土、麻繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The lemon shop rising from a hologram ground.
從全息地面升起的檸檬店。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A lemon cut into a thin slice reveals delicate tissue that glows when light passes through it. The project asked how this natural rhythm of light and division could shape an architectural space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 切成薄片的檸檬顯露出細緻的組織，在光線穿透時發出光芒。這個專題探問，這種光與分隔的自然節奏如何能塑造建築空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Backlit slices were studied closely to read the radiating segments and the soft walls between them. Their regular yet living separation became the key to the design.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 逆光的切片被仔細研究，以解讀放射狀的瓣與其間柔軟的隔膜。這種規律卻充滿生命的分隔成為設計的關鍵。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Conceptual drawings transformed the slice into spirals, curved stems, scooped blocks and hanging forms. These pieces suggested floors, ramps and supports for a small shop.
captions: The conceptual drawing of transformed forms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 概念繪圖把切片轉化為螺旋、彎曲的莖、挖空的量塊與懸吊的形體。這些構件暗示了一間小店的樓板、坡道與支撐。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Soft white floors of clay rest on branching stems above a field of hologram paper. A long ramp links the levels, and light scatters across the ground like juice in the sun.
captions: The ramp leading to the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 黏土做成的柔軟白色樓板棲於分枝的莖柱上，下方是一片全息紙場域。一條長坡道連接各層，光線在地面上散射，如陽光下的果汁。
captions: 分枝莖柱上的層疊樓板。

sections.heading: Glowing Segments - A Shop Grown from a Slice of Light
sections.body: A lemon is an ordinary fruit until it is cut thin and held against the light, when its hidden tissue suddenly glows like a stained window. This project began from such a chance discovery and asked whether the rhythm inside a slice could become a place. Close study of backlit slices revealed radiating segments separated by soft, translucent walls, a structure that is regular yet clearly alive. Conceptual drawings then loosened this order into a vocabulary of spirals, curving stems, scooped blocks and pendant forms, each suggesting a part of a building. The final model translates that vocabulary into a small shop. Rounded floors of white clay rest on branching stems, a long ramp winds between them, and tiny figures climb toward an upper platform. Beneath everything lies a shimmering ground of hologram paper, which scatters coloured light in the way a lemon catches the sun. The guidance encouraged patient looking at everyday things, showing how a moment of delight in the kitchen can grow into a convincing spatial idea.

zh-Hant.heading: 發光的瓣-從一片光中長出的商店
zh-Hant.body: 檸檬是一種平凡的水果，直到它被切薄並迎著光舉起，隱藏的組織才突然如彩色玻璃窗般發光。這個專題從這樣一次偶然的發現出發，探問切片內部的節奏能否成為一個場所。對逆光切片的仔細研究，揭示出由柔軟半透明隔膜分開的放射狀瓣片，一種規律卻明顯充滿生命的結構。概念繪圖接著把這種秩序鬆開，化為螺旋、彎曲的莖、挖空的量塊與懸垂形體的語彙，每一種都暗示建築的一部分。最終模型把這套語彙轉譯為一間小店。白色黏土做成的圓潤樓板棲於分枝的莖柱上，一條長坡道在其間蜿蜒，小小的人形攀向上方的平台。一切之下是一片閃爍的全息紙地面，以檸檬捕捉陽光的方式散射彩色的光。指導鼓勵耐心觀看日常事物，顯示廚房裡的一個愉悅瞬間也能長成令人信服的空間構想。

pins.title: Under Water
pins.description:
Branches seen through clear water are extracted into lines and shapes, then rebuilt as a suspended frame of wooden strips, coloured parchment triangles and elastic threads.

Physical model and drawing | Water and refraction study | Wooden strips, PVC panels, coloured parchment paper, transparent elastic rope | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 水下
zh-Hant.description:
透過清澈水面看到的枝條被萃取為線條與形狀，再以木條、彩色羊皮紙三角形與彈性細繩重建為一個懸吊的框架。

實體模型與繪圖｜水與折射研究｜木條、PVC板、彩色羊皮紙、透明彈性繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The suspended frame of sticks and coloured triangles.
木條與彩色三角形構成的懸吊框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Branches under water appear broken and shifted by the moving surface above them. The project asked how the world below the water and the light refracted at its surface could be built as one structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 水下的枝條被上方流動的水面折斷並偏移。這個專題探問，水面下的世界與水面折射的光如何能被建成同一個結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Submerged branches were photographed and their ideology extracted as dotted lines and shapes. Bold black extractions captured how stems split and bend at the surface.
captions: A bold extraction of the branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 沉在水中的枝條被拍攝下來，其意象被萃取為虛線與形狀。粗黑的萃取圖捕捉到莖在水面處分裂與彎折的樣子。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden strips were joined into open polyhedra to stand for the branches. Coloured parchment triangles and transparent elastic rope were added for the underwater world and the refracted light.
captions: The model hanging from a branch.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條被連接成開放的多面體，代表枝條。彩色羊皮紙三角形與透明彈性繩被加入，代表水下世界與折射的光。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished frame hangs from a single branch and divides into an upper and a lower world. Under light it casts layered shadows that recall the unpredictable shimmer of water.
captions: The frame lit in the dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的框架懸掛在一根枝條下，分成上下兩個世界。在光線下，它投下層層陰影，令人想起水面難以預測的閃爍。
captions: 在黑暗中被照亮的框架。

sections.heading: Refracted Branches - A Frame Between Air and Water
sections.body: Looking into still water, one sees branches that seem to bend, break and drift, as if the surface were rewriting the world beneath it. This project took that optical puzzle as its brief. It started with photographs of submerged twigs and reeds, followed by drawings that extracted their character as dotted lines, broken strokes and bold black wedges. These studies revealed a vocabulary of sudden angles where a stem meets the surface and changes direction. The model then translated this vocabulary into a suspended structure. Slender wooden strips were joined into open polyhedra that read as branches, while triangles of red, yellow and blue parchment marked the hidden world below. Transparent elastic rope stretched across the frame stands for the refracted light, almost invisible until it catches a reflection. Hung from a single found branch, the piece divides into an upper and a lower realm, and under a lamp it throws layered shadows that tremble like ripples. The guidance encouraged careful extraction from observation, revealing how an everyday glance can generate a precise and poetic structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 折射的枝條-介於空氣與水之間的框架
zh-Hant.body: 望進平靜的水面，人會看到枝條彷彿彎曲、斷裂並漂移，好像水面正在改寫其下的世界。這個專題把這道光學謎題當作設計任務。它從拍攝沉在水中的細枝與蘆葦開始，接著以繪圖把它們的特質萃取為虛線、斷續的筆觸與粗黑的楔形。這些研究揭示了一套突然轉折的語彙，出現在莖與水面相遇並改變方向之處。模型接著把這套語彙轉譯為懸吊的結構。纖細的木條被連接成開放的多面體，讀起來如同枝條，而紅、黃、藍的羊皮紙三角形則標示出下方隱藏的世界。橫越框架拉開的透明彈性繩代表折射的光，幾乎看不見，直到它捕捉到一道反光。懸掛在一根拾得的枝條下，作品分成上下兩個領域，在燈光下投出如漣漪般顫動的層層陰影。指導鼓勵從觀察中仔細萃取，揭示日常的一瞥如何能生成精確而富詩意的結構。

pins.title: Car Bloom
pins.description:
The streamlined body and sharp edges of a sports car are drawn apart into wings, grilles and windows, then folded in white PVC into a flowing pavilion and garden.

Physical model and drawing | Form transformation study | PVC panels, transparency film | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 車之綻放
zh-Hant.description:
跑車的流線車身與銳利邊緣被拆解為翼、進氣格柵與車窗，再以白色PVC摺成一座流動的亭子與花園。

實體模型與繪圖｜形態轉化研究｜PVC板、透明膠片｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A sports car combines a perfectly streamlined shape with an angular, forceful impact. The project asked how these qualities could be carried from a vehicle into architecture.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 跑車結合了完美的流線形體與稜角分明、充滿力量的衝擊感。這個專題探問，這些特質如何能從車輛轉移到建築之中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The car was drawn apart into parts such as the wing, headlight, window, intake grille and cavity. Each sketch recorded how a part creates layers when seen from different angles.
captions: Sketches of the car taken apart.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 車子被拆解繪製為翼、頭燈、車窗、進氣格柵與車腔等部件。每一張速寫記錄了一個部件從不同角度觀看時如何形成層次。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Several paper models tested how flow could be created by bending and folding strips. The best studies were rebuilt in PVC panels as a shell of layered curves.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 數個紙模型測試如何透過彎曲與摺疊紙條創造流動感。最好的研究以PVC板重建為一個由層疊曲線構成的殼。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model spreads into a public garden of curving paths, ramps and canopies. Small trees and figures show people strolling beneath the streamlined roofs.
captions: A curving path through the shell.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型展開為一座由彎曲小徑、坡道與頂棚構成的公共花園。小樹與人形顯示人們在流線屋頂下漫步。

sections.heading: Speed at Rest - Streamlines Unfolding into a Garden
sections.body: A fast car is designed to cut through air, yet its sweeping lines also hold a sculptural calm that invites a slower kind of looking. This project grew from a childhood habit of collecting small model cars and asked how that admiration might be turned toward architecture. Rather than copying the vehicle, it drew the body apart into separate parts, wing, headlight, window, intake grille and inner cavity, studying how each produces overlapping layers as the viewpoint shifts. A series of quick paper models then explored how bending and folding a single strip can generate flow and a sense of enclosure. The most convincing of these were rebuilt in white PVC panels, producing a shell of interleaved curves that lift, twist and settle onto the ground. In the final model the shell becomes a public garden, where ramps rise into canopies, paths slip between folds and small trees stand in sheltered courts. Tiny figures stroll at an unhurried pace beneath forms born from speed. The guidance encouraged transforming a personal passion into an architectural method of analysis and making.

zh-Hant.heading: 靜止的速度-展開為花園的流線
zh-Hant.body: 一輛快車的設計是為了劃破空氣，但它掃掠的線條也蘊含一種雕塑般的沉靜，邀請一種更緩慢的觀看。這個專題源自童年收集小型模型車的習慣，探問這份欣賞如何能轉向建築。它沒有模仿車輛，而是把車身拆解為獨立的部件，翼、頭燈、車窗、進氣格柵與內部車腔，研究每一個部件在視點移動時如何產生重疊的層次。一系列快速的紙模型接著探索，彎曲並摺疊一條紙帶如何能產生流動感與圍合感。其中最具說服力的研究以白色PVC板重建，形成一個由交錯曲線構成的殼，抬起、扭轉並落定於地面。在最終模型中，殼體成為一座公共花園，坡道升為頂棚，小徑在摺面之間穿梭，小樹立於有遮蔽的庭院。小小的人形以從容的步調漫步於由速度所生的形體之下。指導鼓勵把個人熱愛轉化為一套分析與製作的建築方法。

pins.title: Nest of Sticks and Triangles
pins.description:
A nest-like tower of glued wooden strips is followed by a net of scalene triangles, built in sticks, card and PVC to study winding lines and the shadows they cast.

Physical model and drawing | Structure and shadow study | Wooden strips, cardboard, PVC panels, red threads | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 枝條與三角之巢
zh-Hant.description:
一座以膠黏木條構成的巢狀塔之後，是一張不等邊三角形的網，以木條、卡紙與PVC建成，研究蜿蜒的線條及其投下的陰影。

實體模型與繪圖｜結構與陰影研究｜木條、卡紙、PVC板、紅線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The nest-like tower of glued sticks.
膠黏木條構成的巢狀塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Buildings with walls of interlaced timber can look both complicated and remarkably tidy. The project asked how a new combination of glue and slender sticks could create a firm yet airy structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 以交織木料構成牆面的建築，看起來既複雜又出奇地整齊。這個專題探問，膠與纖細木條的新組合如何能創造堅固而通透的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Birds build some of the most remarkable structures in nature, binding twigs with their own saliva. This study of nests guided a tower of short sticks glued at many angles.
captions: The nest-like timber lattice of the Sunnyhills store in Tokyo, the precedent that started the project.
21_21 Design Sight in Tokyo, whose inclined planes and scalene triangles shaped the models.
The tower and its long shadow.
The dense base of the nest.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 鳥類建造了自然界中最非凡的一些結構，以自身的唾液黏合細枝。對鳥巢的這項研究，引導出一座以短木條從多個角度黏合而成的塔。
captions: 啟發本案的東京微熱山丘店鳥巢狀木格構。
東京 21_21 Design Sight，其傾斜量體與不等邊三角形影響了模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A second study turned to inclined structures made of scalene triangles. Drawn nets were rebuilt as a hanging bowl of triangles, rippling card strips and a fan of PVC fins.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二項研究轉向由不等邊三角形構成的傾斜結構。繪製的網被重建為懸掛的三角形碗體、起伏的卡紙條帶與一扇PVC鰭片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Under strong light the models cast separated, flickering shadows across the wall. The shadows became part of the design, extending each structure into the surrounding space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在強光下，模型在牆上投下分離而閃動的陰影。陰影成為設計的一部分，把每個結構延伸到周圍的空間中。

sections.heading: Bound Twigs - Structures That Write in Shadow
sections.body: Travel often sharpens the eye, and this project grew from encounters with buildings whose timber walls appear at once tangled and orderly. Seeking the logic behind that impression, it turned to the nests of birds, among the most ingenious constructions in nature, where twigs are bound together by saliva into forms of surprising strength. Short wooden strips were glued at shifting angles into a tall, porous tower, so that no single stick dominates and the whole holds firm through countless small joints. A second line of inquiry looked at inclined structures composed of scalene triangles. Drawn nets of uneven triangles were rebuilt as a hanging bowl of folded panels, a field of rippling card strips and a fan of thin PVC fins, each testing how winding lines and gaps might divide light. Photographed under a strong lamp, the models throw separated, flickering shadows that seem to move across the wall. The guidance encouraged reading precedents through first principles, showing how observation of nature and structure can produce a personal and poetic language of making.

zh-Hant.heading: 黏合的細枝-以陰影書寫的結構
zh-Hant.body: 旅行常常使眼光更加敏銳，這個專題源自與一些建築的相遇，它們的木構牆面看起來同時糾結又井然有序。為了尋找這種印象背後的邏輯，它轉向鳥巢，自然界中最巧妙的構造之一，細枝以唾液黏合成強度驚人的形體。短木條以不斷變化的角度黏合，成為一座高而多孔的塔，沒有任何一根木條佔主導，整體依靠無數細小的接點保持穩固。第二條探索路線則研究由不等邊三角形構成的傾斜結構。繪製的不規則三角網被重建為摺板構成的懸掛碗體、一片起伏的卡紙條帶，以及一扇纖薄的PVC鰭片，每一件都測試蜿蜒的線條與縫隙如何分割光線。在強燈下拍攝時，模型投下分離而閃動的陰影，彷彿在牆上移動。指導鼓勵從基本原理閱讀先例，顯示對自然與結構的觀察如何能產生一種個人而富詩意的製作語言。

pins.title: The Machine Age
pins.description:
Machine drawings are collaged into imagined engines and an industrial skyline, then grown into a city of card platforms on wooden stilts that rises vertically as it develops.

Physical model and collage | Industrial city study | PVC board, wooden strips, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 機械時代
zh-Hant.description:
機械圖被拼貼為想像的引擎與工業天際線，再發展為一座以木條支撐卡紙平台的城市，隨著發展而垂直升起。

實體模型與拼貼｜工業城市研究｜PVC板、木條、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final city rising on stilts.
以木樁升起的最終城市。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Factories and industrial areas have gradually disappeared from city centres. The project asked how the memory of the machine age could remain an integral part of urban growth.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 工廠與工業區已逐漸從城市中心消失。這個專題探問，機械時代的記憶如何能繼續成為城市發展中不可分割的一部分。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Machine drawings were cut and recombined into complex imagined engines with an orderly interior. These collages were then joined into a long skyline of an industrial city.
captions: Stills of the moving castle from the animated film that inspired the project.
Five patent drawings studied for their machine parts: an engine, a typewriter, a tricycle, a water heater and gears.
The skyline of an industrial city.
A city map made from machine pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 機械圖被切開並重新組合為擁有井然內部的複雜想像引擎。這些拼貼接著被連成一條長長的工業城市天際線。
captions: 啟發本案的動畫電影中移動城堡的畫面。
研究機械零件的五張專利圖：引擎、打字機、三輪車、熱水器與齒輪。
以機械碎片構成的城市地圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The map was transformed into a three-dimensional plan, with wooden sticks as stilts and thin card as surfaces. Low views show a forest of supports beneath the platforms.
captions: A fine-pen drawing combining the patent-drawing parts into the moving castle.
The first city plan in progress.
An overview of the first plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 地圖被轉化為立體的平面，以木條為樁柱、薄卡紙為表面。低角度的視角呈現平台下方一片支柱之林。
captions: 以針筆將專利圖零件組合成移動城堡的繪圖。
製作中的第一版城市平面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Realising that cities grow taller and more complex, the model was taken apart and rebuilt vertically in black and white. The final city stacks platforms on stilts like a shadow of the past.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 意識到城市會變得更高、更複雜之後，模型被拆解並以黑白重新垂直建造。最終的城市把平台疊在樁柱上，宛如過去的影子。
captions: 從上方看拆解後的模型。

sections.heading: Industrial Memory - A City Raised on Stilts
sections.body: As factories leave the centres of cities, the era they represent can easily vanish from collective memory. This project asked how that legacy might remain embedded in urban growth rather than being erased. It began by cutting apart detailed machine drawings and recombining them into imagined engines, intricate yet orderly, whose combination of retro beauty and futuristic complexity suggested a world of its own. These collages were extended into a long industrial skyline and then into a map, where mechanical fragments became districts, roads and plazas. The map was translated into a three-dimensional plan, with wooden sticks acting as stilts and thin card forming the floating surfaces of the city. Recognising that cities grow ever taller and more complex, the first model was deliberately deconstructed and rebuilt vertically in a monochrome palette, so that platforms stack upon platforms like layered recollections. The guidance encouraged moving fluidly between collage, drawing and model, demonstrating how a historical theme can inform a speculative urban vision.

zh-Hant.heading: 工業的記憶-架在樁柱上的城市
zh-Hant.body: 當工廠離開城市中心，它們所代表的時代很容易從集體記憶中消失。這個專題探問，這份遺產如何能繼續嵌入城市的成長，而不是被抹去。它從把細緻的機械圖切開並重新組合為想像的引擎開始，這些引擎繁複而井然有序，懷舊之美與未來感的複雜結合，暗示出一個自成一格的世界。這些拼貼被延伸為一條長長的工業天際線，再化為一張地圖，機械碎片在其中成為街區、道路與廣場。地圖被轉譯為立體的平面，以木條作為樁柱，薄卡紙形成城市中漂浮的表面。認識到城市會不斷長得更高、更複雜之後，第一個模型被刻意拆解，並以單色調垂直重建，使平台層層相疊，如同堆積的回憶。指導鼓勵在拼貼、繪圖與模型之間靈活往返，展示歷史主題如何能啟發一種推測性的城市願景。

pins.title: Distances Between Five Characters
pins.description:
Gestures of movement are traced into curving lines and clay figures for five kinds of people, then built as five clusters of curved paper walls joined by bridges, stairs and a clear tower.

Physical model and drawing | Relationship and distance study | Wooden strips, steel wire, adhesive tape, parchment paper, PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 五種角色之間的距離
zh-Hant.description:
動作的姿態被描繪為彎曲的線條與代表五種人的黏土形體，再建成五組由彎曲紙牆構成、以橋、階梯與透明塔連接的群落。

實體模型與繪圖｜關係與距離研究｜木條、鋼線、膠帶、羊皮紙、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Five clusters joined by paths and bridges.
以路徑與橋連接的五個群落。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: People are connected to one another through only a few steps of acquaintance, and buildings may relate in the same way. The project asked how physical distance between people could be translated into distance between spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 人與人之間只隔著少數幾層認識便彼此相連，建築也可能以同樣的方式相關。這個專題探問，人與人之間的身體距離如何能被轉譯為空間之間的距離。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Movements and interactions were traced as curling gesture lines, dotted paths and angular nets. From these patterns, curved clay figures in five colours stood for the peacemaker, enthusiast, observer, individualist and giver.
captions: Stills from the music video whose dance started the project.
Three collages cut from photos of the dancers, with line drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 動作與互動被描繪為捲曲的姿態線、點狀路徑與稜角分明的網。從這些圖案中，五種顏色的彎曲黏土形體分別代表調停者、熱衷者、觀察者、個人主義者與給予者。
captions: 啟發本案的音樂錄影帶舞蹈畫面。
以舞者照片剪貼而成的三張拼貼與線稿。
代表五種角色的黏土形體。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Five individual constructions of curved paper walls were made and arranged in many combinations. The heights and gaps were adjusted until the distances and bridges felt right.
captions: Curved walls around a small figure.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以彎曲紙牆製作出五個獨立的構造，並以多種方式組合排列。高度與間距不斷調整，直到距離與橋樑恰如其分。
captions: 以多種組合排列的紙構件。
環繞小人形的彎曲牆面。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model each character has its own architecture, from shared heights to a strange tower and a lookout. Wooden paths, stepping blocks and clear stairs link them across the ground.
captions: The model seen as a whole.
A clear tower beside the walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，每一種角色都擁有自己的建築，從高度一致的群體到一座奇特的塔與一處瞭望點。木質小徑、踏階方塊與透明階梯在地面上把它們連接起來。

sections.heading: Measured Closeness - Architecture for Five Temperaments
sections.body: Every relationship has a distance, sometimes intimate, sometimes guarded, and this project set out to give that invisible measure an architectural form. It began by watching movement closely, tracing the curl of gestures, the routes of bodies through space and the moments when they connect, divide or stand apart. These drawings evolved into curved clay figures in five colours, each representing a temperament, the peacemaker, the enthusiast, the observer, the individualist and the giver. Five separate constructions of curved paper walls were then made and repeatedly rearranged, with heights and gaps adjusted until each pairing felt correctly near or far. In the final model, architectural character replaces colour. One cluster shares a common height, another offers many entrances, a third grows into a strange tower, the observer receives a lookout, and the enthusiast is given varied structures to leap across. The guidance encouraged careful observation of human behaviour, revealing how social relationships can be measured, mapped and built.

zh-Hant.heading: 度量的親近-為五種性情而建的建築
zh-Hant.body: 每一段關係都有它的距離，有時親密，有時保留，這個專題著手為這種看不見的度量賦予建築形式。它從仔細觀察動作開始，描繪姿態的捲曲、身體穿越空間的路線，以及彼此相連、分開或保持距離的時刻。這些繪圖演變為五種顏色的彎曲黏土形體，每一種代表一種性情，調停者、熱衷者、觀察者、個人主義者與給予者。接著以彎曲紙牆製作出五個獨立的構造，並一再重新排列，不斷調整高度與間距，直到每一組配對的遠近都恰到好處。在最終模型中，建築特質取代了顏色。一個群落共享相同的高度，另一個提供許多入口，第三個長成一座奇特的塔，觀察者得到一處瞭望點，熱衷者則擁有可以跳躍穿越的多樣結構。指導鼓勵仔細觀察人的行為，揭示社會關係如何能被度量、描繪與建造。

pins.title: Stationery Deconstruction
pins.description:
Blue stationery is taken apart, sorted on a grid and collaged, then suspended within wooden frames and glue-gun webs that grow into a spiralling final model.

Physical model and collage | Object deconstruction study | Dismantled stationery, wooden strips, glue gun, watercolour, orange paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 拆解文具
zh-Hant.description:
藍色文具被拆開、在格網上分類並拼貼，再懸掛於木條框架與熱熔膠網之中，最終發展為一座螺旋形的模型。

實體模型與拼貼｜物件拆解研究｜拆解的文具、木條、熱熔膠、水彩、橘色紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final spiralling frame holding stationery parts.
承載文具零件的最終螺旋框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Everyday stationery hides an intricate inner structure that is rarely noticed. The project asked how these dismantled parts could become the material of a spatial composition.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 日常文具藏著很少被注意到的精巧內部結構。這個專題探問，這些拆解後的零件如何能成為空間構成的材料。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A collection of blue stationery was taken apart and every piece was laid out on a measuring grid. The parts were then sorted by type and recombined into flat collages.
captions: Watercolour studies of the blue stationery collection, including branded pens and erasers.
Dismantled parts laid on a grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一批藍色文具被拆開，每一個零件都被排列在量度格網上。零件接著按類型分類，再重新組合為平面拼貼。
captions: 藍色文具收藏的水彩習作，包括有品牌的筆與橡皮擦。
排列在格網上的拆解零件。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Two experimental models were built with proportions based on the golden ratio. One tested colour and structure with orange planes, while the other tested the strength and texture of glue-gun webs.
captions: Painting the stick frame by hand during the build.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以黃金比例為依據，建造了兩個實驗模型。一個以橘色面板測試色彩與結構，另一個則測試熱熔膠網的強度與質感。
captions: 製作過程中以手為木條框架上色。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The two experiments were combined into a final model whose frame twists into a spiral. Stationery parts are set along the curve so that light and shadow animate the composition.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 兩項實驗被結合為最終模型，其框架扭轉成螺旋。文具零件沿著曲線安置，讓光影為整個構成注入生氣。

sections.heading: Hidden Anatomy - Spiral of Disassembled Things
sections.body: A long habit of collecting stationery gave this project its quiet starting point, but curiosity soon moved beyond surfaces toward the hidden anatomy of familiar objects. Pens, cutters, correction tapes and cases were opened one by one, and their springs, shells and tiny mechanisms were laid out on a measuring grid like specimens awaiting classification. Sorting these fragments by type and recombining them in flat collages revealed rhythms of colour and form that the intact objects had concealed. The search then turned to space. Two experimental frames proportioned by the golden ratio explored complementary questions, one pairing blue members with planes of orange paper to test colour and structure, the other stretching webs of glue between wooden bars to probe strength, translucency and shadow. The final model unites both lessons in a frame that twists upward into a spiral, with dismantled parts suspended along its curve. Under directed light the composition throws layered shadows, and ordinary tools are transformed into an architecture of memory and precise attention.

zh-Hant.heading: 隱藏的解剖-拆解之物的螺旋
zh-Hant.body: 長久收集文具的習慣為這個專題提供了安靜的起點，但好奇心很快越過表面，轉向熟悉物件的隱藏解剖。筆、美工刀、修正帶與筆盒被一一打開，彈簧、外殼與微小的機件被排列在量度格網上，宛如等待分類的標本。按類型整理這些碎片，並在平面拼貼中重新組合，揭示出完整物件所掩藏的色彩與形體節奏。探索接著轉向空間。兩個以黃金比例定出比例的實驗框架探討互補的問題，一個以藍色桿件搭配橘色紙面測試色彩與結構，另一個在木條之間拉出膠網，探究強度、透明度與陰影。最終模型把兩項發現結合為一個向上扭轉成螺旋的框架，拆解後的零件沿著曲線懸掛。在定向光線下，構成投下層層陰影，平凡的工具轉化為一種記憶與精確專注的建築。

pins.title: Five Staircases
pins.description:
Staircases are drawn into a dense web of crossing flights, then built as white paper stair models that are combined into clusters linking separate routes.

Physical model and drawing | Staircase and perspective study | 300g cardboard, wooden strips | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 五座階梯
zh-Hant.description:
階梯被繪製為一張由交錯梯段構成的密網，再以白色紙模型建造，並組合為連接不同路線的群集。

實體模型與繪圖｜階梯與透視研究｜300克卡紙、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Paper staircases combined into a cluster.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Staircases strongly drive the sense of depth and perspective in a space. The project asked how different routes taken by different characters could be expressed through stairs alone.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 階梯強烈地推動空間中的深度與透視感。這個專題探問，不同角色所走的不同路線，如何能只透過階梯來表達。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Five styles of staircase were studied for their structure and details. A line drawing multiplied and interwove them into a dense field of crossing flights, with coloured paths tracing separate journeys.
captions: Film-strip sequences of stills from the film that inspired the project.
A collage of film screenshots, with staircases traced in pink.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 五種風格的階梯被研究其結構與細部。一幅線描把它們重複並交織成一片交錯梯段的密集場域，以彩色路徑描繪各自的旅程。
captions: 啟發本案的電影劇照膠卷序列。
以電影截圖拼貼而成、並以粉紅線描出樓梯的拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Each type of stair was then made as a paper model to understand its structure. Straight, folding and spiral flights were photographed from above to compare their geometry.
captions: The stair models collaged with cut-out figures from the film.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 接著每一種階梯都被製作成紙模型，以理解其結構。直跑、折返與螺旋的梯段從上方拍攝，以比較它們的幾何。
captions: 樓梯模型與電影人物剪影拼貼。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The individual models were joined into clusters that express the relationships between the routes. Stairs meet, overlap and branch so that each path touches the others.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 個別模型被連接成群集，表達各路線之間的關係。階梯相遇、重疊與分岔，使每一條路徑都與其他路徑相觸。
captions: 連接成單一構成的階梯。

sections.heading: Ascending Routes - Relationships Told in Stairs
sections.body: Few architectural elements carry the eye into depth as forcefully as a staircase, and this project took that quality as its sole instrument of storytelling. Observation began with scenes composed in strict one-point perspective, where stairs seemed to organise both space and narrative. Five distinct staircases were identified as the paths of five protagonists, each with its own style of rise, landing and balustrade. A large line drawing multiplied these flights into a vertiginous field, where coloured threads trace individual journeys through a labyrinth of steps. Paper models then translated each type into three dimensions, allowing the logic of straight, folding and spiral stairs to be understood through making rather than looking. Photographed from above against a dark ground, the models read almost like diagrams of movement. In the final stage the separate stairs were joined into clusters, meeting, overlapping and branching so that every route touches the others. Character and relationship are thus rendered not through figures but through the shared geometry of ascent.

zh-Hant.heading: 上升的路線-以階梯講述的關係
zh-Hant.body: 很少有建築元素能像階梯那樣有力地把目光帶入深處，這個專題便以這種特質作為唯一的敘事工具。觀察從以嚴格一點透視構成的場景開始，階梯在其中似乎同時組織著空間與敘事。五座各具特色的階梯被辨識為五位主角的路徑，每一座都有自己的升起、平台與欄杆形式。一幅大型線描把這些梯段重複成令人暈眩的場域，彩色的線在階梯迷宮中描出各自的旅程。紙模型接著把每一種類型轉譯為立體，讓直跑、折返與螺旋階梯的邏輯透過製作而非觀看來理解。在深色底面上從上方拍攝時，模型讀起來幾乎像是移動的圖解。在最後階段，獨立的階梯被連接成群集，相遇、重疊與分岔，使每一條路線都與其他路線相觸。角色與關係因此不是透過人物來呈現，而是透過上升的共同幾何。

pins.title: The Toilet City
pins.description:
Dozens of toilets are drawn from observation and then multiplied into a dense isometric city where fixtures, pipes and tiny figures form an imagined landscape.

Drawing | Everyday object and imagined city | Pen line drawing, digital colour | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 馬桶之城
zh-Hant.description:
數十個馬桶從觀察中被描繪出來，再增殖為一座密集的等角城市，衛浴器具、管線與微小的人形構成一片想像的景觀。

繪圖｜日常物件與想像城市｜鋼筆線描、數位上色｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 由馬桶構成的等角城市。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The toilet is a private place where everyday defences fall away and only physical need remains. The project asked how this humble fixture could become the building block of an imagined city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 馬桶是一個私密的地方，日常的防備在此卸下，只剩下身體的需要。這個專題探問，這件平凡的器具如何能成為一座想像城市的基本構件。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many different toilets were drawn in line, from wall-hung bowls to tall cisterns. The drawings compare the variety of shapes, seats and tanks hidden within a single type.
captions: A photo of a real toilet, the starting point for the drawings.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 許多不同的馬桶以線條描繪，從壁掛式便器到高水箱款式。這些繪圖比較了單一類型之中隱藏的多樣形狀、座圈與水箱。
captions: 作為繪圖起點的真實馬桶照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The fixtures were repeated, stacked and joined by pipes into blocks and streets. Rows of bowls became terraces while tanks grew into towers.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 器具被重複、堆疊，並以管線連接成街區與街道。成排的便器成為階台，水箱則長成高塔。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final isometric drawing presents a crowded city built entirely from toilets and their parts. Pink lines pick out pipes and small playful figures moving through the scene.
captions: Pipes and towers in the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的等角繪圖呈現一座完全由馬桶及其零件建成的擁擠城市。粉紅色線條勾勒出管線，以及在畫面中穿梭的俏皮小人形。

sections.heading: Private Ground - A Metropolis of Humble Fixtures
sections.body: Some of the most honest moments of daily life unfold in the smallest room, where reading, idle scrolling or staring at floor tiles coincide with the quiet surrender of every social defence. This project treated that intimacy with humour and seriousness at once, choosing the toilet as the unlikely protagonist of an urban fantasy. It began with patient observation, drawing dozens of fixtures in clean line, from low wall-hung bowls to tall cisterns with exposed flush valves, so that a single familiar type revealed an unexpected range of silhouettes. These studies became a vocabulary for building. Bowls were lined up into terraces, tanks were stacked into towers, and pipes stretched across the page as bridges, conduits and streets. The resulting isometric drawing presents a crowded metropolis in which every element is a fixture or a fragment of one. Touches of pink highlight plumbing and tiny playful figures wandering through the scene, transforming a private necessity into a shared and lively civic landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 私密之地-平凡器具的大都會
zh-Hant.body: 日常生活中最坦誠的一些時刻，發生在最小的房間裡，閱讀、隨意滑手機或凝視地磚，同時伴隨著所有社交防備的安靜卸下。這個專題以幽默與認真並存的態度對待這份私密，選擇馬桶作為一場城市幻想中意想不到的主角。它從耐心的觀察開始，以俐落的線條描繪數十件器具，從低矮的壁掛便器到露出沖水閥的高水箱，使單一熟悉的類型展現出意外豐富的輪廓。這些研究成為建造的語彙。便器排列成階台，水箱堆疊成高塔，管線在紙面上延伸為橋樑、管道與街道。完成的等角繪圖呈現一座擁擠的大都會，其中每一個元素都是一件器具或其碎片。點點粉紅勾勒出管線，以及在畫面中漫遊的俏皮小人形，把一項私人的必需轉化為一片共享而生動的城市景觀。

pins.title: Triangular Composition
pins.description:
A photograph is reduced to a net of triangles, printed and folded into paper fragments, then gathered inside a wooden frame that casts a jagged shadow.

Physical model and drawing | 2D to 3D transformation study | 250g paper, printed triangulation, wooden battens | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 三角構成
zh-Hant.description:
一張照片被簡化為三角形的網，印出後摺成紙片，再聚集於一個木條框架之中，投下參差的陰影。

實體模型與繪圖｜二維到三維轉化研究｜250克紙、印刷三角網、木條｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final frame and its shadow.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Abstract structures can be found hidden within ordinary photographs. The project asked how such a structure could be extracted and changed from a flat image into a three-dimensional form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 抽象的結構可以隱藏在普通的照片之中。這個專題探問，如何能提取這樣的結構，並把它從平面影像轉變為立體形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A photograph was traced into an irregular net of triangles. The net was restructured digitally and printed onto paper ready to be cut and folded.
captions: The source photo whose abstract structure was traced into triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張照片被描繪為不規則的三角網。這張網以數位方式重新組構，並印在紙上，準備切割與摺疊。
captions: 被描繪成三角形抽象結構的原始照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The printed sheets were folded into small faceted fragments with sharp peaks. These pieces were then joined into a larger cluster on the work table.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 印好的紙張被摺成帶有尖峰的小型多面碎片。這些碎片接著在工作桌上被組合為更大的群集。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The fragments were gathered inside a frame of wooden battens with a folded canopy above. Under a single light the frame projects a jagged shadow onto the wall.
captions: The frame seen from the front.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 碎片被聚集在一個木條框架之中，上方覆以摺疊的頂篷。在單一光源下，框架在牆上投下參差的陰影。

sections.heading: Folded Facets - From Image to Faceted Space
sections.body: Every photograph contains a latent geometry, and this project set out to uncover it by reading an image not for what it shows but for the structure beneath its tones. Points of contrast were connected into an irregular net of triangles, a drawing that keeps the rhythm of the original while discarding its subject. Restructured digitally and printed onto heavy paper, the net became a set of instructions for folding. Each sheet was scored and bent into small faceted fragments with sharp peaks and hollow valleys, an initial exploration of how a two-dimensional pattern can stand up and occupy space. Gathered on the work table, the fragments began to cluster like crystals, their planes catching light at varying angles. The final model houses this cluster inside a simple frame of wooden battens, crowned by a folded canopy that echoes the triangulated net. Lit by a single lamp, the frame casts a jagged shadow across the wall, returning the form to a flat image and closing a quiet cycle between surface and depth.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺疊的刻面-從影像到多面空間
zh-Hant.body: 每一張照片都蘊含著潛在的幾何，這個專題著手揭示它，閱讀一幅影像時，關注的不是它所呈現的內容，而是色調之下的結構。對比的點被連接成不規則的三角網，這幅繪圖保留了原作的節奏，同時捨棄了它的主題。經過數位重組並印在厚紙上之後，這張網成為一套摺疊的指引。每一張紙都被壓線並彎折成帶有尖峰與凹谷的小型多面碎片，這是對二維圖案如何站立並佔據空間的初步探索。在工作桌上聚集時，碎片開始像晶體般成群，各個面以不同角度捕捉光線。最終模型把這個群集安置在簡單的木條框架中，頂部覆以呼應三角網的摺疊頂篷。在一盞燈的照射下，框架在牆上投下參差的陰影，讓形體回到平面影像，完成表面與深度之間一個安靜的循環。

pins.title: Triangle Structure
pins.description:
The layered petals of an orchid are abstracted into a net of triangles, then built as a tangled frame of wooden strips holding white card planes hung on elastic cords.

Physical model and drawing | Natural form and structure study | Wooden strips, elastic cords, white cardboard, translucent PVC | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 三角結構
zh-Hant.description:
蘭花層層的花瓣被抽象為三角形的網，再以木條建成糾結的框架，其中以彈性繩懸掛白色卡紙面板。

實體模型與繪圖｜自然形態與結構研究｜木條、彈性繩、白卡紙、半透明PVC｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished frame of wooden strips.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A flower holds many petals within a strong and orderly structure. The project asked how the growth of petals from a dense core could be expressed as an architectural frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一朵花在堅固而有序的結構中容納了許多花瓣。這個專題探問，花瓣從密集核心生長出來的過程，如何能被表達為一個建築框架。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The outlines of the petals were traced and simplified into an irregular net of angular cells. This drawing turned soft curves into a structure of straight lines and triangles.
captions: Phalaenopsis orchid photos, with the flower core traced into triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 花瓣的輪廓被描繪並簡化為不規則的稜角網格。這幅繪圖把柔和的曲線轉化為由直線與三角形構成的結構。
captions: 蝴蝶蘭照片，並將花心描繪成三角形。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden strips were cut to many lengths and joined into triangles that grow from a dense base. The hardest step was threading card planes into the jammed frame and hanging them on elastic cords.
captions: Assembling the wooden-strip frame by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木條被切成多種長度，接合成從密集基部生長出來的三角形。最困難的一步，是把卡紙面板穿入擁擠的框架，並以彈性繩懸掛起來。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final frame is dense at the bottom and gradually sparser towards the top, like a flower opening. Card planes face different directions to show petals growing outward.
captions: The frame seen from the front.
A low view into the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的框架底部密集，向上逐漸稀疏，宛如一朵正在綻放的花。卡紙面板朝向不同方向，呈現花瓣向外生長。
captions: 朝向多個方向的卡紙面板。

sections.heading: Opening Petals - A Frame That Grows Toward Light
sections.body: A flower can be read as a lesson in structure, its many petals held in an order that is both delicate and remarkably strong. This project began by studying the layered form of an orchid, tracing the outline of each petal and simplifying the result into a restless net of angular cells. Through this act of drawing, soft curves were translated into straight lines and triangles, a vocabulary suited to building. Wooden strips were then cut to many lengths and joined into triangular units, beginning with a dense cluster that recalls the core of the bloom. As the frame rose, the joints were spaced further apart, so that the structure loosens and opens like petals unfolding over time. The most demanding task was threading white card planes into the crowded lattice and suspending them on elastic cords, each turned toward a different direction. Seen under a single lamp, the frame casts a vast and intricate shadow, and the slow logic of natural growth becomes a spatial experience of density and release.

zh-Hant.heading: 綻放的花瓣-向光生長的框架
zh-Hant.body: 一朵花可以被讀作一堂結構課，它的眾多花瓣以一種既細膩又出奇堅固的秩序被維繫著。這個專題從研究蘭花的層疊形態開始，描繪每一片花瓣的輪廓，再把結果簡化為一張躁動的稜角網格。透過這樣的描繪，柔和的曲線被轉譯為直線與三角形，成為適合建造的語彙。接著木條被切成多種長度，接合成三角形單元，從一個令人聯想到花心的密集群聚開始。隨著框架升高，接點之間的距離逐漸拉開，使結構像隨時間展開的花瓣般鬆散而開放。最艱難的工作，是把白色卡紙面板穿入擁擠的格架，並以彈性繩懸掛，每一片都轉向不同的方向。在單一燈光下觀看時，框架投下巨大而繁複的陰影，自然生長的緩慢邏輯化為一種關於密集與舒展的空間經驗。

pins.title: Two Rooms in Borrowed Colours
pins.description:
Colour palettes drawn from cinematic scenes are translated into a two-storey house model, with a pink living room below and a floral bedroom above.

Interior model | Colour and atmosphere study | Museum board, acrylic paint, clay, fabric | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 借來色彩的兩個房間
zh-Hant.description:
從電影場景中提取的色彩被轉譯為一座兩層住宅模型，下層是粉紅色的客廳，上層是碎花的臥室。

室內模型｜色彩與氛圍研究｜博物館紙板、壓克力顏料、黏土、布料｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Scenes in films often rely on strong, carefully matched colours to create a mood. The project asked how such palettes could be extracted and turned into real interior spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 電影中的場景常常依靠強烈而精心搭配的色彩來營造氛圍。這個專題探問，如何能提取這樣的色彩組合，並把它轉化為真實的室內空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Three scenes were studied for their dominant colours, furnishings and textures. Their palettes were listed as materials such as patterned tiles, carpets, sofas and chandeliers.
captions: Posters of the two films whose colours inspired the rooms.
Three film scenes with the colour palettes extracted from them.
Reference interior moodboards for the two rooms.
The house seen from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 三個場景被研究其主要色彩、陳設與質感。它們的色彩組合被列為各種材料，例如花紋地磚、地毯、沙發與吊燈。
captions: 啟發兩個房間配色的兩部電影海報。
三個電影場景及從中萃取的色票。
兩個房間的室內參考情境板。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Furniture was made by hand from board, clay and fabric and tested inside each room. A pink minimalist room and a cream pastoral room were developed side by side.
captions: Making the miniature furniture by hand.
Furniture tested in the pink room.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 家具以紙板、黏土與布料手工製作，並在每個房間中測試。粉紅色的極簡房間與米白色的田園房間並行發展。
captions: 在粉紅房間中測試的家具。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The pink room combines patterned floor tiles, grey curtains and a glass-ball chandelier. The bedroom turns red plaid into small floral fabric with plants and off-white walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 粉紅房間結合花紋地磚、灰色窗簾與玻璃球吊燈。臥室把紅色格紋轉化為小碎花布料，搭配植物與米白牆面。

sections.heading: Colour as Atmosphere - Interiors Drawn From the Screen
sections.body: Colour on screen rarely appears by chance, and this project set out to learn from scenes whose palettes are as deliberate as their framing. Three interiors were studied closely, one dominated by pink, another by earthy yellow and a third by red plaid fabrics, and each was translated into a list of material decisions, patterned tiles, woven carpets, metal or wooden tables, glass or bamboo chandeliers. These lists became the brief for a compact two-storey house built in museum board. Below, a minimalist living room adopts the strong pink, balancing it with grey curtains, a pale table and a cluster of glass globes so the space never becomes monotonous. Above, a pastoral bedroom converts the bold plaid into a softer floral print, softened further by plants and off-white walls that brighten the room. Furniture was crafted by hand from board, clay and fabric and repeatedly adjusted inside each space. The resulting model demonstrates how atmosphere can be designed through colour, texture and the careful staging of everyday objects.

zh-Hant.heading: 色彩即氛圍-取自銀幕的室內
zh-Hant.body: 銀幕上的色彩很少是偶然出現的，這個專題著手向那些色彩組合與構圖同樣經過深思的場景學習。三個室內被仔細研究，一個以粉紅為主調，另一個以土黃為主，第三個則以紅色格紋布料為特色，每一個都被轉譯為一份材料決策清單，花紋地磚、編織地毯、金屬或木桌、玻璃或竹製吊燈。這些清單成為一座以博物館紙板建造的小巧兩層住宅的設計任務。下層的極簡客廳採用強烈的粉紅，以灰色窗簾、淺色桌子與一串玻璃球燈加以平衡，使空間不致單調。上層的田園臥室把醒目的格紋轉化為較柔和的碎花，再以植物與使房間明亮的米白牆面進一步柔化。家具以紙板、黏土與布料手工製作，並在每個空間中反覆調整。完成的模型展示了氛圍如何能透過色彩、質感與日常物件的細心佈置來設計。

pins.title: Ribbons of Survival
pins.description:
Emotions are assigned colours and tested in resin, bubble glue and clay, then built as a landscape of curved foam-paper ribbons and red wire rising in layers.

Physical model and material testing | Emotion and colour study | Foam paper, wire, resin, bubble glue, plasticine | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 求生的彩帶
zh-Hant.description:
情緒被賦予色彩，並以樹脂、泡泡膠與黏土測試，再建成一片由彎曲泡沫紙彩帶與紅色鐵絲層層升起的地景。

實體模型與材料測試｜情緒與色彩研究｜泡沫紙、鐵絲、樹脂、泡泡膠、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Emotions can be understood as colours, each with its own intensity and temperature. The project asked how a story of hardship and the desire to survive could be expressed through colour and form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 情緒可以被理解為色彩，各有其強度與溫度。這個專題探問，一段關於困境與求生意志的故事，如何能透過色彩與形體來表達。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Colours were assigned meanings such as blue for bravery, orange for warmth and dark red for anger. Resin, bubble glue and plasticine were mixed and dried to observe how the colours changed.
captions: The character study of the film's heroine that the project grew from.
Collages of faces and film stills exploring the character's emotions.
Bubble glue on a curved wire.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 色彩被賦予意義，例如藍色代表勇敢、橘色代表溫暖、深紅代表憤怒。樹脂、泡泡膠與黏土被混合並風乾，以觀察色彩的變化。
captions: 本案起點：電影女主角的角色研究。
以臉孔與電影劇照拼貼探索角色情緒。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Many papers were tried before foam paper proved able to hold smooth curves. Strips of different lengths were cut and bent around one another like rising stairs.
captions: The ribbons seen from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 嘗試了多種紙材之後，泡沫紙被證明能維持流暢的曲線。不同長度的條帶被切割並彼此環繞彎曲，宛如上升的階梯。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model blue and orange ribbons climb over dark mounds, threaded with red wire. The layered levels express the struggle and the will to keep going.
captions: A low view of the layered mounds.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，藍色與橘色彩帶攀越深色的丘體，其間穿插紅色鐵絲。層層的高度表達掙扎與繼續前行的意志。

sections.heading: Coloured Feeling - A Landscape of Struggle and Hope
sections.body: Every emotion seems to carry a hue, and this project treated that intuition as a method for building. Responding to a narrative of hardship, it first assembled a palette of feelings, blue for bravery, orange for warmth, dark red for anger and resentment, black for darkness, gold for vitality. These meanings were tested through material experiments. Pigment was mixed into resin and allowed to set in spherical moulds, coloured bubble glue was beaded along a bent wire, and plasticine was blended until bright tones dissolved into murky combinations, each trial revealing how colour behaves once it becomes matter. Several papers were tried before foam paper proved able to hold long, smooth curves. Strips of varied length were then cut, painted and bent around one another, evoking stairs that must be climbed with effort. Red wire threads through the composition like a persistent tension. The finished landscape rises in layers of blue and orange over dark mounds, giving tangible form to the will to survive and the hope that sustains it.

zh-Hant.heading: 有色的感受-掙扎與希望的地景
zh-Hant.body: 每一種情緒似乎都帶著一種色調，這個專題把這份直覺當作建造的方法。回應一段關於困境的敘事，它首先整理出一組感受的色彩，藍色代表勇敢，橘色代表溫暖，深紅代表憤怒與怨恨，黑色代表黑暗，金色代表活力。這些意義透過材料實驗加以測試。顏料被混入樹脂並在球形模具中凝固，有色的泡泡膠沿著彎曲的鐵絲串成珠狀，黏土則被反覆揉合，直到鮮明的色調溶成混濁的組合，每一次嘗試都揭示色彩成為物質之後的表現。嘗試了數種紙材之後，泡沫紙被證明能維持長而流暢的曲線。接著不同長度的條帶被切割、上色並彼此環繞彎曲，令人聯想到必須費力攀登的階梯。紅色鐵絲貫穿整個構成，宛如持續的張力。完成的地景以藍色與橘色在深色丘體上層層升起，為求生的意志與支撐它的希望賦予可觸的形體。

pins.title: Levitation
pins.description:
The squeeze of a rolling pin into dough suggested a city built on a drifting asteroid, developed through layered PVC terrains into a floating ribbed habitat.

Physical model | Form and landscape study | PVC boards, clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 懸浮
zh-Hant.description:
擀麵棍壓入麵團的形態，令人聯想到一座建在漂浮小行星上的城市，並透過層疊的PVC地形，發展為一座懸浮的肋狀居所。

實體模型｜形態與地景研究｜PVC板、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A rolling pin pressed into soft dough creates a strange fusion of a rigid object and a yielding mass. The project asked how this fusion could become a habitat for a future city drifting in space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 擀麵棍壓入柔軟的麵團，形成堅硬物件與柔順團塊之間奇特的融合。這個專題探問，這樣的融合如何能成為一座漂浮於太空的未來城市的居所。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Two trial models were made from cut PVC sheets. One translated mountain outlines into overlapping geometric shapes, while the other stacked contour layers to imitate rugged terrain.
captions: The inspiration: rolling and kneading dough by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 以切割的PVC片製作了兩個試驗模型。其中一個把山的輪廓轉化為重疊的幾何形狀，另一個則以疊層的等高線模仿崎嶇的地形。
captions: 靈感來源：以手揉捏與桿麵團。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The refined model combined the geometric structure with the natural terrain, drawing each layer with slight changes. Hundreds of PVC slices were cut and stacked into flowing tiers.
captions: Cutting and layering the PVC pieces by hand.
Holding the refined model in hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 深化模型把幾何結構與自然地形結合，每一層都以些微的變化描繪。數百片PVC被切割並疊成流動的層階。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final form spreads like a star of ribbed arms around hollow chambers. Circular voids open inside the layers to connect the spaces where people would gather.
captions: A spherical void within the layers.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的形體像一顆由肋狀臂膀組成的星，環繞著中空的腔室展開。圓形的空洞在層層之間打開，連結人們聚集的空間。

sections.heading: Kneaded Ground - A City Adrift Among the Stars
sections.body: An ordinary kitchen gesture became the seed of an architectural speculation. When a rolling pin sinks into dough, a rigid cylinder and a soft, yielding mass merge into a single form, and this union suggested a city carved into a drifting asteroid, where future inhabitants would draw upon the resources of space. The idea was first modelled in clay and then rebuilt in PVC sheet. Two preliminary studies tested opposite approaches. One traced the outlines of mountains and recomposed them as overlapping arcs and rings, an artificial order laid upon nature, while the other stacked contour layers to imitate a rough and eroded terrain. The refined model merged these logics, setting geometric structures within a landscape of hundreds of slices, each drawn with a slight variation from the last. The resulting body extends outward like a star of ribbed arms, and within its folds circular voids open as luminous chambers. These hollows bind the floating mass together, imagining a habitat in which the shape of the ground itself encourages encounter and connection.

zh-Hant.heading: 揉捏的大地-漂浮星際的城市
zh-Hant.body: 一個平凡的廚房動作，成為一場建築推想的種子。當擀麵棍沉入麵團，堅硬的圓柱與柔軟順從的團塊融合為單一的形體，這樣的結合令人聯想到一座刻入漂浮小行星的城市，未來的居民將在那裡取用太空的資源。這個想法先以黏土塑形，再以PVC片重建。兩個初步研究測試了相反的方法。其一描繪山的輪廓，再重組為相互重疊的弧線與圓環，是一種加諸自然之上的人工秩序；其二則疊起等高線層，模仿粗糙而受侵蝕的地形。深化模型融合了這兩種邏輯，把幾何結構置於由數百片切片構成的地景之中，每一片都與前一片略有不同。最終的形體像一顆由肋狀臂膀組成的星向外延展，在其褶皺之中，圓形空洞化為明亮的腔室。這些中空把漂浮的團塊維繫在一起，想像一種居所，讓大地本身的形狀促成相遇與連結。

pins.title: Reforming
pins.description:
The habit of assembling scale models led to a landscape built part by part, with folded silver paper shards and scattered strips that trace paths of light.

Physical model | Assembly and composition study | Dutch paper, wooden strips, acrylic strips, steel wire, wooden board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重組
zh-Hant.description:
組裝比例模型的習慣，引出一片逐件建造的地景，由摺疊的銀色紙片與散落的條帶構成，描繪光的路徑。

實體模型｜組裝與構成研究｜荷蘭紙、木條、壓克力條、鋼絲、木板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The landscape of shards and strips.
碎片與條帶構成的地景。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Assembling a model means building each component separately before gathering them into a whole. The project asked whether this process could generate a space where scattered parts remain linked.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 組裝模型意味著先分別製作每個部件，再把它們聚合成整體。這個專題探問，這樣的過程能否生成一個讓散落的部件仍彼此相連的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The angular plates of a toy armour were sketched and overlapped to draw a concept profile. Its sharp outline became the prototype for a main body surrounded by smaller fragments.
captions: The assembled robot model whose armour inspired the structure, with sketches traced from it.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 玩具盔甲的稜角板片被描繪並重疊，以繪出概念輪廓。它尖銳的外形成為主體的原型，四周環繞著較小的碎片。
captions: 啟發結構的組裝機器人模型盔甲，以及據此描繪的草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The profile was developed into folded three-dimensional pieces of Dutch paper. The main body and some wooden strips were sprayed silver and fitted with acrylic strips and steel wire.
captions: Cutting and folding the paper pieces by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 輪廓被發展為以荷蘭紙摺成的立體部件。主體與部分木條被噴上銀色，並裝上壓克力條與鋼絲。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: All parts were set on a wooden board to form areas separated by fragments yet joined by lines. The acrylic strips run through the space like the path of light.
captions: A side view of the main body.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 所有部件被放置在木板上，形成由碎片分隔卻由線條連結的區域。壓克力條貫穿空間，宛如光的路徑。

sections.heading: Gathered Fragments - Lines of Light Across a Broken Field
sections.body: Building a scale model is an act of patience, in which each component is shaped alone before taking its place in a larger whole. This project turned that patient method into a spatial idea. The angular plates of a toy armour were sketched, overlapped and traced until a sharp concept profile emerged, and this outline became the prototype for a main body surrounded by smaller fragments, as though pieces had been launched outward like sparks. The profile was then developed in folded Dutch paper, its facets cut and scored into crisp three-dimensional volumes. The main body and a number of wooden strips were sprayed with silver pigment, giving them a cold, glistening surface, and were fitted with acrylic strips and steel wire. Finally, every part was arranged across a wooden board. Areas are separated by leaning shards, yet the long acrylic lines pass between them and stitch the field together. These lines read as paths of light, revealing how a scattered composition can still hold a hidden coherence.

zh-Hant.heading: 聚合的碎片-橫越破碎場域的光線
zh-Hant.body: 建造比例模型是一種耐心的行為，每個部件都先被單獨塑造，然後才在更大的整體中就位。這個專題把這種耐心的方法轉化為一個空間構想。玩具盔甲的稜角板片被描繪、重疊並反覆描摹，直到浮現一個尖銳的概念輪廓，這個外形成為主體的原型，四周環繞著較小的碎片，彷彿部件像火花般向外迸射。輪廓接著以荷蘭紙摺製發展，各個面被切割與壓摺，成為俐落的立體量體。主體與若干木條被噴上銀色顏料，賦予冷冽閃亮的表面，並裝上壓克力條與鋼絲。最後，所有部件被佈置在一塊木板上。各個區域由斜倚的碎片分隔，而長長的壓克力線條在其間穿行，把整個場域縫合起來。這些線條被解讀為光的路徑，揭示一個散落的構成如何仍能保有隱藏的連貫。

pins.title: Fluxion
pins.description:
A static wooden structure that seems to float inspired a flow of bamboo sticks that parts around three wooden poles and rejoins above a reflective acrylic base.

Physical model | Flow and structure study | Bamboo sticks, wooden sticks, wooden poles, acrylic board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 流動
zh-Hant.description:
一座看似漂浮的靜態木構造，啟發了一道竹籤之流，它繞過三根木柱分開，又在反光的壓克力底板上方重新匯合。

實體模型｜流動與結構研究｜竹籤、木棒、木柱、壓克力板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The flow of sticks around three poles.
繞過三根木柱的竹籤之流。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A wooden interior can seem to move while remaining completely still. The project asked how this sense of dynamic stillness could be recreated with bamboo sticks, a material that feels sharper and more restless than wood.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 木構的室內可以在完全靜止之中看似在流動。這個專題探問，如何以竹籤重現這種動態的靜止感，竹籤這種材料比木材感覺更尖銳、更躁動。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Copy paper was laid over the grain of wood to trace its direction and shape. The traced strokes helped reveal the texture of a fluid through another medium.
captions: The floating timber structure of the opera house that inspired the project, with the flow sketch drawn from it.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 描圖紙被覆在木紋上，描繪它的方向與形狀。描出的筆觸幫助透過另一種媒材揭示流體的質地。
captions: 啟發本案的歌劇院木構造，以及據此繪製的流動草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Three wooden poles were set up as both resistance and support, and sticks were glued to the base to build a trend of floating. When the flow met a pole, the sticks were deflected back or turned in a new direction.
captions: Gluing the bamboo sticks around the poles by hand.
The prototype flowing around the three wooden poles.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三根木柱被設置為阻力與支撐，竹籤被黏在底座上，以建立漂浮的走勢。當流動遇到木柱，竹籤便被反彈回去或轉向新的方向。
captions: 以手將竹籤黏在木柱周圍。
環繞三根木柱流動的原型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model the flow splits around the poles and leaves gaps, then meets again through tension. A transparent acrylic base reflects the whole structure sharply.
captions: Two layers of flow in the dark.
A low view of the flow.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，流動繞著木柱分開並留下空隙，然後因張力而再度匯合。透明的壓克力底板清晰地映出整個結構。

sections.heading: Arrested Current - A Stream of Sticks Parting and Rejoining
sections.body: Some structures achieve the paradox of motion held in stillness, their timber members appearing to drift even though nothing moves. This project set out to recreate that quality with bamboo sticks, chosen because they perform a similar role to wood yet carry a sharper and more agitated character. The study began by laying copy paper over wood grain and tracing its direction, a simple exercise that allowed the texture of a fluid to be read through another medium. These strokes then guided the construction. Three wooden poles were planted in the base, serving at once as obstacles and as supports, and thousands of sticks were glued in a common direction to suggest a current. Wherever the flow meets a pole it is deflected, turned back or split, leaving gaps in the middle, yet tension draws the separated strands together again beyond each obstruction. Mounted on a transparent acrylic board, the whole structure is mirrored below, so that the arrested stream seems to hover between its own image and the dark.

zh-Hant.heading: 凝止的水流-分離又匯合的竹籤之流
zh-Hant.body: 有些結構達成了一種悖論，在靜止之中保有運動，它們的木構件看似在漂移，儘管一切都沒有移動。這個專題著手以竹籤重現這樣的特質，選擇竹籤是因為它扮演與木材相似的角色，卻帶有更尖銳、更躁動的性格。研究從把描圖紙覆在木紋上、描繪其方向開始，這個簡單的練習讓流體的質地得以透過另一種媒材被解讀。這些筆觸接著引導了建造。三根木柱被立在底座上，同時作為障礙與支撐，數以千計的竹籤沿著共同的方向黏合，暗示一道水流。每當流動遇上木柱，它便被偏折、折返或分開，在中間留下空隙，然而張力在每個阻礙之後又把分離的流束重新拉攏。安置在透明壓克力板上，整個結構被映照於下方，使這道凝止的水流彷彿懸浮在自身的倒影與黑暗之間。

pins.title: Hands Play
pins.description:
The form and movement of the hand are tested in cardboard, wire, toothpicks and plasticine, then a half-closed fist becomes a sheltering palm pavilion.

Physical models | Body and form study | Cardboard, wire, toothpicks, plasticine | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 手的遊戲
zh-Hant.description:
手的形態與動作以紙板、鐵絲、牙籤與黏土加以測試，接著半握的拳頭成為一座遮蔽的手掌亭。

實體模型｜身體與形態研究｜紙板、鐵絲、牙籤、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A hand is made of an irregular palm and five cylindrical fingers whose joints can open, grip, rotate and shake. The project asked how different materials could express the abstract form of the hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 手由不規則的手掌與五根圓柱狀的手指組成，其關節可以張開、握住、旋轉與擺動。這個專題探問，不同的材料如何能表達手的抽象形態。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many sketches reduced the hand to outlines, joints and grids of segments. These drawings tested how posture and movement could be read as simple geometry.
captions: A notebook page of hand sketches with handwritten notes on form, structure and movement.
Photos observing the different forms, postures and movements of the hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 大量的草圖把手簡化為輪廓、關節與分段的網格。這些繪圖測試姿態與動作如何能被解讀為簡單的幾何。
captions: 手部草圖筆記頁，附有關於形狀、結構與動作的手寫筆記。
觀察手的不同形態、姿勢與動作的照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Four hands were made in cardboard, wire, toothpicks and plasticine, and their strengths were compared. Cardboard was easiest to work and could recover its shape, while plasticine hardened and could no longer bend.
captions: A half-clenched fist, the gesture that became the pavilion.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 以紙板、鐵絲、牙籤與黏土製作了四隻手，並比較它們的優點。紙板最容易加工，也能恢復原本的形狀，而黏土乾燥後變硬，無法再彎曲。
captions: 半握的拳頭，成為亭子的手勢。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A half-closed fist was modelled in clay as a shelter from wind and rain. The idea was then built as a cardboard pavilion where a figure stands within the curve of the palm.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 半握的拳頭以黏土塑造成遮風避雨的庇護所。這個構想接著被建成紙板亭，一個人形站在手掌的弧線之中。

sections.heading: Sheltering Palm - The Hand as a First Architecture
sections.body: The hand may be the most flexible part of the body, and this project treated its gestures as a source of space. It began with observation, describing the palm as an irregular pentagon joined to five cylindrical fingers, its skin traced by veins and textures that change with age. Sketches then reduced these features to outlines, joints and grids of segments, so that each posture could be read as geometry. The idea was tested through four material experiments. Cardboard folded into a fist yet sprang back to its original shape, wire captured posture with delicate lines but needed to be reset by hand, toothpicks echoed the pattern of veins but resisted adjustment once glued, and plasticine offered volume until it dried and stiffened. Comparing these results, cardboard proved the most adaptable. A half-closed fist, first modelled in clay, suggested a space protected from wind and rain. Rebuilt in cardboard as a pavilion, the curved palm gathers a small figure within its embrace, evoking the warmth of being held.

zh-Hant.heading: 庇護的手掌-作為最初建築的手
zh-Hant.body: 手也許是身體最靈活的部位，這個專題把它的姿勢當作空間的來源。研究從觀察開始，把手掌描述為一個不規則的五邊形，連接著五根圓柱狀的手指，皮膚上布滿隨年齡改變的血管與紋理。草圖接著把這些特徵簡化為輪廓、關節與分段的網格，使每一種姿態都能被解讀為幾何。這個構想透過四項材料實驗加以測試。紙板能摺成拳頭，卻會彈回原來的形狀；鐵絲以細緻的線條捕捉姿態，卻需要用手重新調整；牙籤呼應血管的紋路，但黏合後便難以修改；黏土提供了體積，直到乾燥變硬為止。比較這些結果，紙板被證明最具適應性。一個先以黏土塑造的半握拳頭，暗示了一個免受風雨侵襲的空間。以紙板重建為一座亭子之後，彎曲的手掌把一個小小的人形聚攏在懷抱之中，喚起被擁抱時的溫暖。

pins.title: Line, Plane and Block
pins.description:
Three basic exercises turn colour straws into a rising spiral of lines, PVC panels into a zigzag of planes and pink and white foam into a swirling tower of blocks.

Physical models | Basic form study | Colour straws, PVC panels, white and pink foam | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 線、面與塊
zh-Hant.description:
三個基礎練習把彩色吸管化為上升的螺旋線，把PVC板化為鋸齒狀的面，並把粉紅與白色泡棉化為旋轉的塊體之塔。

實體模型｜基礎形態研究｜彩色吸管、PVC板、白色與粉紅色泡棉｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The swirling tower of foam blocks.
泡棉塊體構成的旋轉之塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Line, plane and block are the most basic elements of three-dimensional form. The project asked how each element could create movement when used on its own.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 線、面與塊是立體形態最基本的元素。這個專題探問，每一種元素在單獨使用時如何能創造動勢。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Colour straws were cut to different heights and set upright in a curve. Seen from above, the lines open into a spiral that grows taller toward one end.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 彩色吸管被切成不同的高度，沿著曲線直立排列。從上方看，這些線條展開為一道朝一端逐漸升高的螺旋。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: PVC panels were folded into a zigzag and set on a dark base. From above, the folded planes form a dense network of angled corridors.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: PVC板被摺成鋸齒狀，放置在深色底座上。從上方看，摺疊的面形成一張由斜向廊道構成的密集網絡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Small blocks of pink and white foam were stacked and rotated as they rose. The tower twists upward while its colours shift from pink to white.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 粉紅與白色的小泡棉塊在堆疊上升時逐層旋轉。這座塔向上扭轉，色彩也從粉紅漸變為白色。

sections.heading: Three Elements - Movement From the Simplest Means
sections.body: Every built form can be traced back to three elementary components, the line, the plane and the block, and this set of exercises examined how each could generate movement without the help of the others. In the first study, colour straws were trimmed to graduated heights and planted upright along a curve. Viewed from the side they rise like a wave, and from above they open into a spiral that tightens toward its tallest point, demonstrating how a field of simple lines can describe direction. The second study folded thin PVC panels into a continuous zigzag set upon a dark base, so that the planes enclose a maze of angled corridors where light and shadow alternate across each fold. The final study stacked small cubes of pink and white foam, turning each layer slightly as it climbed. The resulting tower twists upward while its colour gradually lightens from pink to white.
