Together these exercises show that rhythm and motion can emerge from the most modest materials and the clearest rules.

zh-Hant.heading: 三種元素-以最簡單的手段創造動勢
zh-Hant.body: 每一種建造的形態都可以追溯到三種基本的組成，線、面與塊，這組練習探討每一種元素如何能在沒有其他元素協助的情況下產生動勢。在第一個研究中，彩色吸管被修剪成漸變的高度，沿著曲線直立排列。從側面看，它們如波浪般升起；從上方看，它們展開為一道朝最高點收緊的螺旋，展示一片簡單的線條如何能描述方向。第二個研究把薄PVC板摺成連續的鋸齒，放置在深色底座上，使這些面圍合出一座由斜向廊道構成的迷宮，光與影在每一道摺痕間交替。最後一個研究堆疊粉紅與白色的小泡棉方塊，每一層在攀升時都略微轉動。完成的塔向上扭轉，色彩也從粉紅逐漸淡為白色。這些練習共同說明，韻律與動勢可以從最樸素的材料與最清晰的規則中浮現。

pins.title: Learning from Cube
pins.description:
A childhood story about a cube leads to perspective drawings, stacked foam cubes and twenty-one framed cubes of three sizes nested one inside another.

Physical models and drawing | Scale and proportion study | Foam, wooden strips, panels | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 向立方體學習
zh-Hant.description:
一個關於立方體的童年故事，引出透視繪圖、堆疊的泡棉方塊，以及二十一個三種尺寸、彼此嵌套的框架立方體。

實體模型與繪圖｜尺度與比例研究｜泡棉、木條、板材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A bedtime story told of a shy cube who gained confidence by meeting others like itself. The project asked how this simple shape could become a series of studies about space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個睡前故事講述一個害羞的立方體，在遇見與自己相似的同伴後獲得了自信。這個專題探問，這個簡單的形體如何能成為一系列關於空間的研究。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Cubes were drawn in one-point and two-point perspective to understand how they recede in space. Small foam cubes were then combined into different arrangements on a table.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 立方體以一點與兩點透視繪製，以理解它們如何在空間中後退。接著小泡棉方塊在桌上被組合成不同的排列。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: One arrangement was built as a solid foam model and analysed in top, side, front and back views. Axonometric drawings recorded how its stepped volumes fit together.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 其中一種排列被建成實心的泡棉模型，並以頂視、側視、正視與背視加以分析。軸測圖記錄了階梯狀量體如何彼此契合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Twenty-one cubes of three, six and nine centimetres were made with different open and closed faces. Smaller cubes were placed inside larger ones to test how three plus six could make nine.
captions: Nine-centimetre cubes from open to closed.
A frame cube holding a smaller frame.
A cube within a panelled cube.
A cube set on its corner inside another.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 製作了二十一個三公分、六公分與九公分的立方體，各有不同的開放與封閉面。較小的立方體被放入較大的立方體中，測試三加六如何能成為九。
captions: 從開放到封閉的九公分立方體。
包含較小框架的框架立方體。
在板面立方體之中的立方體。
以角落立於另一個立方體內的立方體。

sections.heading: Kindred Volumes - Scale and Confidence in a Simple Form
sections.body: A story heard at bedtime can shape the way space is imagined. Here a tale of a shy cube that finds confidence among companions of its own kind became the starting point for a sequence of studies on the most elementary of volumes. Drawings first explored the cube in one-point and two-point perspective, scattering boxes across the page to observe how edges converge and recede. Small foam cubes were then combined into varied clusters, and one arrangement was developed into a solid stepped model, recorded through top, side, front and back views and through axonometric drawings that clarify how its volumes interlock. The final stage turned to scale and proportion. Twenty-one cubes were built from wooden strips and panels in three sizes, each with a different balance of open frame and closed face. Placing smaller cubes within larger ones tested a playful equation in which three and six combine to make nine. Through these nested frames the project reveals how a simple form gains richness and presence through relationship.

zh-Hant.heading: 相契的量體-簡單形體中的尺度與自信
zh-Hant.body: 一個睡前聽到的故事，可以塑造人們想像空間的方式。在這裡，一個害羞的立方體在同類夥伴之中找到自信的故事，成為一系列以最基本量體為主題的研究起點。繪圖首先以一點與兩點透視探索立方體，把方盒散布在紙面上，觀察邊線如何匯聚與後退。接著小泡棉方塊被組合成多樣的群組，其中一種排列被發展為實心的階梯模型，並透過頂視、側視、正視與背視，以及闡明量體如何相互咬合的軸測圖加以記錄。最後的階段轉向尺度與比例。以木條與板材製作了三種尺寸的二十一個立方體，每一個的開放框架與封閉面都有不同的平衡。把較小的立方體置入較大的立方體之中，測試了一道三與六相加成為九的趣味算式。透過這些嵌套的框架，這個專題揭示一個簡單的形體如何因關係而獲得豐富與存在感。

pins.title: Transforming Composition
pins.description:
Drawings that abstract natural and artificial materials lead to two timber-strip structures, one light and one dense, combined into a frame cube with floating panels.

Physical model and drawing | Composition study | Wooden strips, PVC panels | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 轉化構成
zh-Hant.description:
抽象化自然與人工材料的繪圖，引出兩種木條結構，一輕一密，並組合成一座帶有漂浮板片的框架立方體。

實體模型與繪圖｜構成研究｜木條、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Natural and artificial materials found in daily life each carry their own patterns and proportions. The project asked how a flat composition drawn from them could be transformed into a three-dimensional structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 日常生活中的自然與人工材料各自帶有獨特的紋理與比例。這個專題探問，從中提取的平面構成如何能轉化為立體結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Grass, soil, a metal shelf and an outdoor bin were translated into line drawings. The shelf produced strong grids and chevrons, while the ground became a net of triangles.
captions: Photos of the observed flowers, dirt, shelf and trash can beside their line analyses.
The ground as a net of triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草、泥土、金屬架與戶外垃圾桶被轉譯為線條繪圖。金屬架產生強烈的網格與人字紋，而地面則化為一張三角形的網。
captions: 觀察到的花草、泥土、層架與垃圾桶照片及其線條分析。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The planar composition of the shelf was laid out on a grid and built in wooden strips. Two structures were made, one light and clear and the other dense and complex.
captions: Strips laid out on a grid.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 金屬架的平面構成被佈置在網格上，並以木條建造。製作了兩種結構，一種輕盈清晰，另一種密集繁複。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The light structure was turned upside down and set over the dense base to form a single cube. White PVC panels were inserted to float within the frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 輕盈的結構被倒轉，放置在密集的基座之上，形成單一的立方體。白色PVC板被插入，漂浮在框架之中。

sections.heading: Grid and Ground - Everyday Patterns Rebuilt as Space
sections.body: Ordinary surroundings hold a quiet repertoire of patterns, and this project began by noticing them. Flowers and grass, bare soil, a metal shelf glimpsed in a corner and an outdoor bin were each translated into line drawings that stripped away colour and texture to reveal underlying structure. The natural subjects dissolved into restless curves and irregular triangles, while the artificial objects yielded strict grids, repeated verticals and bold chevrons. Among these studies the composition of the shelf proved the most suggestive. Its planar order was laid out on a gridded board and built with fine wooden strips, producing two contrasting structures, one light and clear, the other dense and intricate. Rather than choosing between them, the final model inverted the lighter frame and set it over the denser base, so that openness and complexity meet within a single cube. White panels were inserted at intervals, appearing to hover between the members. The result shows how patterns drawn from the everyday can be rebuilt as layered space.

zh-Hant.heading: 網格與地面-重建為空間的日常紋理
zh-Hant.body: 平凡的周遭蘊藏著一套安靜的紋理，這個專題從注意它們開始。花與草、裸露的泥土、在角落瞥見的金屬架，以及一個戶外垃圾桶，各自被轉譯為線條繪圖，剝除色彩與質感，揭示其底層的結構。自然的對象溶解為躁動的曲線與不規則的三角形，而人工物件則產生嚴謹的網格、重複的垂直線與醒目的人字紋。在這些研究之中，金屬架的構成最具啟發性。它的平面秩序被佈置在有網格的板上，並以細木條建造，產生兩種對比的結構，一種輕盈清晰，另一種密集繁複。最終的模型沒有在兩者之間取捨，而是把較輕的框架倒轉，置於較密的基座之上，使開放與繁複在單一的立方體中相遇。白色板片間隔地插入，彷彿懸浮在構件之間。成果展示了取自日常的紋理如何能被重建為層疊的空間。

pins.title: Transforming a Multifunctional Building
pins.description:
Elements taken from a transforming toy robot become folding card volumes with wooden fasteners, then a translucent frame of acrylic panels and taut lines.

Physical model and sketches | Transformable structure study | Cardboard, wooden fasteners, acrylic panels, strips, thread | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 變形的多功能建築
zh-Hant.description:
取自可變形玩具機器人的元素，化為帶有木製扣件的摺疊卡紙量體，接著發展為由壓克力板與緊繃線條構成的半透明框架。

實體模型與草圖｜可變形結構研究｜卡紙、木製扣件、壓克力板、條材、線｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The translucent frame of the second model.
第二個模型的半透明框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A transforming toy changes its shape and function through rotating joints and simple geometric parts. The project asked how these principles could shape a building that adapts to different uses and sites.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 可變形的玩具透過旋轉的關節與簡單的幾何部件改變形狀與功能。這個專題探問，這些原理如何能塑造一座適應不同用途與基地的建築。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches broke the toy into sharp triangles and lines and studied its rotating attachments. Added parts were drawn as rails and hinges that let the pieces move.
captions: Photos of the robot model whose transforming parts inspired the building.
Rails and hinges drawn as added parts.
A drawing of the first model.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖把玩具拆解為尖銳的三角形與線條，並研究其旋轉的附件。附加部件被繪製為讓構件得以移動的軌道與鉸鏈。
captions: 啟發這棟建築的可變形機器人模型照片。
繪成附加部件的軌道與鉸鏈。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first model folded card into angular volumes held by wooden fasteners, which were firmer than tape. Their colour contrasted with the card and made the structure more flexible.
captions: Cutting and fastening the parts by hand.
A series of views of the first model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一個模型把卡紙摺成稜角分明的量體，並以比膠帶更牢固的木製扣件固定。扣件的顏色與卡紙形成對比，也使結構更具彈性。
captions: 以手裁切並固定各部件。
第一個模型的一系列視角。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The second model replaced the card with translucent panels and rebuilt the structure as a frame of strips and taut lines. On land it can transform into many shapes, and on water it can spread out and float.
captions: A montage of the building spread out on a river.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第二個模型以半透明板取代卡紙，並把結構重建為由條材與緊繃線條構成的框架。在陸地上它能變換為多種形狀，在水面上則能展開並漂浮。
captions: 建築在河面上展開的合成圖。

sections.heading: Folding Machine - A Building That Changes Its Shape
sections.body: A toy that transforms from one figure into another offers an unusual lesson in architecture, for its parts must rotate, slide and lock while belonging to one body. This project extracted those principles, focusing on rotating attachments and simple geometric components, and reimagined them as a building able to change function. Early sketches dissolved the toy into sharp triangles and radiating lines, while further drawings proposed rails and hinges as added parts that allow movement. The first model translated these ideas into folded card, its angular volumes held together by wooden fasteners chosen because tape proved too weak. The pale wood contrasted with the card and lent the joints a visible role. A second model then replaced the card entirely, reconstructing the structure as a translucent frame of panels braced by strips and taut lines. Imagined at full scale, the building would reshape itself on land to suit each site and, on water, unfold and float.

zh-Hant.heading: 摺疊的機器-改變形狀的建築
zh-Hant.body: 一個能從一種形象變換為另一種形象的玩具，為建築提供了一堂不尋常的課，因為它的部件必須旋轉、滑動與鎖定，卻同屬一體。這個專題提取這些原理，聚焦於旋轉的附件與簡單的幾何部件，並把它們重新想像為一座能夠改變功能的建築。早期的草圖把玩具溶解為尖銳的三角形與放射的線條，進一步的繪圖則提出軌道與鉸鏈作為讓運動成為可能的附加部件。第一個模型把這些構想轉譯為摺疊的卡紙，稜角分明的量體以木製扣件固定，選擇扣件是因為膠帶被證明太過薄弱。淺色的木材與卡紙形成對比，使接點扮演明顯的角色。第二個模型接著完全取代了卡紙，把結構重建為由板片構成、以條材與緊繃線條支撐的半透明框架。若以實際尺度想像，這座建築能在陸地上重塑自身以適應每個基地，並在水面上展開漂浮。

pins.title: Replan and Joint Bridge
pins.description:
Observation of a busy station district leads to a curving bridge that separates cyclists and walkers while offering steps for rest, shade and conversation.

Physical model and sketches | Urban connector design | Cardboard, white board, scale figures | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重新規劃的連接橋
zh-Hant.description:
對一個繁忙車站街區的觀察，引出一座彎曲的橋，它分隔騎車者與步行者，同時提供可以休息、遮陰與交談的階梯。

實體模型與草圖｜城市連接體設計｜卡紙、白色板材、比例人偶｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The bridge model with figures resting on its steps.
人偶在階梯上休息的橋梁模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Near a busy railway station a park was divided into many parts, which kept people apart and made the long wait to cross the road troublesome. The project asked how a bridge could improve transport while also giving people a place to rest and communicate.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在一個繁忙的火車站附近，一座公園被分割為許多部分，使人們彼此疏離，等待過馬路的時間也冗長而麻煩。這個專題探問，一座橋如何能改善交通，同時為人們提供休息與交流的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The movements of residents and travellers were observed, from cycling and walking to resting in the shade. Shortcomings were identified, including cyclists colliding with walkers and the lack of shelter from strong sun.
captions: Photos of the railway station and the desolate park beside it.
Location research of the station area, with maps, flows and street observation photos.
A mood board of lively street scenes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究觀察了居民與旅客的活動，從騎車、步行到在陰涼處休息。研究辨識出種種缺點，包括騎車者與步行者相撞，以及缺乏遮擋強烈陽光的遮蔽。
captions: 火車站與旁邊荒涼公園的照片。
車站周邊的基地研究，含地圖、人流與街頭觀察照片。
騎車者與步行者的路線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stepped platforms were sketched as places to sit and talk, and sloped walls were tested as shade. Separate curving lanes were drawn so that bicycles and people would not cross.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 階梯狀的平台被繪製為可以坐下交談的地方，斜牆則被測試作為遮陰。草圖畫出分開的彎曲通道，使自行車與行人不再交錯。
captions: 作為遮陰而測試的斜牆。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final bridge branches and curves, with rows of steps where figures relax, gather and shelter from the sun. Gentle slopes allow travellers to pull luggage easily while cyclists keep to their own lane.
captions: The model annotated with relaxing, shadowing, cycling and communicating.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終的橋梁分岔而彎曲，一排排階梯讓人偶在其中放鬆、聚集並躲避陽光。和緩的坡道讓旅客能輕鬆拉著行李，騎車者則保持在自己的車道上。
captions: 標註休憩、遮蔭、騎行與交流的模型。

sections.heading: Bridge as Plaza - Movement and Pause Above the Street
sections.body: A bridge is usually measured by how quickly it carries people across, yet this project asked what it might offer to those who linger. Beside a busy railway station, a park had been divided into fragments, keeping neighbours apart and forcing long waits at the crossing, while strong sun left few places to shelter. Careful observation recorded the rhythms of residents and travellers, people cycling, wandering, enjoying the cool shade and hurrying with luggage toward their trains. From these notes a set of strategies emerged, addressing communication, shade, safe separation and convenience. Sketches developed stepped platforms where people could sit and talk, sloped walls that cast shadow, and parallel curving lanes that keep bicycles and pedestrians from colliding. The model draws these ideas into a single branching structure in white board. Rows of steps hold small figures relaxing and gathering, raised edges shelter seats from the sun, and gentle slopes ease the passage of luggage. The bridge becomes an elevated plaza where movement and pause can coexist.

zh-Hant.heading: 作為廣場的橋-街道之上的移動與停留
zh-Hant.body: 一座橋通常以它多快把人送到對岸來衡量，這個專題卻探問它能為那些逗留的人提供什麼。在一個繁忙的火車站旁，一座公園被分割成片段，使鄰里彼此疏離，也迫使人們在路口長時間等待，而強烈的陽光讓可以遮蔽的地方寥寥無幾。細心的觀察記錄了居民與旅客的節奏，有人騎車，有人閒逛，有人享受陰涼，也有人拖著行李趕往火車。從這些紀錄中浮現出一組策略，回應交流、遮陰、安全分隔與便利。草圖發展出可以讓人坐下交談的階梯平台、投下陰影的斜牆，以及讓自行車與行人不再相撞的平行彎曲通道。模型以白色板材把這些構想匯聚為單一的分岔結構。一排排階梯承載著放鬆與聚集的小人偶，升起的邊緣為座位遮擋陽光，和緩的坡道讓行李的通行更輕鬆。這座橋成為一個高架廣場，讓移動與停留得以共存。

pins.title: Tower and Space
pins.description:
Four storeys of a slender tower of grids, cardboard and ropes each tell a separate story, showing difference and harmony across changing scales.

Physical model | Scale and narrative study | Cardboard, wooden strips, PVC boards, linen ropes | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 塔與空間
zh-Hant.description:
一座由網格、紙板與繩索構成的纖細高塔，四個樓層各自講述一個獨立的故事，展現在變化尺度之間的差異與和諧。

實體模型｜尺度與敘事研究｜紙板、木條、PVC板、亞麻繩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The same world looks entirely different when viewed at very different scales. The project asked how a single tower could hold four independent stories while remaining one harmonious whole.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 同一個世界在截然不同的尺度下觀看時，看起來完全不同。這個專題探問，一座塔如何能容納四個獨立的故事，同時仍是一個和諧的整體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A sequence of images zooming from a vast landscape to the texture of skin was studied for its jumps in scale. Four short literary passages were then chosen, each suggesting a different mood for one floor.
captions: The sequence of film stills, from microns to a thousand metres, that inspired the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究分析了一組從遼闊地景一路放大到皮膚紋理的圖像，觀察其中尺度的跳躍。接著選擇了四段簡短的文學片段，各自為一個樓層暗示不同的氛圍。
captions: 啟發這座塔、從微米到千米的電影劇照序列。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first floor became a labyrinth of walls seen through a grid, and the second a cluster of white blocks. The third floor raised stairs and ropes toward a high point, and each level was framed by wooden strips.
captions: The first floor with the passage that inspired it.
The second floor with the passage that inspired it.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一層成為透過網格看見的牆體迷宮，第二層則是一簇白色的塊體。第三層把階梯與繩索升向高處，每一層都以木條框起。
captions: 第一層及啟發它的文字段落。
第二層及啟發它的文字段落。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The fourth floor holds a small solitary chamber within a translucent pyramid. Stacked together, the four floors show difference and harmony across scales.
captions: The third floor with the passage that inspired it.
The fourth floor with the passage that inspired it.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第四層在半透明的角錐中容納一個孤獨的小房間。四個樓層疊合在一起，展現跨越尺度的差異與和諧。
captions: 第三層及啟發它的文字段落。
第四層及啟發它的文字段落。

sections.heading: Stacked Worlds - Four Stories Within One Tower
sections.body: The same world can appear utterly different when observed from far away or from very close, and this project explored how such shifts of scale might be gathered into a single vertical structure. A sequence of images that travels from an expansive landscape down to the fine texture of skin served as the initial reference, revealing how each leap in scale produces a new kind of space. Four brief literary passages were then selected, each evoking a distinct emotional condition, and every floor of the tower was assigned one of them. The lowest level became a labyrinth of walls glimpsed through a dense grid, recalling a journey of sorrow and remembrance. The second gathered white blocks around an empty centre, suggesting time that circles rather than advances. The third lifted stairs and ropes toward a precarious summit, and the highest enclosed a solitary chamber within a translucent pyramid. Framed by slender wooden strips, the four worlds are stacked into one tower, where difference and harmony are held in balance.

zh-Hant.heading: 疊合的世界-一座塔中的四個故事
zh-Hant.body: 同一個世界從遠處或極近處觀看時，可以顯得截然不同，這個專題探索如何把這樣的尺度轉換匯聚為單一的垂直結構。一組從遼闊地景一路深入到皮膚細緻紋理的圖像，作為最初的參考，揭示每一次尺度的跳躍如何產生一種新的空間。接著選擇了四段簡短的文學片段，各自喚起一種獨特的情感狀態，塔的每一層都被賦予其中之一。最低的一層成為透過密集網格瞥見的牆體迷宮，令人想起一段悲傷與追憶的旅程。第二層把白色塊體聚集在空蕩的中心周圍，暗示一種環繞而非前進的時間。第三層把階梯與繩索升向一個危險的頂點，最高的一層則在半透明的角錐中圍合出一個孤獨的房間。在纖細木條的框架中，這四個世界被疊合為一座塔，差異與和諧在其中保持平衡。

pins.title: Space and Structure
pins.description:
Sticks, foam and board are tested as line, block and plane, then linear plans are layered into a card model whose levels are refined and opened to light.

Physical model and drawing | Space and structure study | Card paper, wooden sticks, foam | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 空間與結構
zh-Hant.description:
木棒、泡棉與板材被測試為線、塊與面，接著線性平面被層疊為一座卡紙模型，其樓層經過精簡，並向光線敞開。

實體模型與繪圖｜空間與結構研究｜卡紙、木棒、泡棉｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of linear planes.
線性平面構成的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Line, block and plane can each define space, yet they rarely work alone in a building. The project asked how a limited set of materials could create many different spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 線、塊與面各自都能界定空間，但在建築中它們很少單獨運作。這個專題探問，一組有限的材料如何能創造多種不同的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sticks, blue foam and paper board were first used alone and then combined into basic structures. Linear plans proved an interesting language, as lines crossing vertically or in parallel could create different levels.
captions: A refined model of frames and blocks.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 木棒、藍色泡棉與紙板先被單獨使用，再組合成基本結構。線性平面被證明是一種有趣的語言，因為垂直或平行交錯的線條能創造不同的層次。
captions: 框架與塊體的深化模型。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Preliminary boards tested linear plans with foam blocks, and refined models raised the ground plan to follow upper levels. The many levels proved unnecessary, which led to an improved model.
captions: An interior view of the spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 初步的底板以泡棉塊測試線性平面，深化模型則讓地面平面跟隨上層的結構。過多的樓層被證明並不必要，因而促成了改良的模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model keeps the linear language but reduces the plans to one or two levels. Transparent planes were added so that light passes through and the inner spaces can be seen clearly.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型保留了線性語言，但把平面精簡為一到兩層。加入的透明平面讓光線穿透，也讓內部空間得以清楚看見。

sections.heading: Lines Becoming Rooms - Clarity Through Reduction
sections.body: Architecture may be understood as a meeting of art and science, and this project approached that meeting through the most basic means. Sticks, blue foam and paper board were first explored as line, block and plane, each used alone before being combined into small structures. From these experiments a single idea emerged with unusual force, that linear plans, lines drawn on the ground and raised into thin walls, could generate surprisingly rich space when they cross vertically or run in parallel. Preliminary boards tested such plans together with foam blocks, and refined models raised the ground plan so that it followed the structure of levels above. Yet the abundance of levels began to confuse rather than enrich, and this recognition guided the final model. Here the linear language is retained but restrained to one or two levels, while transparent planes are inserted among the walls. Light now passes into the interior and its spaces can be read with clarity, demonstrating how reduction can sharpen a design.

zh-Hant.heading: 化為房間的線-透過精簡獲得清晰
zh-Hant.body: 建築可以被理解為藝術與科學的交會，這個專題透過最基本的手段接近這樣的交會。木棒、藍色泡棉與紙板首先被探索為線、塊與面，各自單獨使用，然後再組合成小型結構。從這些實驗中浮現出一個格外有力的想法，線性平面，也就是畫在地面上、再升起為薄牆的線條，在垂直交錯或平行延伸時，能產生出人意料的豐富空間。初步的底板把這樣的平面與泡棉塊一起測試，深化模型則讓地面平面跟隨上方樓層的結構。然而樓層的繁多開始造成混亂而非豐富，這樣的體認引導了最終的模型。在這裡，線性語言被保留，卻收斂為一到兩層，透明的平面則被插入牆體之間。光線如今進入內部，空間得以被清晰地閱讀，展示了精簡如何能使設計更加銳利。

pins.title: Linear Structure
pins.description:
Hundreds of parallel lines drawn on transparent paper are raised as card walls of varying height, so a light board beneath glows through them in different strengths.

Physical model and drawing | Linear structure study | Card paper, transparent paper, model trees, light board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 線性結構
zh-Hant.description:
畫在透明紙上的數百條平行線被升起為高度不一的卡紙牆，讓下方的發光板以不同的強度透過它們發光。

實體模型與繪圖｜線性結構研究｜卡紙、透明紙、模型樹、發光板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The field of card walls lit from below.
由下方照亮的卡紙牆場域。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A single structure or pattern, used on its own, can still produce many interesting spaces. The project asked whether a model built only from lines and planes could create a rich landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 單一的結構或圖樣即使單獨使用，仍能產生許多有趣的空間。這個專題探問，一個只由線與面構成的模型能否創造豐富的地景。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Inspired by a linear elevated park, many lines of different lengths were drawn in parallel on transparent paper. The concept drawing became a dense field of strokes.
captions: A photo of New York's High Line Park, the inspiration for the lines.
A concept drawing of parallel lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 受一座線性高架公園啟發，許多長度不一的線條被平行地畫在透明紙上。這張概念圖成為一片密集的筆觸場域。
captions: 啟發這些線條的紐約高線公園照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Following the length of each line, card was cut to different heights and set on the paper. Model trees were placed among the walls to give a sense of scale.
captions: The field of walls and trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 依循每條線的長度，卡紙被切成不同的高度並立在紙上。模型樹被放置在牆體之間，以提供尺度感。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A light board placed beneath the transparent paper makes the model glow. The light passes through with different strengths because of the different heights of the planes.
captions: The skyline of walls and trees.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 放在透明紙下方的發光板使模型發光。由於面的高度各異，光線以不同的強度穿透。

sections.heading: Glowing Lines - A Landscape Drawn in Light
sections.body: A single structural idea, pursued with discipline, can yield a surprising variety of space, and this project tested that belief using nothing more than lines and planes. Taking cues from a linear elevated park, it began with a concept drawing in which countless lines of differing lengths run parallel across a sheet of transparent paper, their density shifting like grass in wind. Each line was then translated directly into form. Card was cut to a height that followed the length of its line and stood upright on the paper, so that the drawing rose into a field of thin walls, some low enough to step over, others tall enough to enclose a path. Small model trees were placed among them to establish scale and to suggest a park through which visitors might wander. The decisive move was to set a light board beneath the transparent base. Light now rises through the field, filtered more or less strongly by planes of different heights, and the drawing becomes a luminous landscape.

zh-Hant.heading: 發光的線-以光繪出的地景
zh-Hant.body: 一個以紀律追求的單一結構構想，可以產生出人意料的多樣空間，這個專題僅以線與面來檢驗這樣的信念。從一座線性高架公園得到啟發，研究從一張概念圖開始，無數長度不一的線條平行地橫越一張透明紙，其密度如風中的草般變化。每一條線接著被直接轉譯為形體。卡紙被切成與線條長度相應的高度，直立在紙上，使這張圖升起為一片薄牆的場域，有些低得可以跨過，有些則高得足以圍合一條小徑。小型模型樹被放置在其間，以建立尺度，並暗示一座讓訪客可以漫步其中的公園。關鍵的一步是在透明的底面下放置一塊發光板。光線如今穿過整個場域向上升起，被高度各異的面或強或弱地過濾，這張圖便成為一片明亮的地景。

pins.title: Triangles Structure
pins.description:
Random shapes traced from natural textures are reduced to triangles, built as stick pyramids and extended across a ground plan into a towering frame.

Physical model and drawing | Structure study | Museum board, wooden sticks, card paper, model trees | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 三角結構
zh-Hant.description:
從自然紋理描摹的隨機形狀被簡化為三角形，建成木棒角錐，再沿著地面平面延伸為一座高聳的框架。

實體模型與繪圖｜結構研究｜博物館紙板、木棒、卡紙、模型樹｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: 三角形構成的高聳框架。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Linear plans alone could not create enough different spaces. The project asked which other structure could offer a stronger sense of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 單靠線性平面無法創造足夠多樣的空間。這個專題探問，還有哪一種結構能提供更強的空間感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Many random shapes were drawn following the textures in a set of photographs. Among them the triangle proved the most orderly and gave the strongest sense of space.
captions: Photos of branches and a pile of shrimps beside the strokes drawn from them.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 許多隨機形狀依循一組照片中的紋理被描繪出來。其中三角形被證明最有秩序，也帶來最強的空間感。
captions: 樹枝與一堆蝦子的照片及從中描繪的筆觸。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Triangles were cut out and wooden sticks of different lengths were glued to their edges to form pyramids. These basic units could clearly extend in any direction.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 三角形被切下，不同長度的木棒被黏在它們的邊緣，形成角錐。這些基本單元顯然能向任何方向延伸。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The units were placed on a ground plan and extended with more sticks into a large frame. With only triangles, a great variety of spaces formed above trees and paths.
captions: A low view under the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些單元被放置在地面平面上，並以更多木棒延伸為一座大型框架。僅僅透過三角形，在樹木與小徑之上便形成了豐富多樣的空間。
captions: 框架下方的低角度視角。

sections.heading: Order From Chance - Triangles That Learn to Grow
sections.body: When a sequence of linear plans failed to yield enough variety, this project turned elsewhere for a structural language. It began by drawing random shapes that followed the textures of a set of photographs, letting brushy strokes and scattered marks accumulate across the page. From this apparently chaotic material a single figure stood out. The triangle, the most stable and orderly of shapes, produced the strongest sense of space, and a dense net of triangles was drawn to explore its possibilities. The figures were then cut out and wooden sticks of varying lengths were glued to their edges, lifting each flat triangle into a slender pyramid. Building several of these units revealed a crucial property, that the structure could extend freely in any direction. A ground plan was therefore prepared, the units were set upon it and further sticks were added to link them, until a towering lattice rose above model trees and paths. With a single geometric rule, an astonishing diversity of enclosed and open spaces emerged.

zh-Hant.heading: 偶然中的秩序-學會生長的三角形
zh-Hant.body: 當一系列線性平面無法產生足夠的變化時，這個專題轉向別處尋找結構語言。研究從描繪隨機形狀開始，這些形狀依循一組照片的紋理，讓刷痕般的筆觸與散落的記號在紙面上累積。從這些看似混亂的材料中，一個形狀脫穎而出。三角形是最穩定、最有秩序的形狀，它帶來最強的空間感，於是一張密集的三角網被繪製出來，探索它的可能性。這些形狀接著被切下，長度不一的木棒被黏在它們的邊緣，把每一個平面三角形升起為纖細的角錐。製作數個這樣的單元之後，一個關鍵的特性顯現出來，這種結構能夠自由地向任何方向延伸。於是準備了一張地面平面，單元被放置其上，再加入更多木棒把它們連結起來，直到一座高聳的格架在模型樹與小徑之上升起。僅憑一條幾何規則，便浮現出令人驚嘆的多樣圍合與開放空間。

pins.title: Shoes Exploration
pins.description:
Sneakers are sketched and taken apart to find their structures, and the wavy spaces they reveal grow into a park of curved sheets around a spiral tower.

Physical model and sketches | Object deconstruction study | PVC, card paper, iron wire, rope, wooden sticks, museum board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 鞋的探索
zh-Hant.description:
運動鞋被描繪並拆解以尋找其結構，它們所揭示的波浪狀空間，發展為一座環繞螺旋塔、由彎曲薄片構成的公園。

實體模型與草圖｜物件解構研究｜PVC、卡紙、鐵絲、繩子、木棒、博物館紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A sneaker is assembled from many layered parts that wrap the foot in curving forms. The project asked what kinds of space could be discovered by taking such objects apart.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一隻運動鞋由許多層疊的部件組成，以彎曲的形態包覆雙腳。這個專題探問，拆解這樣的物件能發現哪些種類的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Several sneakers were studied and drawn in continuous overlapping lines, and one pair was dismantled to reveal its layers. Shaded sketches then analysed the hollow spaces formed by the curving parts.
captions: Dismantling a pair of sneakers by hand.
Shaded analyses of the hollow spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究分析並以連續交疊的線條描繪了數隻運動鞋，其中一雙被拆解以揭示其層次。帶陰影的草圖接著分析了彎曲部件所形成的中空空間。
captions: 以陰影分析中空的空間。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Process models curled white strips into loops and waves to test these hollow spaces. The spaces formed by wavy elements became the theme of the final model.
captions: The sneaker reconstruction with wire and rope.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 過程模型把白色條帶捲成環圈與波浪，以測試這些中空空間。由波浪狀元素形成的空間成為最終模型的主題。
captions: 以鐵絲與繩子重構的球鞋模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model combines paper, sticks, transparent sheets, strings and wire into a park with a tower. Wavy surfaces connect the tower with the surrounding shelter, and spiral stairs rise beneath wire arches.
captions: The final model with callouts to the sneakers behind each part.
The spiral stair of the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型結合紙張、木棒、透明片、繩子與鐵絲，形成一座帶有塔的公園。波浪狀的表面連結塔與周圍的遮蔽空間，螺旋階梯在鐵絲拱下升起。
captions: 最終模型，並標出各部分所取材的球鞋。

sections.heading: Unlaced Forms - Wavy Spaces Drawn From Footwear
sections.body: An everyday object can conceal a surprising architecture, and this project uncovered one inside the familiar sneaker. Several pairs were studied and drawn in continuous, overlapping lines. One pair was then carefully dismantled, revealing a sequence of layered parts, each curving to wrap and support the foot. Shaded sketches analysed the hollows formed between these parts, recording how wavy surfaces fold to make shelter. Process models translated these findings into curled white strips, looping and overlapping to form pockets of enclosed space. Encouraged by the beauty of these wavy forms, the final model gathered as many materials as possible, combining paper, sticks, transparent sheets, strings and iron wire into a small park with a tower at its heart. Broad curved surfaces sweep outward to link the tower with a surrounding shelter, while timber treads spiral upward beneath delicate arches of wire. The resulting landscape appears almost natural, its fluid order discovered within an ordinary shoe.

zh-Hant.heading: 鬆開的形體-取自鞋履的波浪空間
zh-Hant.body: 一件日常物品可以隱藏著令人驚訝的建築，這個專題在熟悉的運動鞋之中發現了一座。研究分析了數雙鞋，並以連續交疊的線條加以描繪。其中一雙接著被仔細拆解，揭示出一連串層疊的部件，每一件都彎曲著包覆並支撐雙腳。帶陰影的草圖分析了這些部件之間形成的凹處，記錄波浪狀的表面如何摺疊成為遮蔽。過程模型把這些發現轉譯為捲曲的白色條帶，它們迴繞交疊，形成一個個圍合的空間口袋。受到這些波浪形態之美的鼓舞，最終模型集結了盡可能多的材料，結合紙張、木棒、透明片、繩子與鐵絲，形成一座以塔為核心的小公園。寬闊的彎曲表面向外延展，把塔與周圍的遮蔽空間連結起來，木製踏階則在纖細的鐵絲拱下螺旋上升。完成的地景幾乎顯得自然，它流動的秩序是在一隻平凡的鞋中被發現的。

pins.title: Tree Houses
pins.description:
Rather than a single house, stairs and terraces follow the flow of real branches set on a dark base, so that resting places climb through the tree.

Physical model and drawing | Nature and structure study | Rope, wooden sticks, wooden board, branches | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 樹屋
zh-Hant.description:
這個專題並非建造單一的房屋，而是讓階梯與平台沿著立在深色底座上的真實樹枝流動，使休憩的地方穿越樹木向上攀升。

實體模型與繪圖｜自然與結構研究｜繩子、木棒、木板、樹枝｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tree house model of branches and terraces.
樹枝與平台構成的樹屋模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Many tree houses blend with nature because they follow the structure and lines of the trees that hold them. The project asked how a place for rest could be built without cutting or forcing the branches.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 許多樹屋能融入自然，是因為它們依循承托它們的樹木的結構與線條。這個專題探問，如何能在不砍斷也不扭曲樹枝的情況下，建造一個休憩的地方。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Concept drawings placed small platforms, stairs and joints between trunks and branches. Stairs were seen as the best way to show changes of level.
captions: A photo of a tree house that inspired the project.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 概念圖把小型平台、階梯與接點放置在樹幹與枝條之間。階梯被視為表現高度變化的最佳方式。
captions: 樹枝與平台之間的接點。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: An elevation drawing layered stairs, rooms and terraces along the flowing lines of the tree. Real branches were then bound together as the main frame instead of many supporting sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一張立面圖沿著樹木流動的線條層疊了階梯、房間與平台。接著真實的樹枝被綁紮在一起作為主要框架，取代大量的支撐木棒。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: In the final model the branches carry all the stairs and terraces, and figures rest at every level. Set on a dark rocky base, the structure looks like part of nature.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在最終模型中，樹枝承載著所有的階梯與平台，人偶在每一層休息。立在深色的岩石狀底座上，這個結構看起來宛如自然的一部分。

sections.heading: Following the Branch - Stairs That Grow Through a Tree
sections.body: The most convincing tree houses seem to grow from their hosts, following the structure and lines of the trees that carry them rather than imposing a separate order. This project took that observation as its guiding principle and set aside the idea of a single enclosed house. Instead it proposed a vertical sequence of places for rest, linked by stairs, because stairs most clearly express a change of level. Concept drawings scattered small platforms between trunks, traced flights of steps along rising branches and studied the joints where timber meets bark. An elevation drawing then layered rooms, terraces and stairs into a dense composition that follows the flowing lines of the tree without cutting any limb. In the model, real branches were bound together with rope to form the primary frame, replacing the many supporting sticks a conventional structure would require. Stairs and terraces climb along these branches above a dark rocky base, and small figures pause at every level, making a dwelling that feels like a natural extension of the tree.

zh-Hant.heading: 依循枝條-穿越樹木生長的階梯
zh-Hant.body: 最令人信服的樹屋似乎是從它們的宿主長出來的，它們依循承載它們的樹木的結構與線條，而不是強加一種獨立的秩序。這個專題把這樣的觀察作為指導原則，並擱置了單一封閉房屋的構想。取而代之的是一組垂直排列的休憩地點，以階梯相連，因為階梯最能清楚地表達高度的變化。概念圖把小型平台散布在樹幹之間，沿著上升的枝條描繪一段段階梯，並研究木材與樹皮相接的接點。一張立面圖接著把房間、平台與階梯層疊為一個密集的構成，它依循樹木流動的線條，而不砍斷任何枝幹。在模型中，真實的樹枝以繩子綁紮在一起，形成主要框架，取代傳統結構所需要的大量支撐木棒。階梯與平台在深色的岩石狀底座之上沿著這些枝條攀升，小人偶在每一層駐足，構成一處宛如樹木自然延伸的居所。

pins.title: Lifted Triangles
pins.description:
A photograph is traced into a mesh of triangles, built in wooden sticks on a printed board, then released and lifted into a towering cage of sticks and paper planes.

Physical model and drawing | 2D to 3D transformation study | Wooden sticks, paper | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 升起的三角形
zh-Hant.description:
一張照片被描繪成三角形網格，以木棒在印好的紙板上建構，再被釋放並抬升為一座由木棒與紙片構成的高聳籠狀構造。

實體模型與繪圖｜平面到立體的轉化研究｜木棒、紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final tower of sticks and paper planes.
木棒與紙片構成的最終塔體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A flat image has no thickness, yet it can hold a pattern that suggests structure. The project asked how a drawing on paper could be built up into a form that can be touched and explored.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 平面圖像沒有厚度，卻能承載暗示結構的圖案。這個專題探問，一張紙上的圖如何能被建構成一個可以觸摸與探索的形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A photograph taken by the student was traced into a mesh of irregular triangles, chosen because the triangle is the most stable structural figure. The line drawing was printed onto paperboard so that every line could guide the placement of a stick.
captions: The sky photo and the triangulated line drawing traced from it.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 學生自己拍攝的一張照片被描繪成不規則的三角形網格，選擇三角形是因為它是最穩定的結構圖形。這張線條圖被印在紙板上，讓每一條線都能引導一根木棒的位置。
captions: 天空照片及從中描繪的三角化線稿。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Wooden sticks were glued along the printed lines and the blank areas between them were cut away. The released mesh became a flexible platform that could be bent, folded and lifted into three dimensions.
captions: Building the stick mesh by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 木棒沿著印出的線條黏合，線條之間的空白區域則被切除。被釋放的網格成為一個柔韌的平台，可以彎曲、摺疊並抬升為立體。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model rises as a dense cage of triangles, with paper planes inserted at varying angles and small figures placed among them. Under directed light the lines cast intricate shadows, while the layered waves suggest different stories and the complexity of society.
captions: A low view of the model.
A close view of the triangles.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型升起為一座密集的三角形籠狀構造，紙片以不同角度插入，小人偶散布其間。在定向光線下，線條投下繁複的影子，層疊的波浪則暗示不同的故事與社會的複雜。

sections.heading: Paper Mesh Rising - Shadows of Stable Lines
sections.body: Every built form begins, in some sense, as a flat image, and this project made that passage its explicit subject. A photograph was traced into an irregular net of triangles, the most stable figure available to a builder, so that the resulting drawing already carried a latent structure within its lines. Printed onto paperboard, the drawing became a template: wooden sticks were glued along each line and the empty fields between them were cut away, releasing a mesh that could bend and fold without losing coherence. What had been a picture now behaved like a material. Lifted and gathered, the mesh grew into a towering cage in which paper planes were inserted at shifting angles, catching light and closing certain cells while leaving others open. Small figures inhabit the interior, giving scale to a landscape of ridges and hollows. Under directed light the sticks throw dense shadows across the ground, a second drawing produced by the first. The model thus reads as a meditation on thickness, showing how a line, once given depth, begins to shelter, divide and narrate.

zh-Hant.heading: 紙網升起-穩定線條的影子
zh-Hant.body: 每一個被建造的形體，在某種意義上都始於一幅平面的圖像，這個專題正以這段轉化為主題。一張照片被描繪成一張不規則的三角形網格，三角形最為穩定，因此線條中早已隱含結構。圖面被印在紙板上，成為一個模板，木棒沿著每一條線黏合，線條之間的空白則被切除，釋放出一張能彎曲、能摺疊卻不失整體性的網。原本的圖像於是開始像一種材料般運作。網格被抬升、收攏，長成一座高聳的籠狀構造，紙片以不斷變化的角度插入其中，捕捉光線，封閉某些格子，同時讓其他格子保持敞開。小人偶棲居於內部。在定向光線下，木棒在地面投下濃密的影子，那是由第一張圖所生成的第二張圖。這座模型因此可以被讀作一段關於厚度的沉思，揭示一條線一旦獲得深度，便開始遮蔽、分隔與敘事。

pins.title: Music Wave
pins.description:
Recorded sound waves and light traces are translated into fanned sticks and curled paper, then combined into a refined model of ribbons looping through clusters of sticks.

Physical model and drawing | Sound and form study | Wooden sticks, paper, wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 音樂波浪
zh-Hant.description:
錄下的聲波與光軌被轉譯為扇形木棒與捲曲紙片，再結合為一座紙帶在木棒束之間迴旋的深化模型。

實體模型與繪圖｜聲音與形式研究｜木棒、紙、鐵絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The refined model of sticks and paper ribbons.
木棒與紙帶構成的深化模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Sound is invisible, yet a recording reveals waves with rhythm, density and shape. The project asked whether these waves could be translated into a physical structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 聲音是看不見的，但一段錄音能揭示具有節奏、密度與形狀的波動。這個專題探問，這些波動能否被轉譯為一個實體的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Recorded waveforms were studied alongside sketches and long-exposure light traces that drew the movement of sound in the air. The traces showed loops and twists rather than simple peaks, suggesting forms that coil through space.
captions: The light-trace experiment with an arm and a speaker.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 錄下的波形與草圖，以及描繪聲音在空氣中移動的長時間曝光光軌一同被研究。光軌呈現的是迴圈與扭轉，而非單純的波峰，暗示著在空間中盤繞的形式。
captions: 以手臂與喇叭進行的光軌實驗。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Initial models explored three forms, one fanning wooden sticks into a rolling wave and others curling strips of paper into open shells. Each tested how sticks, card and wire could express the flexibility of a wave.
captions: An initial model of fanned sticks.
An initial model of curled paper.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 初步模型探索了三種形式，其中一個把木棒展開成翻滾的波浪，其他則把紙條捲成敞開的殼體。每一個模型都測試木棒、卡紙與鐵絲如何表達波動的柔韌。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The refined model combined the three initial ideas within a frame large enough to hold it. Paper ribbons loop between clusters of wooden sticks, so that the composition reads as the shape of sound itself.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 深化模型把三個初步構想結合在一個足以容納它的框架之中。紙帶在一束束木棒之間迴旋，使整個構成讀起來就像聲音本身的形狀。

sections.heading: Listening With the Hands - Ribbons of Sound
sections.body: Sound occupies space without ever appearing in it, and this project set out to give that invisible occupant a body. Recorded waveforms supplied a first portrait, dense bands of peaks and troughs, but long-exposure traces of light revealed something less orderly: loops, knots and sweeping curves that suggested a wave moves through the air rather than along a line. Sketches followed these coils, and three initial models tested different translations. In one, wooden sticks fan out in a rolling sequence, their regular spacing echoing the pulse of a beat; in others, strips of paper curl into open shells that hold shadow like a resonant cavity. Each material carried a distinct temperament, sticks articulating rhythm while paper expressed continuity. The refined model gathered these temperaments within a frame large enough to contain them. Ribbons swing between bundles of crossing sticks, so that sharp accents and long sustained tones coexist in one suspended structure. The result is less a representation of a particular piece than an instrument for seeing, where listening becomes a matter of form, interval and light.

zh-Hant.heading: 用手聆聽-聲音的紙帶
zh-Hant.body: 聲音佔據空間，卻從不在其中顯現，這個專題試圖為它賦予身體。錄下的波形提供了第一幅肖像，但長時間曝光的光軌卻揭露出較不規則的面貌，包括迴圈、結點與大幅擺盪的曲線，暗示波動是在空氣中穿行，而非沿著一條線前進。草圖追隨這些盤繞的軌跡，三個初步模型則測試不同的轉譯方式。其中一個以木棒展開成連續翻滾的扇形，規律的間距呼應節拍的脈動；其他模型則把紙條捲成敞開的殼體。每一種材料都帶有獨特的性格，木棒表達節奏，紙片則表達連續。深化模型把這些性格收攏在一個足以容納它們的框架之中。紙帶在交錯的木棒束之間擺盪，使尖銳的重音與綿長的延音共存於同一個懸浮的結構。最終的成果與其說是某首樂曲的再現，不如說是一件用來觀看的樂器，讓聆聽成為形式、間隔與光線的問題。

pins.title: Electronic World
pins.description:
The layout of a circuit board is sketched and read as a city plan, then built in straws, sticks, card, foam and screws as towers gathered around a central core.

Physical model and drawing | Urban analogy study | Straws, wooden sticks, white card, foam, screws | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 電子世界
zh-Hant.description:
一塊電路板的配置被描繪下來並當作城市平面閱讀，再以吸管、木棒、卡紙、泡棉與螺絲建構為圍繞中央核心的塔樓群。

實體模型與繪圖｜城市類比研究｜吸管、木棒、白卡紙、泡棉、螺絲｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The city model with its core towers.
帶有核心塔樓的城市模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A city runs on departments, companies and services, much as a circuit board runs on power, a core, memory and circuits. The project asked whether the logic of a circuit board could organise a city.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一座城市依靠各種部門、公司與服務運作，就像一塊電路板依靠電源、核心、記憶體與線路運作。這個專題探問，電路板的邏輯能否用來組織一座城市。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The layout of a circuit board was sketched, scanned and redrawn as lines and shapes. Each component was read as an urban function, with circuit lines becoming connections between districts.
captions: A graphics card traced into the line sketch.
Inspiration images of circuit boards and a city at night.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一塊電路板的配置被描繪、掃描，並重繪為線條與形狀。每一個元件都被讀作一種城市機能，線路則成為街區之間的連結。
captions: 將一張顯示卡描繪成線稿。
電路板與夜間城市的靈感圖片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The drawn lines were built up with straws, wooden sticks, white card, foam and screws. Different materials identified different functions, while lines tied every department back to the core.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 描繪的線條以吸管、木棒、白色卡紙、泡棉與螺絲建構起來。不同的材料標示不同的機能，線條則把每一個部門繫回核心。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model gathers tall towers around a central core, with low blocks and paths spreading across the board. Small figures move along the connections, showing a city that runs like a circuit.
captions: A side view of the city model.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型把高聳的塔樓聚集在中央核心周圍，低矮的街區與路徑則在底板上蔓延。小人偶沿著連結移動，呈現一座像電路般運作的城市。

sections.heading: Currents Becoming Streets - The City as Circuit
sections.body: Analogies between machines and cities are old, yet this project tested one with unusual literalness. A circuit board was treated as a plan: its core became a civic centre, its memory and power units became districts, and the fine traces linking them became streets and lines of service. The board was sketched by hand, scanned and redrawn, so that the drawing preserved both the precision of the original and the hesitations of a hand learning its pattern. Translation into a model required a vocabulary of materials, and here difference itself carried meaning. Straws, wooden sticks, white card, foam and screws each marked a distinct function, allowing a viewer to read the city as an assembly of systems rather than a uniform mass. Towers of stacked plates and threaded columns rise around the core, low blocks spread outward, and taut lines bind every department back to the centre. Small figures populate the routes between them. The resulting landscape suggests that a city, like a circuit, depends less on any single building than on the continuity of its connections.

zh-Hant.heading: 化為街道的電流-作為電路的城市
zh-Hant.body: 把機器與城市相互類比由來已久，這個專題則直接檢驗了其中一個。一塊電路板被當作一張平面圖來閱讀，它的核心成為市民中心，記憶體與電源單元成為不同的街區，連接它們的細密線路則成為街道與服務的路徑。電路板先以手繪描下，再經掃描與重繪，保留了原物的精確與手的遲疑。轉譯為模型需要一套材料的語彙，而在這裡，差異本身就承載著意義。吸管、木棒、白色卡紙、泡棉與螺絲各自標示一種機能，讓觀者能把城市讀作一組系統的集合，而不是一團均質的量體。由層疊板片與螺紋柱構成的塔樓圍繞核心升起，低矮的街區向外蔓延，繃緊的線條把每一個部門重新繫回中心。小人偶分布在它們之間的路徑上。這片地景暗示，一座城市就像一塊電路板，所依賴的不是任何單一建築，而是連結的連續。

pins.title: Section of the City
pins.description:
An old mixed-use building with overhanging floors is sketched in section, then built in museum board and cut open to show shops, a basement, offices and homes stacked floor by floor.

Physical model and drawing | Building section study | Museum board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 城市的剖面
zh-Hant.description:
一棟帶有懸挑樓層的老舊混合使用建築以剖面描繪，再以博物館紙板建造並剖開，呈現逐層疊放的商店、地下室、辦公室與住家。

實體模型與繪圖｜建築剖面研究｜博物館紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Older city blocks often stack many lives into a single building, from shops and clinics to offices and homes. The project asked how one section could reveal this layered everyday life.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 老城區的街廓常把許多種生活疊放在單一建築之中，從商店、診所到辦公室與住家。這個專題探問，一個剖面如何能揭示這種層疊的日常生活。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A profile of an old building with overhanging upper floors was sketched and studied. Its interior was found to hold a tea shop, a basement, a clinic, offices, neighbourhood units and lofts.
captions: Inspiration images of a dense old town and a cut-away building, with their source link.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一棟上層樓層向外懸挑的老建築被描繪下輪廓並加以研究。它的內部容納了茶飲店、地下室、診所、辦公室、鄰里單元與閣樓。
captions: 密集舊城與建築剖面的靈感圖片及其來源連結。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The sketch was developed into a full section with stairs, floors and furniture in every room. The building was divided into a lower commercial zone of four floors and an upper living zone of three floors.
captions: The model with its overhanging floors.
The upper floors of the model.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 草圖被發展為一張完整的剖面，每個房間都繪有階梯、樓板與家具。建築被劃分為下方四層的商業區與上方三層的居住區。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model, built from museum board, cuts the building open to show every floor at once. Symbolic furniture identifies each room, such as a single shelf for the basement and simple tables for the commercial floors.
captions: A room with a curved stair.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 以博物館紙板製作的最終模型把建築剖開，同時呈現每一個樓層。象徵性的家具標示每個房間，例如以一座貨架代表地下室，以簡單的桌子代表商業樓層。

sections.heading: Floors of Ordinary Life - A Building Cut Open
sections.body: A section is the drawing that architecture uses to confess what a facade conceals, and this project adopted it as both method and subject. The starting point was an old mixed-use building whose upper floors lean outward over the street, a type in which commerce and dwelling have long been stacked without ceremony. A sketched profile recorded its silhouette, and a fuller section then populated each level: a tea shop at street height, a basement for storage, a clinic and offices above, and neighbourhood units and lofts near the roof. The building was divided into two clear parts, four lower floors devoted to economic life and three upper floors devoted to living. Built in white museum board, the model removes the outer wall entirely, so that stairs, slabs and rooms can be read at a single glance. Furniture is reduced to symbols, a single shelf announcing the basement and plain tables standing for the commercial floors. Through this restraint the model becomes a portrait of density, showing how ordinary routines coexist within one vertical neighbourhood.

zh-Hant.heading: 日常生活的樓層-被剖開的建築
zh-Hant.body: 剖面是建築用來坦白立面所隱藏之物的圖，這個專題把它同時當作方法與主題。起點是一棟老舊的混合使用建築，它的上層樓層向街道外傾懸挑。一張剖面草圖記錄下它的輪廓，接著一張更完整的剖面圖為每一層填入內容，包括街面高度的茶飲店、用於儲物的地下室、樓上的診所與辦公室，以及靠近屋頂的鄰里單元與閣樓。建築被劃分為清楚的兩個部分，下方四層屬於經濟生活，上方三層屬於居住。模型以白色博物館紙板製作，完全移除外牆，使階梯、樓板與房間能被一眼讀盡。家具被簡化為符號，一座貨架便宣告地下室的存在，幾張簡單的桌子則代表商業樓層。透過這樣的節制，模型成為一幅關於密度的肖像，揭示日常的作息如何共存於一個垂直的鄰里之中。

pins.title: Twist Tower
pins.description:
Wires strung between two hexagonal plates inside a clear acrylic prism are pulled, spun and twisted until the view through the tower almost closes.

Physical model and drawing | Perception and structure study | Acrylic, museum board, wire | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 扭轉之塔
zh-Hant.description:
在透明壓克力稜柱內，張拉於兩片六角形板之間的線材被拉起、旋轉與扭轉，直到穿過塔身的視線幾乎閉合。

實體模型與繪圖｜知覺與結構研究｜壓克力、博物館紙板、線材｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Most things have two sides, yet people tend to recognise only the side they already know. The project asked how a structure could show that the closer one looks, the less one sees.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 大多數事物都有兩面，但人們往往只辨認自己已經熟悉的那一面。這個專題探問，一個結構如何能顯示看得越近，看見的反而越少。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches studied a hexagonal frame with wires strung between a top and a bottom plate. The wires were arranged in a ring so that turning one plate would change how they cross.
captions: A photo of the twisting landmark tower that inspired the project.
Sketches of the frame and wires.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖研究了一個六角形框架，線材張拉於上下兩片板之間。線材排列成一圈，使轉動其中一片板便會改變它們交錯的方式。
captions: 啟發本案的扭轉地標塔照片。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A transparent acrylic prism about thirty centimetres tall was built, with wires running between its two hexagonal ends. The top was then tested by pulling it up, spinning it and twisting it.
captions: Threading the wires through the prism by hand.
The pull, spin and twist test with the lyric that inspired it.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一座約三十公分高的透明壓克力稜柱被建造出來，線材貫穿於它兩端的六角形之間。接著以拉起、旋轉與扭轉三種方式測試它的頂部。
captions: 拉、轉、扭測試及啟發它的歌詞。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Each extra turn crossed the wires more tightly until the view through the tower almost closed. Looking down the prism, the wires gather into a star that grows denser with every twist.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 每多轉一圈，線材便交錯得更緊，直到穿過塔身的視線幾乎閉合。沿著稜柱往下看，線材聚成一顆星，隨著每一次扭轉變得更加密集。

sections.heading: Seeing Less by Looking Closer - A Prism of Turning Lines
sections.body: Perception tends to settle on the familiar face of things, and this project built an object that resists such settling. Its premise is simple: almost everything has two sides, yet habit allows only one to be recognised. Sketches developed a hexagonal frame in which wires stretch between a top and a bottom plate, arranged in a ring so that any rotation would change their relationship. The built version is a slender acrylic prism, transparent enough to promise full visibility. Tests then applied three gestures to its lid, pulling it upward, spinning it and finally twisting it. With each movement the parallel wires began to lean, cross and gather, and every additional turn drew them tighter. Viewed down the axis of the prism, the lines converge into a radiating star whose centre narrows as the twisting increases, until the opening through which one looks nearly disappears. The tower thus enacts its own argument. Clarity of material does not guarantee clarity of sight, and the harder a single view is pursued, the more completely the other side withdraws.

zh-Hant.heading: 越看越少-轉動線條的稜柱
zh-Hant.body: 知覺往往停留在事物熟悉的那一面，這個專題則建造了一件抗拒這種停留的物件。它的前提很簡單，幾乎每件事物都有兩面，但習慣只讓人辨認其中一面。草圖發展出一個六角形框架，線材在上下兩片板之間拉伸，排列成一圈，使任何旋轉都會改變它們之間的關係。實際建造的版本是一座細長的壓克力稜柱。接著的測試對它的頂蓋施加三種動作，先向上拉起，再旋轉，最後扭轉。每一次動作都讓原本平行的線材開始傾斜、交錯與聚攏，每多轉一圈，它們便被拉得更緊。沿著稜柱的軸線往下看，線條匯聚成一顆放射狀的星，其中心隨著扭轉增加而收窄，直到人們用來觀看的開口幾乎消失。這座塔因而演示了它自身的論證。材料的清晰並不保證視線的清晰，越是執著地追求單一的視角，另一面便退隱得越徹底。

pins.title: Tower of Rings
pins.description:
Circular layers of different heights and thicknesses are sketched, then built as cardboard rings pierced by radial wooden sticks into a tilting, open tower.

Physical model and drawing | Tower form study | Wooden sticks, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 環之塔
zh-Hant.description:
不同高度與厚度的圓形層片先被描繪，再以卡紙圓環與放射狀木棒建構為一座傾斜而敞開的塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜塔體形式研究｜木棒、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower of rings standing on its edge.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A tower is usually read as a solid mass that rises in a single direction. The project asked how a tower could instead be made of open layers that can be seen through and turned.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 塔通常被理解為朝單一方向升起的實心量體。這個專題探問，一座塔能否改由可被看穿、可被轉動的敞開層片構成。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches studied stacked circular layers that change in height and thickness from bottom to top. Radial lines and concentric rings were tested as two systems that could hold these layers together.
captions: A historical engraving of a tower, with its source link.
Sketches of stacked circular layers with handwritten notes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖研究了由下而上改變高度與厚度的層疊圓形層片。放射線與同心圓環被測試為兩套能把這些層片結合在一起的系統。
captions: 一幅塔的歷史版畫及其來源連結。
堆疊圓形層的草圖及手寫筆記。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Cardboard rings of different widths were cut and threaded with wooden sticks running out from the centre. The assembly was checked on a light table so that the overlapping rings and gaps could be read clearly.
captions: The rings on a light table.
Rings and sticks seen from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 不同寬度的卡紙圓環被裁切，並以從中心向外延伸的木棒串接。組合體在燈箱上檢視，使重疊的圓環與縫隙能被清楚判讀。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower stacks open rings around a radial frame, so that light and shadow pass through every level. Tilted on its edge, it reads as both a tower and a turning wheel.
captions: The stacked rings of the tower.
The tower seen from the side.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔把敞開的圓環層疊在放射狀框架周圍，使光與影穿透每一層。當它以邊緣傾斜立起時，既像一座塔，也像一個轉動的輪。

sections.heading: Rings Without a Core - A Tower That Turns
sections.body: Towers have long been imagined as solid accumulations, mass piled upon mass until height itself becomes a statement of power. This project questioned that inheritance by asking what remains of a tower when its body is opened. Sketches began with circular layers stacked like terraces, each varying in height and thickness, and traced how they might grow, contract and spiral as they rise. Two organising systems emerged from these drawings: concentric rings that define each level and radial lines that pin the levels together from the centre outward. In the model, cardboard rings of different widths were cut and threaded with fine wooden sticks, and the assembly was studied on a light table where every overlap and gap became legible. The resulting structure is porous rather than heavy. Light falls through it, shadows fan across the ground, and the eye travels inward without meeting a wall. When the model is tipped onto its edge, the tower becomes a wheel, suggesting that verticality may be a matter of orientation as much as of mass, and that structure can be generous with emptiness.

zh-Hant.heading: 沒有核心的環-會轉動的塔
zh-Hant.body: 塔長久以來被想像為實心的累積，量體一層層堆疊，直到高度本身成為權力的宣示。這個專題質疑這樣的傳統，探問當塔的身體被打開之後還剩下什麼。草圖從如梯田般層疊的圓形層片開始，每一層的高度與厚度各不相同，並描繪它們在上升時如何生長、收縮與盤旋。兩套組織系統從這些圖中浮現，一是界定每一層的同心圓環，二是從中心向外把各層固定在一起的放射線。在模型中，不同寬度的卡紙圓環被裁切，並以細木棒串接，組合體在燈箱上被研究，每一處重疊與縫隙都變得清晰可讀。最終的結構是多孔的，而非沉重的。光線穿透其中，影子在地面展開，視線向內移動而不會遇上一道牆。當模型以邊緣傾倒時，塔便成為一個輪，暗示垂直性既關乎量體，也關乎方向，而結構可以對空無慷慨。

pins.title: Triangle Creatures
pins.description:
A landscape photograph is reduced to a net of triangles, cut out and rebuilt with sticks and card, then flipped and bent into strange creature-like forms.

Physical model and drawing | Triangulation study | Wooden sticks, cardboard | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 三角形生物
zh-Hant.description:
一張風景照片被簡化為三角形網格，裁切後以木棒與卡紙重建，再翻轉、彎折成奇異的生物般形體。

實體模型與繪圖｜三角化研究｜木棒、卡紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Almost everything in a landscape can be redrawn as triangles, some small and delicate and others gigantic. The project asked what new forms could appear when such a pattern is lifted off the page.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 風景中幾乎一切都能被重繪為三角形，有些細小精緻，有些則巨大驚人。這個專題探問，當這樣的圖案被從紙面上抬起時，會出現什麼新的形體。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Photographs of nature were traced by joining their edges and corners until every area became a triangle. The original image was then removed, leaving only a net of triangles in their simplest form.
captions: The landscape photo and the net of triangles traced from it.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 自然的照片被描繪，連接其邊緣與角點，直到每一個區域都成為三角形。原始影像隨後被移除，只留下最簡形式的三角形網格。
captions: 風景照片及從中描繪的三角網。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The net was cut in different ways, sometimes into separate areas and sometimes as one piece without breaking. Thin wooden sticks joined each triangle and were reinforced with strong glue.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 網格以不同方式被切割，有時分成獨立的區塊，有時則整片切下而不斷開。細木棒把每一個三角形接合起來，並以強力膠加固。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Flipped and bent in different directions, the nets became strange shapes made entirely of triangles. Each form casts a sharp shadow and looks like a creature caught in motion.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 在不同方向翻轉與彎折後，網格成為完全由三角形構成的奇異形狀。每一個形體都投下銳利的影子，看來像一隻在運動中被捕捉的生物。

sections.heading: Landscapes Learning to Crawl - The Life of a Net
sections.body: Triangulation is usually a technique of measurement, a way of making a surface calculable, yet in this project it became a way of making a surface alive. Photographs of nature were traced by joining edges and corners until every patch of sky, slope and shadow had been reduced to a triangle in its simplest form. When the photograph was removed, what remained was a drawing without subject, a net of pure relationships. Cutting that net introduced choice. Some versions were divided into separate areas, others were released as a single continuous piece, and each decision altered how the net could later move. Thin wooden sticks were glued along the edges, giving every triangle a frame and every joint a hinge. Flipped, bent and folded in different directions, the nets rose from the table as creatures with spines, wings and claws, their shadows sharper than their bodies. The models suggest that a landscape, once abstracted, does not lose its vitality. It simply exchanges stillness for posture, becoming an animal of geometry that seems ready to crawl away.

zh-Hant.heading: 學會爬行的風景-網格的生命
zh-Hant.body: 三角化通常是一種測量技術，但在這個專題中，它成為一種讓表面活起來的方法。自然的照片被描繪，連接邊緣與角點，直到天空、坡地與陰影的每一塊都被簡化為最簡形式的三角形。當照片被移除，留下的是一張沒有主題的圖，一張純粹由關係構成的網。切割這張網引入了選擇。有些版本被分成獨立的區塊，有些則作為一整片連續的網被釋放，而每一個決定都改變了這張網日後能如何運動。細木棒沿著邊緣黏合，讓每個三角形擁有框架，每個接點成為鉸鏈。在不同方向翻轉、彎折與摺疊後，網格從桌面上升起，成為帶有脊椎、翅膀與爪子的生物。這些模型暗示，一片風景被抽象化之後並不會失去生命力。它只是以姿態取代靜止，成為一隻彷彿隨時要爬走的幾何動物。

pins.title: The Personality Space
pins.description:
Five sides of one personality are sketched as zones inside a box, then built as an acrylic cube of shards, sticks, coloured sand and reflective pieces.

Physical model and drawing | Personality space study | Acrylic, wooden sticks, paper, museum board, wire, sand | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 個性空間
zh-Hant.description:
同一個人的五種個性面向被描繪為盒中的區域，再建構為一座由碎片、木棒、彩色沙與反光片構成的壓克力立方體。

實體模型與繪圖｜個性空間研究｜壓克力、木棒、紙、博物館紙板、鐵絲、沙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The acrylic cube of the personality space.
個性空間的壓克力立方體。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A personality is made of several sides that are difficult to see from outside. The project asked how a single box could hold and reveal these different sides as spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個人的個性由多個從外部難以看見的面向組成。這個專題探問，一個盒子如何能把這些不同的面向容納並呈現為空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches divided a box into zones whose sizes reflected how much of each personality was present. Four sides were named as funny, tolerable, violent and complicated, with the most important side placed in the middle.
captions: A concept sketch of the zones.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖把一個盒子劃分為多個區域，其大小反映每一種個性所占的比例。四個面向被命名為風趣、包容、暴烈與複雜，最重要的一面則被放在中央。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Clear acrylic was used for the outer walls, with thin wooden sticks, paper shards and wire assembled inside. Holes between the layers were planned so that sand could pass through and move around.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 外牆使用透明壓克力，內部則組裝細木棒、紙片與鐵絲。層與層之間預留孔洞，讓沙能穿過並四處移動。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: White and light blue sand softens the sharp shards of the violent side and adds a sense of mystery. Reflective pieces and clear sticks let the sand slide and glitter, so the interior changes with every angle.
captions: Views of the tolerable, violent, funny and complicated zones.
The cube filled with blue sand.
Reflective pieces in the funny zone.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 白色與淺藍色的沙柔化了暴烈一面的尖銳碎片，並增添神秘感。反光片與透明棒讓沙滑動並閃爍，使內部隨著每個角度而變化。
captions: 可容忍、暴力、有趣與複雜各區的視圖。

sections.heading: A Self in Glass - Sand Between the Shards
sections.body: To describe a personality in words is to flatten it, and this project chose instead to give one a volume. A box was imagined as the container of a whole self, and sketches divided it into zones whose proportions reflected how strongly each trait was present. Four sides were named, funny, tolerable, violent and complicated, while the most essential quality was placed at the centre, around a store of water and clear reflective pieces that suggest an easy openness toward others. Built in clear acrylic, the outer walls conceal nothing. Inside, thin sticks, cut paper and wire form thickets of different character: red blades crowd the violent zone, prisms and coloured film brighten the funny one, and dense black lines tangle the complicated corner. Holes between the layers allow white and pale blue sand to drift through the structure, softening sharp edges and veiling parts of the interior. As the cube is turned, the sand slides, glitters and resettles, so that no two views coincide. The model proposes that a character is never fixed, only continually rearranged.

zh-Hant.heading: 玻璃中的自我-碎片之間的沙
zh-Hant.body: 用文字描述一種個性，往往會把它壓扁，這個專題選擇改為賦予它一個體積。一個盒子被想像為完整自我的容器，草圖把它劃分為多個區域，其比例反映每一種特質的強弱。四個面向被命名為風趣、包容、暴烈與複雜，最根本的特質則被放在中央，圍繞著一處儲水與透明反光片。外牆以透明壓克力建造，不隱藏任何東西。內部的細木棒、裁切的紙與鐵絲形成性格各異的叢林，紅色刀片擠滿暴烈的區域，稜鏡與彩色薄片照亮風趣的區域，濃密的黑色線條則纏繞在複雜的角落。層與層之間的孔洞讓白色與淺藍色的沙在結構中漂移，柔化尖銳的邊緣，也遮掩內部的某些部分。當立方體被轉動，沙便滑動、閃爍並重新沉積，使任何兩個視角都不相同。這座模型提出，性格從來不是固定的，而是不斷被重新排列。

pins.title: Thunder
pins.description:
Leaf veins, brain waves and storms are sketched as swirling lines, then built from many small shattered pieces of board into a curving storm with a hollow eye.

Physical model and drawing | Storm form study | Museum board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 雷
zh-Hant.description:
葉脈、腦波與風暴被描繪為旋轉的線條，再以許多細小的碎板片建構為一場帶有中空風眼的彎曲風暴。

實體模型與繪圖｜風暴形式研究｜博物館紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The storm model of shattered board pieces.
碎板片構成的風暴模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A storm is powerful and dangerous, yet its form is made of countless small movements. The project asked how this energy could be captured in a static model.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 風暴強大而危險，但它的形態由無數細小的運動構成。這個專題探問，如何能在一個靜態的模型中捕捉這股能量。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Studies of leaves and clouds found that the veins of a leaf resemble the lines of brain waves. These lines were combined with the swirl of a storm in a series of sketches.
captions: A photo of a storm, with its source link.
Sketches of swirls and storm lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 對葉片與雲的研究發現，葉脈與腦波的線條十分相似。這些線條在一系列草圖中與風暴的漩渦結合。
captions: 一張暴風雨照片及其來源連結。
漩渦與風暴線條的草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The model was built from many little shattered plates of board, set at changing angles along a curve. Gaps and a wind hole were left between the pieces so that the form could breathe.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 模型以許多細小的碎板片建構，沿著一道曲線以不斷變化的角度排列。碎片之間留有縫隙與一個風洞，讓形體得以呼吸。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished storm curls into a wave around a hollow eye and looks powerful from every angle. Its fine details change as the viewer moves, much like a storm of thoughts.
captions: The swirling body of the storm.
The hollow eye of the storm.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的風暴圍繞一個中空的風眼捲成波浪，從每個角度看都充滿力量。它的細節隨著觀者移動而改變，就像一場思緒的風暴。

sections.heading: A Storm of Thought - Shards Around an Empty Eye
sections.body: Weather and thinking share a vocabulary of fronts, pressures and sudden flashes, and this project took that resemblance literally. Studies of leaves and clouds revealed that the branching veins of a leaf echo the jagged traces of brain waves, and sketches began to braid these lines into the coiling motion of a storm. Spirals tightened into knots, strokes stretched into wind, and the drawings suggested a form that would be at once organic and violent. The model translated this energy through fragmentation. Hundreds of small shattered plates of board were set along a sweeping curve, each tilted slightly differently from its neighbour, so that the surface reads as a field of flickering motion rather than a continuous skin. Gaps between the pieces and a hollow wind eye allow light and air to pass through the mass. Seen from above, the storm wraps around its empty centre; seen from the side, it rises as a breaking wave. The work suggests that turbulence is composed of countless small decisions, and that a moment of insight may be the stillness found at the centre of the swirl.

zh-Hant.heading: 思緒的風暴-圍繞空洞風眼的碎片
zh-Hant.body: 天氣與思考共享一套關於鋒面、氣壓與突然閃現的語彙，這個專題把這種相似性當真。對葉片與雲的研究揭示，葉片分枝的脈絡呼應著腦波鋸齒狀的軌跡，草圖開始把這些線條編織成風暴盤繞的運動。漩渦收緊成結，筆觸延伸為風，這些圖暗示一種同時具有有機性與暴烈性的形體。模型透過碎裂來轉譯這股能量。數百片細小的碎板片沿著一道大幅掃過的曲線排列，每一片的傾角都與相鄰的略有不同，使表面讀起來像一片閃爍的運動場，而不是一層連續的表皮。碎片之間的縫隙與一個中空的風眼讓光與空氣穿過量體。從上方看，風暴包圍著空洞的中心；從側面看，它升起為一道正在碎裂的浪。這件作品暗示，紊流由無數細小的決定構成，而靈光乍現的一刻，也許正是漩渦中心的那份靜止。

pins.title: Superimposed Spaces
pins.description:
Nine spatial diagrams are composed into images, built as superimposed study models, redrawn by line weight and finally imagined as a structure cantilevering over a river.

Physical model, drawing and digital model | Diagram-to-model study | Polystyrene foam board, museum board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 疊合的空間
zh-Hant.description:
九張空間圖解被組合成影像，建構為疊合的研究模型，再依線條粗細重繪，最終被想像為一座懸挑於河面上的結構。

實體模型、繪圖與數位模型｜圖解轉模型研究｜聚苯乙烯泡棉板、博物館紙板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The structure imagined over a river.
被想像於河面上的結構。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Flat diagrams can describe spatial effects, yet they say little about the spaces those effects might create. The project asked how two-dimensional diagrams could be converted into three-dimensional study models.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 平面圖解能描述空間效果，卻很少說明這些效果可能創造的空間。這個專題探問，二維圖解如何能轉化為三維的研究模型。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Nine diagrams were drawn from an artwork image, each representing a different concept of spatial effect. Three composite images were then made from these diagrams to create a vivid relation of space.
captions: The source artwork beside a composite image made from the diagrams.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 九張圖解取材自一件藝術作品的影像，各自代表一種空間效果的概念。接著以這些圖解製作三張合成影像，創造鮮明的空間關係。
captions: 原始藝術作品及由圖解組成的合成圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Study models with various geometries and directions were built from the composite images to express superimposition. Photographs of the models from different directions were then combined into new drawings and models.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 依據合成影像建構出具有不同幾何與方向的研究模型，以表達疊合的概念。從不同方向拍攝的模型照片再被組合為新的圖與模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Digital isometrics and line-weight drawings refined the models into draft versions of an architecture. Placed on a site, the structure cantilevers over a river like a boat.
captions: A section render of the structure cantilevered on the river, with a figure.
Rendered views of the imagined experience, with figures.
A rendered model of the structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 數位等角圖與線條粗細圖把模型深化為建築的草擬版本。放置於基地之後，這個結構像一艘船般懸挑於河面上。
captions: 結構懸挑於河上的剖面渲染圖，附人物。
想像體驗的渲染視圖，附人物。

sections.heading: From Diagram to Dwelling - Layers That Learn to Float
sections.body: Diagrams are often treated as a final abstraction, yet this project read them as the beginning of matter. Nine small drawings were extracted from an artwork image, each isolating a distinct spatial effect such as overlap, compression, framing or release. Combined into three composite images, they began to describe relationships rather than objects, and those relationships demanded volume. Study models answered with planes and boxes set at shifting angles, so that every piece seemed to pass through another. The idea of superimposition then turned back upon the process itself. Photographs of the models, taken from different directions, were cut and recombined into hybrid works that are neither drawing nor model, opening spaces that no single view could contain. Digital isometrics followed, and line weights were varied to register distance from the nearest point of sight, translating depth into graphic intensity. Only at the end did a site appear. Set above a river, the structure cantilevers outward like a moored boat, suggesting that a building may emerge from careful translation rather than from an initial image of form.

zh-Hant.heading: 從圖解到棲居-學會漂浮的層次
zh-Hant.body: 圖解常被視為最終的抽象，但這個專題把它讀作物質的開端。九張小圖取材自一件藝術作品的影像，各自分離出一種獨特的空間效果，例如重疊、壓縮、框景或釋放。它們被組合成三張合成影像後，開始描述關係而非物件，而這些關係需要體積。研究模型以不同角度的板片與盒體回應，使每一片彷彿都穿過另一片。疊合的構想接著回頭作用於過程本身。從不同方向拍攝的模型照片被剪裁並重新組合，成為既非圖也非模型的混合作品，打開任何單一視角都無法容納的空間。隨後進行數位等角圖，線條粗細依與最近視點的距離而變化，把深度轉譯為圖面的強度。直到最後，基地才出現。這個結構架在河面之上，像一艘停泊的船般向外懸挑，暗示建築可以從細心的轉譯中浮現，而非始於一個預設的形式意象。

pins.title: Labyrinth
pins.description:
Two patterns are tested in gypsum, card and wooden sticks, then grown into stacked stick labyrinths and forests of curved planes that record the passage of material time.

Physical model and drawing | Material and pattern study | Wooden sticks, gypsum | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 迷宮
zh-Hant.description:
兩種圖案以石膏、卡紙與木棒進行測試，再發展為層疊的木棒迷宮與彎曲板片構成的森林，記錄材料時間的流逝。

實體模型與繪圖｜材料與圖案研究｜木棒、石膏｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Materials carry a feeling of time, yet this feeling is hard to describe in words. The project asked how the properties of materials could become an abstract experience of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 材料承載著時間的感受，但這種感受難以用文字描述。這個專題探問，材料的特性如何能成為一種抽象的空間經驗。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Observing a construction site showed how one material can be transformed into another during building. Two patterns, one of nested right angles and one of radiating curves, were drawn as starting points.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 觀察工地讓人看見，一種材料如何在建造過程中轉化為另一種材料。兩種圖案被繪製為起點，一種是層層嵌套的直角，另一種是放射的曲線。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first pattern was tested in gypsum and layered wooden pieces, producing blocks with stepped edges. These tests were stacked and threaded with sticks to grow upward into a frame.
captions: Material tests of the first pattern.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一種圖案以石膏與層疊的木片測試，產生帶有階梯狀邊緣的塊體。這些試驗品被堆疊，並以木棒串接，向上生長為一個框架。
captions: 第一種圖案的材料試驗。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The first labyrinth rises as a dense stack of sticks and blocks with paths winding through it. The second becomes a forest of curved card planes and tall sticks, where light moves between the layers.
captions: A low view of the frame.
A forest of sticks and planes.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第一座迷宮升起為由木棒與塊體構成的密集堆疊，路徑在其中蜿蜒。第二座則成為由彎曲卡紙板片與高木棒構成的森林，光線在層次之間移動。
captions: 木棒與板片構成的森林。

sections.heading: Material Time - Paths Through Stacked Matter
sections.body: Every material holds a sense of duration, the slow setting of plaster, the grain of wood laid down over years, and this project tried to make such duration spatial. Observation of a construction site offered a starting insight: building often transforms one substance into another, leaving traces of what came before. Two patterns became the means of inquiry. The first, a field of nested right angles, was cast and carved in gypsum and layered timber, producing blocks whose stepped edges recall terraces or worn stairs. The second, a set of radiating curves, was cut from card and bent into sweeping planes. Each pattern was then allowed to grow. Stacked and threaded with wooden sticks, the blocks rose into a dense labyrinth where narrow paths wind between cantilevered pieces, while the curved planes gathered among tall sticks to form a luminous forest. The contrast is instructive. One labyrinth is heavy and enclosing, the other light and porous, yet both invite movement and pause. Together they suggest that a maze can be a record of material time.

zh-Hant.heading: 材料的時間-穿越層疊物質的路徑
zh-Hant.body: 每一種材料都蘊含著時間感，石膏緩慢的凝固、木材經年累積的紋理，這個專題試圖讓這樣的時間成為空間。對工地的觀察提供了起點，建造往往把一種物質轉化為另一種，並留下先前的痕跡。兩種圖案成為探索的方法。第一種是層層嵌套的直角，以石膏與層疊木料鑄造與雕刻，產生階梯狀邊緣的塊體，令人聯想到梯田或磨損的階梯。第二種是一組放射的曲線，以卡紙裁切並彎折為大幅掃過的板片。每一種圖案隨後被允許生長。塊體經堆疊並以木棒串接，升起為一座密集的迷宮，狹窄的路徑在懸挑的構件之間蜿蜒，彎曲板片則聚集在高木棒之間，形成一片明亮的森林。兩者的對比富有啟發。一座迷宮沉重而包覆，另一座輕盈而通透，卻都邀請移動與停留。它們共同暗示，迷宮可以是材料時間的紀錄。

pins.title: Architectural Features
pins.description:
Photographs of old buildings mixing eastern and western styles are sketched and deconstructed, then rebuilt in PVC board as a white model and a brightly coloured playground of arches and stairs.

Physical model and drawing | Facade deconstruction study | PVC board | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 建築特徵
zh-Hant.description:
融合東西方風格的老建築照片被描繪與解構，再以PVC板重建為一座白色模型，以及一座由拱門與階梯構成的鮮豔遊樂場。

實體模型與繪圖｜立面解構研究｜PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The coloured model of arches and stairs.
拱門與階梯構成的彩色模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Old buildings that mix eastern and western styles are rich in arches, balconies and stairs. The project asked how these features could be taken apart and reassembled into a new spatial base.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 融合東西方風格的老建築擁有豐富的拱門、陽台與階梯。這個專題探問，這些特徵如何能被拆解並重新組合為新的空間基礎。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Photographs taken from various angles were traced into line drawings of arches, columns and facades. A dense sketch then gathered these features into one layered composition.
captions: Location photos of the buildings beside the deconstruction sketches.
The film still and the colour palette taken from it.
A layered sketch of facade features.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 從不同角度拍攝的照片被描繪為拱門、柱子與立面的線條圖。接著一張密集的草圖把這些特徵匯集為一個層疊的構成。
captions: 建築的現場照片及解構草圖。
電影劇照及取自其中的色票。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The features were rebuilt in white PVC board as intersecting walls, arches and flights of stairs. Studying the white model revealed new spaces where the old elements overlap.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 這些特徵以白色PVC板重建為相互交錯的牆、拱門與階梯。對白色模型的研究揭示了舊元素重疊之處所形成的新空間。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A final version was painted in a palette of soft pinks, blues and yellows recalling a cherished childhood. With these colours the model looks like a playground for people of every age.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終版本以柔和的粉紅、藍與黃色上色，喚起珍視的童年。有了這些色彩，模型看來像一座適合各年齡的人遊玩的遊樂場。

sections.heading: Arches Remembered in Colour - A Playground of Fragments
sections.body: Historic quarters where eastern and western traditions meet often accumulate a rich vocabulary of arches, balconies, columns and stairs, and this project treated that vocabulary as material for invention rather than preservation. Photographs taken from many angles were traced into line drawings, isolating each feature from its original wall. A dense ink sketch then let the fragments collide, stacking facades, colonnades and staircases into a single restless elevation. Translation into PVC board followed. In the white model, walls intersect, arches open onto unexpected depths and stairs climb toward platforms that belong to no single building, so that the overlaps of the old elements generate new rooms. A second version introduced colour. Drawing on a palette of soft pinks, pale blues, mustard and coral associated with a cherished childhood, the surfaces were painted so that each fragment could be read separately while joining a cheerful whole. The effect shifts the model from ruin to playground. It suggests that heritage can be received playfully, its forms remembered through recombination and its atmosphere renewed through colour.

zh-Hant.heading: 以色彩記憶的拱門-碎片的遊樂場
zh-Hant.body: 東西方傳統交會的歷史街區，常累積出由拱門、陽台、柱子與階梯構成的豐富語彙，這個專題把這套語彙當作創造的材料，而非保存的對象。從多個角度拍攝的照片被描繪為線條圖。接著一張濃密的墨線草圖讓這些碎片相互碰撞，把立面、柱廊與階梯層疊為一個躁動的立面。隨後轉譯為PVC板。在白色模型中，牆面相互交錯，拱門通向出乎意料的深處，階梯攀向不屬於任何單一建築的平台，使舊元素的重疊生成新的房間。第二個版本引入了色彩。取自與珍視童年相連的柔和粉紅、淺藍、芥黃與珊瑚色，表面被上色，使每個碎片既能被單獨辨識，又融入一個愉悅的整體。這樣的效果讓模型從廢墟轉變為遊樂場。它暗示遺產可以被輕快地接收，形式透過重組被記住，氛圍則透過色彩被更新。

pins.title: Tower of Memory
pins.description:
Coloured glue blocks filled with old objects form a memory base, from which coloured stick frames carrying toys and dried plants climb into a crowded tower.

Physical model and drawing | Memory tower study | Wooden sticks, glue, old toys | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 記憶之塔
zh-Hant.description:
填入舊物的彩色膠塊構成記憶的基座，承載玩具與乾燥植物的彩色木棒框架從其上攀升為一座擁擠的塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜記憶塔研究｜木棒、膠、舊玩具｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Childhood memories are vivid and fragmented, mixing play, objects and later disappointments. The project asked how such memories could be stacked into a single structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 童年記憶鮮明而破碎，混合著遊戲、物件與日後的失落。這個專題探問，這樣的記憶如何能被堆疊為單一的結構。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Old toys and small objects were collected as fragments of a past life. Solid glue blocks filled with colour and these objects were made to act as a base of memory.
captions: A collage of film and game images that inspired the tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
