zh-Hant.body: 舊玩具與小物件被收集為過往生活的碎片。以色彩與這些物件填充的實心膠塊被製作出來，作為記憶的基座。
captions: 啟發這座塔的電影與遊戲圖像拼貼。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Coloured wooden sticks were built upward from the base as an open frame. Toys, tubes and dried plants were threaded into the frame at every level.
captions: Making the glue blocks and sticks by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 彩色木棒從基座向上搭建為一個敞開的框架。玩具、管子與乾燥植物在每一層被穿插進框架之中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower glows with translucent blocks below and a tangle of objects above. It reflects both the joy of childhood and the complexity of society and broken friendship.
captions: A crowded level of the tower.
Plants and toys among the sticks.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔下方有半透明的塊體發光，上方則是物件的糾結。它同時反映童年的喜悅，以及社會與破裂友誼的複雜。

sections.heading: Sediment of Play - Climbing Out of Childhood
sections.body: Memory rarely arrives as a clear narrative. It returns in fragments, a toy, a colour, an object once held, and this project built a tower from exactly such fragments. At its base, solid blocks of tinted glue encase small belongings like insects in amber, preserving them while rendering them slightly out of reach. These translucent blocks form a foundation of memory, glowing whenever light passes through. From this base an open frame of coloured wooden sticks climbs upward, and at every level toys, tubes, wires and dried flowers are threaded into the structure. The density increases as the tower rises, so that clarity below gives way to tangle above. A detailed drawing records this accumulation with the patience of an inventory. The work holds two readings at once. It celebrates the brightness and invention of early play, yet it also registers the complexity of growing up, including the fracture of a close friendship. In that tension the tower becomes a vertical diary, where memories are not ordered by time but stacked by weight.

zh-Hant.heading: 遊戲的沉積-從童年攀升而出
zh-Hant.body: 記憶很少以清晰的敘事抵達。它以碎片的方式回來，一件玩具、一種顏色、一件曾經握過的物品，這個專題正是以這樣的碎片建造了一座塔。在基座，染色的實心膠塊把小物件封存其中，如同琥珀中的昆蟲，在保存它們的同時，也讓它們變得稍稍遙不可及。這些半透明的塊體構成記憶的基礎，每當光線穿過便會發亮。彩色木棒構成的敞開框架從基座向上攀升，玩具、管子、鐵絲與乾燥花在每一層被穿插進結構之中。塔越往上，密度越高，使下方的清晰逐漸讓位給上方的糾結。一張細膩的圖以清點般的耐心記錄這樣的累積。這件作品同時容納兩種解讀。它頌揚早年遊戲的明亮與創造，也記錄成長的複雜，包括一段親密友誼的破裂。在這樣的張力中，塔成為一本垂直的日記，記憶不依時間排序，而是依重量堆疊。

pins.title: Fireworks
pins.description:
The bursting of a firework is modelled as treelike frames of PVC and sticks, first as a chaotic white version and then as an ordered, colourful tower of rings and geometric rooms.

Physical model and drawing | Firework form study | PVC board, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 煙火
zh-Hant.description:
煙火的綻放被模擬為由PVC與木棒構成的樹狀框架，先是一個混亂的白色版本，再成為一座由環圈與幾何房間構成的有序彩色塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜煙火形式研究｜PVC板、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The first model of a treelike frame.
樹狀框架的第一個模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A firework sparkles randomly, while architecture is usually built in order. The project asked how the contrast between chaos and order could reveal the development of space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 煙火隨機地閃爍，而建築通常依秩序建造。這個專題探問，混亂與秩序之間的對比如何能揭示空間的發展。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The blossoming of a firework was studied as a trunk that rises and then bursts into branches. Early studies tested how sticks and small boxes could follow this movement.
captions: An early study of sticks and boxes.
A drawing of the chaotic version.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 煙火的綻放被研究為一根先上升、再爆開為枝條的主幹。早期研究測試木棒與小盒體如何能跟隨這樣的運動。
captions: 木棒與盒體的早期研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The first model set geometric rooms above the branches of a treelike frame to show its strength. Close views tested how the rooms balance among the radiating sticks.
captions: A close view of the rooms.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第一個模型把幾何房間放在樹狀框架的枝條之上，以展現它的力量。近景研究測試房間如何在放射的木棒之間取得平衡。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final version adds coloured film, rings and new shapes, lifting the burst onto a spiralling trunk. It strengthens the connection between people and architecture, like the sparkle and strength of life.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終版本加入彩色薄膜、環圈與新的形狀，把綻放抬升到一根盤旋的主幹上。它加強了人與建築之間的連結，就像生命的閃耀與力量。

sections.heading: Order Inside the Burst - A Tree of Sparks
sections.body: A firework lasts only seconds, yet its form is surprisingly legible: a single line rises, pauses and then breaks into a crown of radiating paths. This project read that sequence as a lesson in structure. If the trunk carries the load and the burst distributes it, then a firework resembles a tree, and a tree can hold rooms. Early studies tested sticks and small boxes along this logic, and a first model set geometric chambers among the branches of a treelike frame, letting them perch at shifting angles as if caught mid-flight. The contrast between random sparks and ordered building was deliberately kept visible, so that the chaotic white version reads as an explosion arrested just before it scatters. The final version answered with order and colour. A spiralling trunk of rings lifts the burst higher, and translucent coloured film catches light among the sticks like trailing sparks. What began as a study of a fleeting event becomes a meditation on vitality, suggesting that architecture may borrow from celebration the energy to rise and the generosity to open outward.

zh-Hant.heading: 綻放中的秩序-火花之樹
zh-Hant.body: 煙火只持續幾秒，但它的形式出奇地清晰，一條線上升、停頓，然後碎裂為放射狀路徑構成的冠。這個專題把這段過程讀作一堂結構的課。如果主幹承載重量，而綻放把重量分散，那麼煙火就像一棵樹，而一棵樹可以容納房間。早期研究依循這套邏輯測試木棒與小盒體，第一個模型則把幾何房間安置在樹狀框架的枝條之間，讓它們以不斷變化的角度棲息。隨機火花與有序建造之間的對比被刻意保留，使混亂的白色版本讀起來像一場在散落之前被凝止的爆炸。最終版本以秩序與色彩回應。由環圈構成的盤旋主幹把綻放抬得更高，半透明的彩色薄膜在木棒間捕捉光線，如同拖曳的火花。始於一個轉瞬事件的研究，最終成為一段關於生命力的沉思，暗示建築可以從慶典中借來上升的能量與向外敞開的慷慨。

pins.title: Imaginal Space-Response
pins.description:
Points, lines and planes drawn from a painting are distributed in space and divided by many rhythmic wooden strips, building a tall tower of light and shadow on a clinker base.

Physical model and drawing | Rhythm and light study | Clinker, wood, clay | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 想像空間的回應
zh-Hant.description:
從一幅畫中提取的點、線與面被分布於空間之中，並以大量具節奏的木條劃分，在熟料基座上建構出一座光影交錯的高塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜節奏與光線研究｜熟料、木材、黏土｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The tower of rhythmic wooden strips.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Light can give a space a sense of rhythmic movement that responds to the people within it. The project asked how such rhythm could be created with a limited set of materials.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 光線能賦予空間一種節奏性的運動感，並回應身處其中的人。這個專題探問，如何能以一組有限的材料創造這樣的節奏。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Groups of points, lines and planes were extracted from an abstract painting and stretched into three dimensions. An early model tested how these elements could be distributed in an orderly way.
captions: The source painting and the elements extracted from it.
An early model of the effect.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 點、線與面的組合從一幅抽象畫中被提取出來，並延展為三維。一個早期模型測試這些元素如何能有秩序地分布。
captions: 原始畫作及從中萃取的元素。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A large number of wooden strips were woven into the frame to divide the space and create interactive places. Clinker and clay formed a heavy base beneath the light timber.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 大量木條被編入框架之中，以劃分空間並創造互動的場所。熟料與黏土在輕盈的木材下方形成沉重的基座。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished tower rises as stacked volumes wrapped in vertical strips that cast striped shadows. As light changes, the rhythm of the strips seems to move across the surfaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的塔升起為以垂直木條包覆的層疊量體，投下條紋狀的影子。隨著光線變化，木條的節奏似乎在表面上移動。

sections.heading: Rhythm Made of Shadow - Strips Answering Light
sections.body: Some spaces seem to move even when nothing in them changes, because light passing across repeated elements produces a pulse. This project set out to construct that pulse deliberately. Its starting point was an abstract painting, from which groups of points, lines and planes were extracted and stretched into three dimensions, transforming a flat composition into a set of spatial instructions. An early model distributed these elements in an orderly frame and tested their effect under light. The decisive move was repetition. A large number of thin wooden strips were woven into the frame, dividing the volume into bands of solid and void and creating places where a body might pause or pass. Beneath this delicate timber, a base of clinker and clay provides weight and texture, anchoring the composition. The finished tower rises as a stack of volumes wrapped in vertical strips, and when light falls across them it draws striped shadows that shift as the source moves. The work suggests that rhythm in architecture is less a property of form than an event shared between structure, light and the observer.

zh-Hant.heading: 由影子構成的節奏-回應光線的木條
zh-Hant.body: 有些空間即使其中沒有任何改變，似乎仍在移動，因為光線掠過重複的元素時會產生脈動。這個專題著手刻意建構這樣的脈動。它的起點是一幅抽象畫，從中提取出點、線與面的組合並延展為三維，把平面的構成轉化為一組空間的指令。一個早期模型把這些元素分布在有秩序的框架中，並測試它們在光線下的效果。決定性的一步是重複。大量細木條被編入框架，把體積劃分為實與虛的帶狀，創造讓身體得以停留或穿越的場所。在這些纖細的木材下方，熟料與黏土構成的基座提供重量與質感，穩定整個構成。完成的塔升起為以垂直木條包覆的層疊量體，當光線落在其上，便畫出隨光源移動而變化的條紋影子。這件作品暗示，建築中的節奏與其說是形式的屬性，不如說是結構、光線與觀者共同參與的事件。

pins.title: Four Rooms of Rebirth
pins.description:
A story of loss and renewal is divided into four episodes, each answered by a material and a space, and stacked into one tower of tunnels, cages, colourful rooms and gates.

Physical model and drawing | Narrative space study | PVC board, wooden sticks, clay, iridescent film, foam balls | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重生的四個房間
zh-Hant.description:
一段關於失落與重生的故事被分為四個段落，各自以一種材料與空間回應，並堆疊成一座由隧道、籠子、彩色房間與門構成的塔。

實體模型與繪圖｜敘事空間研究｜PVC板、木棒、黏土、幻彩膜、泡棉球｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The finished tower of four rooms.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A narrative is usually read in sequence, while a space is experienced all at once. The project asked how four episodes of a story could be translated into four connected spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 敘事通常依序被閱讀，空間卻是一次被整體經驗。這個專題探問，一個故事的四個段落如何能轉譯為四個相連的空間。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The story was divided into a fall, a refusal, a discovery of the senses and a return. Each episode was sketched as a spatial figure such as a tunnel, a cage or a colourful room.
captions: The poster of the film that inspired the project.
Film stills of the four parts of the story around the coloured sketch of the four spaces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 故事被分為墜落、拒絕、感官的發現與回歸四段。每一段都被描繪為一種空間形象，例如隧道、籠子或彩色房間。
captions: 故事四個段落的電影劇照，環繞四個空間的彩色草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Spiralling PVC strips and rings formed the tunnel of the fall, while a black box set in stone clay expressed reluctance and doubt. Stick frames and a line drawing then organised the episodes into one climbing structure.
captions: Making the model by hand, from clay to coloured film.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 螺旋的PVC條與圓環構成墜落的隧道，而嵌在石塑黏土中的黑盒則表達猶豫與懷疑。木棒框架與一張線稿再把各段落組織為一個向上攀升的結構。
captions: 親手製作模型，從黏土到彩色膠片。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Floating foam balls, blue stairs and iridescent gates mark the joy of the senses and the way back to life. Read from base to top, the tower turns a story into a route that can be climbed.
captions: The black box beneath the rings.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 漂浮的泡棉球、藍色階梯與幻彩的門，標示感官的喜悅與回到生命的路徑。由基座讀到頂端，這座塔把故事化為一條可以攀登的路線。

sections.heading: Story Climbed - Rooms Between Loss and Return
sections.body: This project begins with a conviction that a story can be inhabited as well as told. A narrative of loss and renewal is divided into four episodes, and each is given a spatial body rather than an illustration. The fall becomes a tunnel of spiralling strips and suspended rings, through which fragments of memory seem to drift. Reluctance becomes a black box sunk in heavy stone clay, a cave in which doubt can hide. The discovery of the senses becomes a room of colour, filled with floating foam balls and iridescent film that changes with every glance. The return becomes a set of bright gates at the summit. Stacked rather than placed side by side, these episodes form a single tower, so that the sequence of the plot is converted into vertical movement. A viewer reads the work by climbing it with the eye, passing from darkness to colour. In this way the model proposes that architecture can hold time, and that emotional change may be measured in steps, thresholds and light.

zh-Hant.heading: 可攀登的故事-失落與回歸之間的房間
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題始於一個信念：故事不僅能被講述，也能被居住。一段關於失落與重生的敘事被分為四個段落，每一段都獲得一個空間的身體，而非一幅插圖。墜落化為由螺旋條帶與懸浮圓環構成的隧道，記憶的碎片彷彿在其中漂流。猶豫化為沉入厚重石塑黏土的黑盒，是一個讓懷疑得以藏身的洞穴。感官的發現化為一個色彩的房間，充滿漂浮的泡棉球與隨每次注視而變化的幻彩膜。回歸則化為頂端一組明亮的門。這些段落並非並置，而是堆疊為一座塔，使情節的順序轉化為垂直的移動。觀者以目光攀登來閱讀作品，從黑暗走向色彩。這個模型由此提出，建築能夠承載時間，而情感的轉變或許可以用階梯、門檻與光線來丈量。

pins.title: Rhythmic Canvas Fusion
pins.description:
Successive dance poses are traced into overlapping lines, and the lines are rebuilt as a field of stick frames and folded white planes that a visitor moves through like a stage.

Physical model and drawing | Movement-to-space study | PVC board, wooden sticks | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 節奏畫布的融合
zh-Hant.description:
連續的舞姿被描繪為重疊的線條，這些線條再被重建為由木棒框架與摺疊白色平面構成的場域，讓訪客如在舞台般穿行其中。

實體模型與繪圖｜動作轉空間研究｜PVC板、木棒｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The field of frames and folded planes.
框架與摺疊平面構成的場域。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Dance exists in time and disappears as soon as it is performed. The project asked how the fluid motion of a dancer could be captured in a lasting architectural space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 舞蹈存在於時間之中，一經演出便消逝。這個專題探問，舞者流動的動作如何能被捕捉於持久的建築空間中。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Following the method of a painting that shows a figure in successive positions, a sequence of dance poses was reduced to joints and lines. Overlaid on one sheet, the lines formed an abstract drawing of rhythm.
captions: Photos of the dance beside the figure sketches drawn from them.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 依循一幅以連續位置描繪人物的畫作的方法，一連串舞姿被簡化為關節與線條。疊加在同一張紙上，這些線條形成一張抽象的節奏圖。
captions: 舞蹈照片及從中描繪的人物草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Folded white planes were stacked along a spine to test how the drawing could gain depth. Stick frames were then threaded among the folds to give the movement a measurable structure.
captions: Folds and frames in close view.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 摺疊的白色平面沿著一條軸線堆疊，測試這張圖如何獲得深度。接著木棒框架被穿插於摺面之間，為動作提供可量度的結構。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final model spreads the frames and folds into a wide field dotted with small red figures. Visitors would pass through it as through a stage, meeting changing rhythms of enclosure and openness.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型把框架與摺面展開為一片點綴著小紅人的寬闊場域。訪客將如穿越舞台般通過其中，遇見圍合與開放不斷變化的節奏。

sections.heading: Motion Held Still - Folds of a Dancing Field
sections.body: Dance is perhaps the most fleeting of the arts, vanishing in the instant of its performance, and this project asks whether architecture might hold some trace of that disappearance. Its method borrows from painting that records a figure in successive positions. A sequence of dance poses is reduced to joints and connecting strokes, then overlaid until the separate bodies dissolve into a single drawing of rhythm. From this drawing the model takes its two materials. Folded white planes, stacked along a spine, give the strokes depth and the quality of fabric caught in motion. Thin stick frames, threaded among the folds, supply measure and order, like a score beneath a performance. Spread across a wide base, the frames and folds become a field rather than an object, and small red figures reveal its scale. To walk through it would be to repeat the dance at a slower tempo, moving from compressed passages to sudden openings. The project thus suggests that space can serve as a stage that remembers.

zh-Hant.heading: 被留住的動作-舞動場域的摺痕
zh-Hant.body: 舞蹈或許是最短暫的藝術，在演出的瞬間便消逝，這個專題探問建築能否留住這種消逝的某種痕跡。它的方法借自以連續位置記錄人物的繪畫。一連串舞姿被簡化為關節與連接的筆觸，再層層疊加，直到各個身體溶解為一張節奏之圖。模型的兩種材料皆源於這張圖。沿軸線堆疊的摺疊白色平面賦予筆觸深度，以及布料在動作中被捕捉的質感。穿插於摺面之間的細木棒框架提供尺度與秩序，宛如演出下方的樂譜。展開於寬闊的基座上，框架與摺面成為一片場域而非一個物件，點點小紅人揭示其尺度。穿行其中，就是以較慢的節拍重演這支舞，從壓縮的通道走向突然的開敞。這個專題由此暗示，空間可以成為一座懂得記憶的舞台。

pins.title: Living in the Deep Sea
pins.description:
Dense ink drawings of reef life lead to a blue unit space filled with foam granules, acrylic balls and dried flowers that lets a visitor feel the depth of the sea.

Installation and drawing | Ecosystem unit space | Polystyrene granules, non-woven fabric, dried flowers, acrylic balls | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 棲居深海
zh-Hant.description:
描繪珊瑚礁生物的濃密墨線圖，引向一個以泡棉顆粒、壓克力球與乾燥花填滿的藍色單元空間，讓訪客感受海洋的深度。

裝置與繪圖｜生態單元空間｜聚苯乙烯顆粒、不織布、乾燥花、壓克力球｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The blue unit space of the deep sea.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The deep sea is the largest ecosystem on the planet, yet it is threatened by climate change and pollution while remaining almost unseen. The project asked how its beauty could be shown to people as a space they can experience.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 深海是地球上最大的生態系，卻受到氣候變遷與污染的威脅，又幾乎不為人所見。這個專題探問，它的美如何能以一個可經驗的空間呈現給人們。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Reef forms, shells, jellyfish and turtles were studied through dense ink drawings. The patterns of these drawings became a vocabulary of clusters, tendrils and layered textures.
captions: An ink drawing of reef life.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 珊瑚礁的形態、貝殼、水母與海龜透過濃密的墨線圖被研究。這些圖的紋樣成為由群聚、捲鬚與層疊質地構成的語彙。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: A painted study fixed the deep blue atmosphere with shoals of fish over dark seaweed. The palette and layering were then carried into the materials of a cube-shaped unit.
captions: A painted study of the deep sea.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一張彩繪研究以暗色海草上方的魚群確立深藍的氛圍。接著這種色彩與層次被帶入一個立方體單元的材料中。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Foam granules, acrylic balls, non-woven fabric and dried flowers fill the unit with clusters that recall coral and drifting life. Looking inside gives a situational experience of the deep sea from within an enclosed space.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 泡棉顆粒、壓克力球、不織布與乾燥花以讓人聯想珊瑚與漂流生命的群聚填滿這個單元。向內觀看，便能在一個圍合空間中獲得深海的情境經驗。

sections.heading: Blue Within a Box - Drawing the Depth of the Sea
sections.body: The deep sea is the largest ecosystem on the planet and also one of the least seen, and this project responds to that paradox by building a small world that can be looked into. Its research begins with the patient discipline of ink. Reef forms, shells, jellyfish and turtles are drawn in dense, repetitive marks until their outlines dissolve into fields of texture, revealing the clustering and branching logic that shapes underwater life. A painted study then sets an atmosphere of deep blue in which shoals of fish pass above dark weeds. These lessons are translated into a cube. Inside it, foam granules gather into mounds that resemble coral, acrylic balls float like bubbles or eggs, and dried flowers and fabric suggest drifting plants. The unit space does not imitate any single place; it condenses many observations into one immersive scene. By asking viewers to lean close, the work turns ecological concern into intimacy, suggesting that care for a distant environment may begin with the experience of its beauty.

zh-Hant.heading: 盒中之藍-描繪海的深度
zh-Hant.body: 深海是地球上最大的生態系，也是最少被看見的生態系之一，這個專題以建構一個可以向內觀看的小世界回應這個矛盾。研究始於墨線耐心的紀律。珊瑚礁的形態、貝殼、水母與海龜以濃密而重複的筆觸被描繪，直到輪廓溶解為質地的場域，揭示塑造水下生命的群聚與分枝邏輯。接著一張彩繪研究確立深藍的氛圍，魚群從暗色海草上方游過。這些體會被轉譯為一個立方體。在其中，泡棉顆粒聚成彷彿珊瑚的小丘，壓克力球如氣泡或卵般漂浮，乾燥花與布料暗示漂流的植物。這個單元空間並不模仿任何單一場所，而是把許多觀察凝聚為一個沉浸的場景。藉由邀請觀者貼近，作品把生態的關切轉化為親密，暗示對遙遠環境的關懷，或許始於對其美的經驗。

pins.title: A Peaceful World
pins.description:
An anti-war education centre is composed by decomposing a giant robot from an animation into spaces of oppression, conflict, hope and connection along one route.

Drawing, model and digital model | Anti-war education centre | Study models, sections, renders | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 和平的世界
zh-Hant.description:
一座反戰教育中心的設計，把動畫中的巨大機器人拆解為壓迫、衝突、希望與連結的空間，並沿一條路線串連。

繪圖、模型與數位模型｜反戰教育中心｜研究模型、剖面、渲染圖｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The shattered tower above the centre.
矗立於中心上方的碎裂之塔。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: War is often remembered through images of power and spectacle, which can hide the suffering it causes. The project asked how a building could lead visitors from the fascination of force towards an understanding of peace.
captions: A collage of war photographs and animation scenes.
Site analysis of the city and its visitors.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 戰爭常透過力量與奇觀的影像被記憶，這些影像可能遮蔽它所造成的苦難。這個專題探問，一座建築如何能引導訪客從對武力的迷戀走向對和平的理解。
captions: 戰爭照片與動畫場景的拼貼。
城市與訪客的基地分析。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A giant robot from an animation was decomposed into its components, and each part was tied to a scene of the story from repression to a whole world. Each scene was then refined into a simple spatial form such as a split, a spiral or a bridge.
captions: The robot decomposed into story scenes.
Spatial forms refined from each scene.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 動畫中的一具巨大機器人被拆解為各個構件，每個部件都對應故事中從壓迫到完整世界的一幕。接著每一幕再被提煉為一種簡單的空間形式，例如裂縫、螺旋或橋。
captions: 被拆解為故事場景的機器人。
從每一幕提煉出的空間形式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Six study models tested spaces of repression, gunfire, confusion, hope, passion and resistance, each paired with a reference photograph. They were then joined in a long sequence that runs from a depressed battlefield to a road of hope.
captions: Six study models of the scenes.
The long sequence of the first building.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 六個研究模型測試了壓迫、槍火、迷惘、希望、熱情與抵抗的空間，各自搭配一張參考照片。它們再被串連為一條長序列，從低陷的戰場延伸到希望之路。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A second building places a shattered tower over a wide hall, while a third links rocky masses with bridges and stairs as a place of connection. Sections show visitors climbing from enclosed darkness towards open light.
captions: Renders of the hall and the shattered tower.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第二棟建築把碎裂的塔置於寬闊大廳之上，第三棟則以橋與階梯連結岩塊般的量體，成為連結的場所。剖面顯示訪客從封閉的黑暗向開敞的光線攀升。
captions: 大廳與碎裂之塔的渲染圖。

sections.heading: Armour Undone - A Route from Force to Understanding
sections.body: This project takes as its starting point an uncomfortable truth: images of war are often thrilling, and the machines of destruction are drawn with a beauty that can obscure the suffering they bring. Rather than reject that fascination, the design works through it. A giant robot from an animation is taken apart piece by piece, and each component is assigned a chapter in a story that moves from repression and fear towards hope and reconciliation. These chapters are distilled into elementary spatial gestures, a split ground, a spiral of walls, a compressed corridor, a bridge. Study models translate the gestures into rooms of shadow, texture and pressure, which are then threaded into a long route. Visitors descend into a depressed battlefield, pass beneath a hail of fragments and gradually rise towards light, finally crossing bridges between rocky masses that suggest a world held together by mutual effort. The centre thus becomes an instrument of persuasion, proposing that peace is not imposed by strength but reached through understanding.

zh-Hant.heading: 卸下的鎧甲-從武力走向理解的路徑
zh-Hant.body: 這個專題從一個令人不安的事實出發：戰爭的影像常令人興奮，毀滅的機器被描繪得如此美麗，足以遮蔽它們帶來的苦難。設計並不排斥這種迷戀，而是穿越它。動畫中的一具巨大機器人被逐件拆解，每個構件都被賦予故事中的一章，從壓迫與恐懼走向希望與和解。這些章節被提煉為基本的空間姿態：裂開的地面、螺旋的牆、壓縮的廊道、一座橋。研究模型把這些姿態轉譯為由陰影、質感與壓力構成的房間，再串連為一條漫長的路線。訪客下降至低陷的戰場，穿過碎片的驟雨，逐步升向光明，最後跨越連結岩塊量體的橋，暗示一個靠彼此努力維繫的世界。這座中心由此成為一件說服的工具，提出和平並非由力量強加，而是透過理解而抵達。

pins.title: Renovation of the Family Hotel
pins.description:
A late-Qing courtyard house in an old alley is renewed as a family hotel, keeping its four-courtyard pattern while hollowed floors draw light, rain and air into the rooms.

Chaozhou, China | Hotel renovation | Mar 2018 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 家族旅館改造
zh-Hant.description:
一座位於老巷中的晚清合院民居被改造為家族旅館，保留原有的四合格局，並以鏤空的樓板把陽光、雨水與空氣引入室內。

中國潮州｜旅館改造｜2018年3月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model with its tiled roof and balcony.
帶有瓦屋頂與陽台的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Most renovations of old buildings in the region strip their interiors and keep only a facade. This house, once a family residence and later a warehouse, had been turned into a guesthouse that kept its original appearance, and the project asked whether an old building can meet present needs without losing its character.
captions: Sketches of the streets and landmarks of the old town.
The port history of the region drawn on a painted map.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 當地多數老建築的翻修只保留立面而掏空內部。這座房子曾是家族宅第，後來成為倉庫，再被改造為保留原貌的民宿；專題由此探問，老建築能否在不失去性格的前提下回應當代的使用需求。
captions: 老城街道與地標的速寫。
以繪製地圖呈現的區域港口歷史。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The site was mapped within the grid of old streets and compared with a reference renovation. The house follows the local four-points-of-gold type, with halls on the front and back and rooms around courtyards, a pattern that later grew a new layer of halls.
captions: Site analysis of the old streets and the house.
The courtyard pattern adapted to new uses, with a long section.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 基地被放回老街的紋理中分析，並與一個參考改造案比較。這座房子屬於當地的「四點金」形制，前後設廳、房間環繞天井，這個格局後來又長出新一層的廳堂。
captions: 老街與房子的基地分析。
因應新用途調整的合院格局與長剖面。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The ground floor keeps the axial layout, while floors above the central axis and the two courtyards are hollowed so that sunlight reaches every level. A sequence of operations split, merged and recombined the volumes before the rooms were fixed.
captions: Plans before and after, elevations and massing operations.
The exploded view from roof to timber frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 一樓維持對稱的軸線格局，而中軸與兩個天井上方的樓板被挖空，讓陽光抵達每一層。一連串分割、合併與重組體量的操作，最後才確定房間的配置。
captions: 改造前後的平面、立面與體量操作。
從屋頂到木構架的爆炸圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Interior model views show a tall atrium where balconies look down into the courtyard. The sloping roof lets sun and rain fall through the hollow floors, so the guests feel the house as a semi-outdoor space connected to the sky.
captions: Interior views of the model atrium.
The model with its balcony and timber railing.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型的室內視角呈現一處挑高中庭，陽台俯望天井。傾斜的屋頂讓陽光與雨水穿過鏤空的樓板落下，使旅人感受到一座與天空相連的半戶外之屋。
captions: 帶陽台與木欄杆的模型。

sections.heading: Hollowed Floors - Letting the Sky Back into a Courtyard House
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to treat the old house not as a shell to be emptied but as a set of rules still alive in its plan. The axis, the halls and the courtyards were read as a grammar of light and gathering, and every new room had to be written in that grammar rather than against it. The decisive move was subtraction: instead of adding volume, floors were cut open so that sun, rain and wind could descend through the building again. Drawings and models were tested for how they let weather in, not only for how they looked. The hotel that emerged is a quiet argument about preservation, holding that the most respectful renewal restores an old house its relation to the sky rather than freezing its facade.

zh-Hant.heading: 鏤空之樓-讓天空回到合院
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生不把老宅視為等待掏空的外殼，而是一套仍在平面中運作的規則。軸線、廳堂與天井被讀成一種關於光與聚集的文法，每一個新增的房間都必須以這套文法書寫，而不是與之對抗。關鍵的一步是減法：不再加建體量，而是剖開樓板，讓陽光、雨水與風重新穿過建築落下。圖面與模型不只檢驗外觀，更檢驗它們如何迎入天氣。最後的旅館成為一則安靜的保存論述：最溫柔的更新，不是凍結一道立面，而是讓一座老屋重新與天空、季節與光影相連。

pins.title: Self Residence
pins.description:
A protected tube house on a historic street is rebuilt inside its facade for a three-generation family, weaving private rooms around a shared spiral stair and rooftop garden.

Guangzhou, China | House renovation | Oct 2016 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自宅
zh-Hant.description:
一棟位於歷史街道、受保護的竹筒屋在保留立面的前提下重建內部，為三代同堂的家庭以一座共享的螺旋梯與屋頂花園串起私密的房間。

中國廣州｜住宅改造｜2016年10月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The model seen from the street.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The house stands on an old street once known for ivory workshops and is protected as a historic building, so its facade cannot change and it may not grow taller. The family of grandparents, parents and children also wanted a studio, a rooftop pond, a garage and a rented shop on the ground floor.
captions: A collage of the street and the towers around it.
Site analysis, design limits and the members of the family.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 房子位於一條曾以象牙作坊聞名的老街，屬於受保護的歷史建築，立面不能更動，也不能加高。祖父母、父母與孩子組成的家庭，還希望擁有工作室、屋頂魚池、車庫，以及一樓出租的店面。
captions: 街道與周邊高樓的拼貼。
基地分析、設計限制與家庭成員。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Furniture was studied as the thing a body touches most, and each piece was abstracted into a block. The blocks were grouped into rooms with different functions and measured against drawings of bodies sitting, reaching and talking.
captions: Rooms built from the blocks and drawings of body scale.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 家具被視為身體最常接觸的物件，每一件都被抽象為方塊。這些方塊再被組成不同機能的房間，並以坐、伸手與交談的人體尺度圖加以檢驗。
captions: 被抽象為簡單方塊的家具。
由方塊組成的房間與人體尺度圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The narrow plan was organised around a spiral stair that rises through all floors. Sections show light wells, a planted roof and stepped rooms set behind the kept facade.
captions: Plans of the three floors and the sloping roof.
The street elevation with the kept facade.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 狹長的平面以一座貫穿各層的螺旋梯組織起來。剖面顯示保留立面之後的採光井、種植屋頂與錯層的房間。
captions: 保留立面的街道立面圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The model opens to show rooms that each family member can own, joined by the stair and by shared spaces where everyone meets. It answers crowded living without sun or wind with an independent yet interrelated house.
captions: Interior views of the stair and the rooms.
The model opened from the side and from above.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 模型被打開，呈現每位家庭成員都能擁有的房間，並以樓梯與共享空間彼此相連。它以一棟既獨立又相互關聯的房子，回應過去擁擠、缺乏陽光與通風的居住狀態。
captions: 樓梯與房間的室內視角。
從側面與上方打開的模型。

sections.heading: Furniture as Measure - Three Generations Inside One Narrow Facade
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to start not from walls but from the objects a family actually touches. Chairs, tables and shelves were reduced to blocks, and the blocks were allowed to gather into rooms, so that space was measured by habit before it was measured by rule. Against the fixed facade and the height limit, this inversion turned constraint into precision: every centimetre of a narrow plan had to justify itself through a body sitting, reaching or talking. The spiral stair then became a social spine, a vertical street where generations cross paths without losing their own corners. The house that results proposes that privacy and togetherness are not opposites but two readings of the same carefully measured void.

zh-Hant.heading: 以家具為尺-一道窄立面裡的三代人
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生不從牆體出發，而從一個家庭真正觸碰的物件開始。椅子、桌子與櫃子被化約為方塊，方塊再聚合成房間，讓空間先以生活習慣丈量，再以法規丈量。面對不可更動的立面與限高，這種翻轉把限制轉化為精準：狹長平面中的每一公分，都必須以一個坐下、伸手或交談的身體來證明自己的必要。螺旋梯於是成為一條社交的脊椎、一條垂直的街道，讓不同世代在此交會，卻不失去各自的角落。這棟房子提出：私密與團聚並非對立，而是同一個被仔細丈量的空洞的兩種讀法。

pins.title: Exhibition Hall of the Institute of Design
pins.description:
An exhibition hall on a university campus is composed from cubes of human behaviour, arranged by a daily timetable and tested through a script of a day in the museum.

Guangzhou, China | Exhibition hall | Apr 2016 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 設計學院展覽館
zh-Hant.description:
一座位於大學校園的展覽館，由人的行為所轉化的方塊組成，依一日的時間表排列，並以「博物館的一天」劇本加以檢驗。

中國廣州｜展覽館｜2016年4月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Floor plans and rendered views of the hall.
展覽館的平面與渲染視角。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: People come to a museum for many reasons: to see an exhibition with friends, to attend a conference, to watch a performance outdoors or simply because an installation at the entrance caught their eye. The project began by dividing these behaviours into fragments and simplifying the objects that go with them.
captions: Drawings of behaviours enclosed in simple cubes.
Behaviour cubes joined into long sections.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 人們因各種理由來到博物館：與朋友看展、參加會議、在戶外觀賞演出，或只是被入口的裝置吸引而駐足。專題從把這些行為拆解為片段，並簡化與之對應的物件開始。
captions: 被收進簡單方塊的行為圖。
串連為長剖面的行為方塊。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Each cube became a programme unit, and physical cube models tested several arrangements on the campus site between a library and a footbridge. Sketches traced paths, water and planting around the site.
captions: Cube models of the programme arrangements.
Site sketches of paths and landscape.
The site plan of the hall on the campus.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 每個方塊成為一個機能單元，實體方塊模型在校園中圖書館與天橋之間的基地上測試了多種排列。草圖則描繪了基地周邊的路徑、水與植栽。
captions: 路徑與地景的基地草圖。
展覽館在校園中的配置圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Coloured plan studies sorted the units into zones, and a timetable charted when each room is used from morning to midnight. The pattern of use decided which spaces could be shared and which needed their own entrance.
captions: Coloured plan studies of the zones.
A timetable of room use through the day.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 彩色平面研究把單元分成不同區域，時間表則記錄每個房間從清晨到深夜的使用時段。這個使用模式決定了哪些空間可以共享，哪些需要獨立的入口。
captions: 一日房間使用的時間表。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A script follows staff, exhibits and visitors through one day, from opening the doors to the crowd leaving at midnight. Exploded axonometrics and elevations show galleries, a projection room, open-air stages and terraces stepping across the site.
captions: The space script drawn as exploded axonometrics.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一段劇本追隨工作人員、展品與訪客走過一天，從開門到午夜人群散去。爆炸軸測圖與立面呈現展廳、放映室、戶外舞台與跨越基地層層退台的平台。
captions: 以爆炸軸測圖繪製的空間劇本。

sections.heading: A Day in Cubes - Composing a Museum from Behaviour
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to look at a museum as a choreography before it is a building. Visitors, staff and exhibits were observed as figures in motion, and each gesture of waiting, talking, watching or carrying was given a small room of its own. These behaviour cubes became a vocabulary, and the design became a question of syntax: which rooms may overlap in time, which must stay apart, and how a single route can hold both the hurried and the lingering. The timetable acted as a hidden score beneath the plan, and the space script tested it as a narrative from opening to midnight. The hall that emerges suggests that programme is not a list of functions but a rhythm of lives sharing one ground.

zh-Hant.heading: 方塊裡的一天-以行為譜寫的博物館
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生在把博物館當成建築之前，先把它看成一段編舞。訪客、工作人員與展品被視為移動中的身影，等待、交談、觀看或搬運的每一個姿態，都被賦予一個屬於自己的小房間。這些行為方塊成為一套詞彙，設計則成為句法的問題：哪些房間可以在時間上重疊，哪些必須分開，一條路徑如何同時容納匆忙與流連。時間表是藏在平面之下的樂譜，空間劇本則把它化為從開館到午夜的敘事加以檢驗。最終的展館提出：機能不是一張用途清單，而是許多生活共享同一片地面的節奏。

pins.title: Rules and Construction
pins.description:
The hollowed interior behind a row of historic arcade facades is rebuilt as a craft market and theatre, using the unwritten rules of the old town to stage new public life.

Shantou, China | Arcade renewal | Mar 2018 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 規則與建造
zh-Hant.description:
一排歷史騎樓立面背後被掏空的內部，被重建為工藝市集與劇場，借用老城中不成文的規則來承載新的公共生活。

中國汕頭｜騎樓更新｜2018年3月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The old town as dark volumes with glimpses of craft life inside.
以深色體量呈現的老城，透出其中的工藝生活。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The architecture of a place follows its own rules, which silently decide its doors, windows, rooms and layouts. In this port city the old arcade district has emptied as the economic centre moved east, and behind the kept street facades many buildings stand demolished or abandoned.
captions: A map of the old part of town and its arcade buildings.
Street photographs from 1933 to 1990 and a day on the street today.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一個地方的建築遵循自己的規則，默默決定門、窗、房間與格局。在這座港口城市，隨著經濟重心東移，老騎樓區逐漸空洞，保留下來的街道立面背後，許多建築已被拆除或荒廢。
captions: 老城區及其騎樓建築的地圖。
1933年至1990年的街道照片與今日街道的一天。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The history of the arcade was traced from merchants who divided storefronts into narrow plots, living above and trading below. Photographs, density maps and comparisons with arcade streets in other cities explained how the type was formed and why it is no longer favoured.
captions: The past of the arcade with photographs and density maps.
An axonometric of the district as it is today.
The pillars, damaged structure and complex interiors investigated.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究追溯騎樓的歷史：商人把店面切分成窄長的地塊，樓上居住、樓下經商。照片、人口密度圖以及與其他城市騎樓街道的比較，說明了這種類型如何形成，又為何不再受青睞。
captions: 以照片與密度圖呈現的騎樓過去。
柱列、受損結構與複雜內部的調查。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The surviving pillars were kept as memories of past life and used to set out new floors. A theatre was added in the spare space behind the arcade, with separate routes for performers and audiences and a woven wire stage planted underneath.
captions: The new functions layered floor by floor.
The ground plan along the street.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 倖存的柱子被保留為往日生活的記憶，並用來定位新的樓層。騎樓背後的閒置空間加入一座劇場，表演者與觀眾的動線互不交錯，網狀的鋼絲舞台下方種植了植物。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The arcade becomes a market where residents teach, train and sell their crafts, with reading rooms, workshops and a balcony above. The stage reaches beyond the auditorium so that people passing in the street also become its audience.
captions: Views of the market, workshops, reading room and balcony.
The street elevation with the new theatre.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 騎樓成為一座市集，居民在此教學、培訓並販售自己的手藝，上方還有閱覽室、工作坊與陽台。舞台延伸到觀眾席之外，讓街上的路人也成為它的觀眾。
captions: 市集、工作坊、閱覽室與陽台的視角。
加入新劇場的街道立面。

sections.heading: Unwritten Rules - Staging Craft Behind an Emptied Arcade
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to read the old district as a text of unwritten rules rather than a collection of picturesque fronts. Narrow plots, shared pillars and the habit of living above and trading below were treated as a grammar that once produced intimacy between commerce and daily life. Research moved patiently through archives, photographs and density maps, so that every later gesture could claim a genealogy. The design then tested how these rules might be rewritten instead of imitated: pillars survive as memory, the theatre bends its circulation to keep performers and audiences apart, and the stage leaks into the street. The project argues that renewal is a form of translation, carrying the logic of a place into a new sentence without erasing its accent.

zh-Hant.heading: 不成文的規則-在空洞騎樓後上演手藝
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生把老街區讀成一部不成文規則的文本，而不只是一排如畫的立面。窄長的地塊、共用的柱列，以及樓上居住、樓下經商的習慣，被視為一套曾讓商業與日常生活親密交織的文法。研究耐心地穿行於檔案、照片與密度圖之間，讓後來的每一個動作都能找到自己的系譜。設計接著測試這些規則如何被改寫而非模仿：柱子以記憶的身分留存，劇場彎折動線讓表演者與觀眾各行其道，舞台則滲入街道。專題主張更新是一種翻譯，把一個地方的邏輯帶進新的句子，卻不抹去它的口音。

pins.title: TJS Elementary School
pins.description:
An elementary school is rethought by questioning what education is for, combining lessons from three case studies with a redesigned timetable to free space for movement.

Shenzhen, China | School design | Oct 2016 | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: TJS 小學
zh-Hant.description:
一所小學的再設計從追問教育的意義出發，結合三個案例研究的啟發與重新編排的課表，為活動釋放出空間。

中國深圳｜學校設計｜2016年10月｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: A long section through the classrooms, courts and pool.
穿過教室、球場與泳池的長剖面。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: The usual answer to a crowded school is to delete or transform rooms and add new floors. A written dialogue instead asked what education means, from learning which fruit to pick to the search for meaning, and whether a school needs so many classrooms at all.
captions: School subjects set out on a chessboard.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 面對擁擠的學校，常見的做法是刪改房間、加建樓層。專題改以一段書寫的對話，追問教育的意義，從學會摘哪一種果實到對意義的追尋，並質疑學校是否真的需要那麼多教室。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Three case studies were rebuilt in drawings and models: a stacked housing complex for its program boxes, a courtyard building for its materials, and a library for its rules of plan and elevation. Experiments with tree roots woven into concrete and a catalogue of standard room sizes followed.
captions: A case study of stacked housing in collaged sections.
A case study of a courtyard building with root-and-concrete tests.
A case study of a library and its pattern rules.
Standard scales of classrooms, courts and halls.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 三個案例被以圖面與模型重建：一座堆疊的集合住宅研究它的機能盒子，一座合院建築研究它的材料，一座圖書館研究它的平面與立面規則。接著進行把樹根編入混凝土的實驗，並整理出各類房間的標準尺寸。
captions: 以拼貼剖面研究的堆疊集合住宅案例。
合院建築案例與樹根混凝土實驗。
圖書館案例及其圖案規則。
教室、球場與大廳的標準尺度。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Foam cube models quickly combined the forms of the three cases. A redesigned curriculum spread subjects through the day, lowering the minimum number of teachers and the classrooms needed, so that large rooms could sit on top and free the ground.
captions: Foam and white models of the school.
The original and redesigned curriculum and classroom use.
An axonometric of the programme and its weighing columns.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 泡棉方塊模型快速組合三個案例的形式。重新設計的課表把各科分散在一天之中，降低所需的最少教師與教室數量，讓大型空間可以置於上方，釋放出地面。
captions: 學校的泡棉與白色模型。
原有與重新設計的課表及教室使用率。
機能與承重柱的軸測圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: A motion track loops over the school, linking a runway, a distributing square, a football field and a basketball court. Beneath it the classrooms, library and dining hall stack around open courts.
captions: Rendered views of the runway, square and courts.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 一條運動跑道環繞在學校上方，串起跑道、集散廣場、足球場與籃球場。其下方的教室、圖書館與餐廳圍繞開放的球場堆疊。
captions: 跑道、廣場與球場的渲染視角。

sections.heading: Fewer Rooms, More Ground - A School Rewritten by Its Timetable
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to suspend the reflex of adding classrooms and to ask instead what a school is for. A dialogue about meaning, survival and better living became the brief, and its doubts were allowed to shape the architecture. Case studies were not copied but dissected, each yielding one transferable idea, whether a stacking logic, a material experiment or a rule binding plan to elevation. The most radical tool turned out to be the timetable: by redistributing lessons through the day, fewer teachers and rooms were needed, and the saved area became ground for running, playing and meeting. The school that emerges treats time as a building material, proposing that education improves not by enclosing more children but by releasing more space for them to move.

zh-Hant.heading: 少一間教室-被課表改寫的學校
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生暫停「加蓋教室」的反射，轉而追問學校究竟為何存在。一段關於意義、生存與更好生活的對話成為設計任務書，其中的懷疑也被允許塑造建築。案例不被複製，而是被解剖，每一個都只萃取出一個可轉移的概念：堆疊的邏輯、材料的實驗，或把平面與立面綁在一起的規則。最激進的工具結果是課表：把課程重新分布於一天之中，所需的教師與教室隨之減少，省下的面積成為奔跑、遊戲與相遇的地面。這所學校把時間當成建材，提出教育的改善不在於容納更多孩子，而在於為孩子釋放更多可以自由移動的空間。

pins.title: En Garde, Prêt, Allez
pins.description:
The shifting triangles of balance in a fencer's attacks and parries are translated into two spatial models and two paintings.

Physical and digital model, painting | Movement and balance study | PVC boards, plastic sticks, Rhino, oil | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 預備、準備、開始
zh-Hant.description:
擊劍攻防中不斷變化的平衡三角，被轉譯為兩件空間模型與兩幅繪畫。

實體與數位模型、繪畫｜動作與平衡研究｜PVC板、塑膠棒、Rhino、油彩｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of rising triangles.
由上升三角形構成的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: In weekly fencing training, every attack and defence demands dynamic stability. The project began by studying each movement of a match to find where force was exerted on specific muscle groups.
captions: Fencing postures and the triangles of balance traced from them.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 在每週的擊劍訓練中，每一次進攻與防守都需要動態的穩定。專題從研究比賽中的每個動作開始，找出力量施加在哪些肌群上。
captions: 擊劍姿勢與從中描出的平衡三角。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: The analysis showed that overall stability rests on several triangular balance states that keep changing. The first approach drew the forward and backward steps of a match as one continuous winding chain of triangles.
captions: The continuous chain of triangles drawn as one form.
Sketches and studies isolating the moments of balance.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 分析顯示整體的穩定建立在數個不斷變化的三角平衡狀態上。第一種方法把比賽中的前進與後退畫成一條連續、蜿蜒的三角鏈。
captions: 畫成單一形體的連續三角鏈。
分離出平衡瞬間的草圖與研究。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The second approach isolated each moment of balance and kept the triangles apart, joining them with linear materials in between. It gives a clearer view of the relationship between each stable moment in time.
captions: The second model of separate moments joined by lines.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 第二種方法把每個平衡瞬間分離出來，讓三角形彼此分開，再以線性材料連接其間。這讓每個穩定瞬間在時間中的關係更加清楚。
captions: 以線連接分離瞬間的第二件模型。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The first model rises like an island of folded triangles. Two paintings then explored the form again through colour and perspective, one seen from another angle and one zooming into its structure.
captions: A painting of the form from another perspective.
A painting zooming into the structure.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 第一件模型如同一座由摺疊三角形構成的島嶼般升起。兩幅繪畫再以色彩與透視重新探索這個形體，一幅換一個角度觀看，一幅則放大進入它的結構。
captions: 從另一個角度描繪形體的繪畫。

sections.heading: Triangles of Balance - A Fencer's Stance Turned into Space
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to treat the body in combat as a source of structure rather than a subject to depict. Each lunge and recovery was slowed down into frames, and in every frame the hidden geometry of support was drawn out, two feet and a centre of gravity forming a triangle that never stays still. From there the work split into two theses about time: one model binds the moments into a continuous rising chain, the other holds them apart and lets thin lines carry the tension between them. Paintings then returned the abstraction to colour and depth. The project suggests that balance is not a state but a negotiation, and that architecture can be drawn from the instant before a movement resolves.

zh-Hant.heading: 平衡的三角-化為空間的擊劍架勢
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生把搏鬥中的身體視為結構的來源，而不是被描繪的對象。每一次弓步與回收被放慢成一格格畫面，在每一格中描出隱藏的支撐幾何：雙腳與重心構成一個從不靜止的三角形。作品由此分成兩種關於時間的論點：一件模型把瞬間綁成一條連續上升的鏈，另一件讓瞬間彼此分離，只以細線承載其間的張力。繪畫再把抽象帶回色彩與深度。專題提出：平衡不是一種狀態，而是一場協商，建築可以從一個動作尚未完成、仍在搖擺的那一刻被提煉出來。

pins.title: Rethinking Waste Plastics
pins.description:
Used straws and cups collected from restaurants, beaches and a cafeteria are rebuilt into prototypes that mimic the internal structure of corals.

Space model | Zero-waste biomimicry study | Waste plastics | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 重新思考廢塑膠
zh-Hant.description:
從餐廳、海灘與學生餐廳收集來的廢棄吸管與杯子，被重新組構成模仿珊瑚內部結構的原型。

空間模型｜零廢棄仿生研究｜廢塑膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final coral-like models of waste plastics.
以廢塑膠做成、如珊瑚般的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Reading about biomimicry in architecture led to a zero-waste design theme for an architecture club: everyday waste would become material for creations that cost nothing. The question was how plastic waste could be reused to give back to the ecological environment.
captions: An inspiration collage of plastics and coral.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一本關於建築仿生學的書，促成了建築社團的「零廢棄永續設計」主題：日常廢棄物將成為零成本創作的材料。問題在於，廢塑膠如何被再利用，回饋給生態環境。
captions: 塑膠與珊瑚的靈感拼貼。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Corals were analysed through sketches of their branching structures, their growth and the way their internal cells support the whole. These notes became rules for joining small plastic pieces.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 研究以草圖分析珊瑚的分枝結構、生長方式，以及內部細胞如何支撐整體。這些筆記成為連接小塊塑膠的規則。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Straws and cups were collected, cut and tested in small experiments of folding, linking and stacking. The trials were compared to find which joints were strong enough to grow into a larger frame.
captions: Experiments with joints and small frames.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 吸管與杯子被收集、裁切，並在摺疊、連接與堆疊的小實驗中測試。這些試驗彼此比較，找出哪一種接點夠強，能長成更大的框架。
captions: 接點與小型框架的實驗。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The final models rise as stacked rings of curled plastic around a transparent core, recalling coral colonies. A detailed drawing records the whole as a net of triangulated cells.
captions: A drawing of the structure as triangulated cells.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 最終模型以捲曲塑膠片構成的層層環圈圍繞透明核心升起，令人想起珊瑚群體。一幅細密的繪圖把整體記錄為三角化的細胞網絡。
captions: 把結構畫成三角化細胞的圖。

sections.heading: Second Reef - Waste Plastics Learning to Grow like Coral
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to look at waste as an ecology waiting for a structure. Straws and cups were collected not as rubbish but as a supply of identical units, and corals were studied as a precedent for how identical units become a living whole. The research insisted on mechanism over appearance: branching, cellular support and growth were drawn until they could be turned into joining rules. Each experiment then tested a rule in the hand, accepting failure as information. The final colonies of curled plastic read as both object and argument, that sustainability can be a method of making rather than a theme to illustrate, and that the cheapest and most ordinary material can carry the most precise thinking.

zh-Hant.heading: 第二座礁-學著像珊瑚生長的廢塑膠
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生把廢棄物看成一個等待結構的生態。吸管與杯子被收集起來，不是當作垃圾，而是一批相同的單元；珊瑚則被當成先例，研究相同的單元如何長成一個活的整體。研究堅持機制先於外觀：分枝、細胞支撐與生長被反覆描繪，直到能轉化為連接的規則。每一個實驗再以雙手檢驗一條規則，並把失敗當作資訊。最後由捲曲塑膠構成的群體，既是物件也是論點：永續可以是一種製作方法，而不只是被圖解的主題；最廉價的材料，也能承載最精準的思考。

pins.title: Among the Desert
pins.description:
A public shelter for extreme weather is shaped from flowing curves, with hedgehog-spine facades of algae that clean the air and adapt to the climate.

Digital model and prototype | Biomimetic facade design | Rhino, Grasshopper, plastics | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 沙漠之中
zh-Hant.description:
一座為極端氣候設計的公共避難空間，由流動的曲線塑形，並以仿刺蝟棘刺的藻類立面淨化空氣、因應氣候。

數位模型與原型｜仿生立面設計｜Rhino、Grasshopper、塑膠｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The public space set in the desert.
位於沙漠中的公共空間。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Climate change makes extreme weather more intense and frequent, and it has taken many lives across Africa. The project proposed a sustainable public space in Niger where citizens can rest and meet in accessible shelter during extreme weather.
captions: A map of extreme weather events in Africa.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 氣候變遷讓極端天氣更加劇烈與頻繁，在非洲奪走了許多生命。專題提出在尼日設置一處永續的公共空間，讓市民在極端天氣中能於便利可達的遮蔽下休息與交流。
captions: 非洲極端天氣事件地圖。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Open, flowing and interlinking curves formed the plan, and the spines of a hedgehog were studied as irregular triangular prisms. Algae was chosen as the facade material for its exchange of gases and heat.
captions: Hedgehog spines and algae studied for the facade.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 開放、流動並相互連結的曲線構成平面，刺蝟的棘刺則被研究為不規則的三角柱。立面材料選擇藻類，因為它能交換氣體與熱。
captions: 為立面研究的刺蝟棘刺與藻類。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The facades were generated in Grasshopper from the spine geometry. Polluted air enters at the bottom of each panel, meets microorganisms in the algae and leaves as fresh oxygen from the top, while the algae also filters daylight.
captions: Principles of the algae facade and its applications.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 立面以棘刺的幾何在Grasshopper中生成。污濁的空氣從每片板材底部進入，與藻類中的微生物接觸，再從頂部以新鮮氧氣釋出，藻類同時也過濾日光。
captions: 藻類立面的原理與應用。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The biomimetic units were also built as two prototypes in water: an aquaponics device that links fish and plants, and an artificial fish habitat that mimics coral to give shelter and breeding space. Both tests show the same geometry working beyond the building.
captions: The aquaponics prototype in a tank with fish.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些仿生單元也被做成兩件水中原型：一件連結魚與植物的魚菜共生裝置，以及一件模仿珊瑚、提供庇護與繁殖空間的人工魚礁。兩項測試都顯示同一套幾何能在建築之外運作。
captions: 魚缸中的魚菜共生原型。

sections.heading: Breathing Skin - A Shelter That Learns from Spines and Algae
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to begin with a fact rather than a form: extreme weather costs lives, and the most exposed people often lack a place to wait it out. From that ethical starting point, nature was consulted as an engineer. The hedgehog offered a geometry of protection, the alga a metabolism of air and light, and parametric tools translated both into a skin that performs rather than decorates. The work then crossed scales and media, testing the same units as underwater prototypes where fish and plants could inhabit them. The project argues that biomimicry is most convincing when it borrows processes instead of shapes, and that a façade can be imagined as a living organ breathing for a community.

zh-Hant.heading: 會呼吸的皮膚-向棘刺與藻類學習的避難所
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生從一個事實而非形式出發：極端天氣奪走生命，而最暴露於危險中的人，往往缺少一處可以安然等待的地方。從這個倫理的起點出發，自然被當成工程師來請教。刺蝟提供保護的幾何，藻類提供空氣與光的代謝，參數化工具則把兩者轉譯為一層真正運作、而非裝飾的皮膚。作品再跨越尺度與媒材，把相同的單元做成水中原型，讓魚與植物得以棲居其中。專題主張：仿生學在借用過程而非形狀時最有說服力，一道立面也可以被想像成一個為社群呼吸的活器官。

pins.title: Intangibly Visible
pins.description:
An installation deconstructs the timber frame of a traditional Chinese temple into a grid of sticks, wrapped in dry-ice smoke that makes heritage both present and fading.

Installation | Heritage and deconstruction study | Wooden sticks, dry ice, cellophane | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 無形可見
zh-Hant.description:
一件裝置把傳統中國寺廟的木構架解構為木棒格網，並以乾冰煙霧包覆，讓文化遺產同時顯現又消逝。

裝置｜文化遺產與解構研究｜木棒、乾冰、玻璃紙｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The installation glowing in the dark.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Traditional temple structures are disappearing, and the craftsmanship behind them is fading from everyday view. The project sought to capture the essence of these frames and raise a sense of urgency for preserving cultural heritage.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 傳統寺廟建築正在消失，背後的工藝也逐漸淡出日常視野。專題試圖捕捉這些構架的精髓，喚起保存文化遺產的急迫感。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Drawings studied the architectural forms of temples, their construction methods and their internal structure, and then extracted the frame alone. Posts, beams and brackets were redrawn as a repeating grid.
captions: Drawings of temple forms, construction and the extracted frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 繪圖研究了寺廟的建築形式、營造方法與內部結構，再單獨提取出構架。柱、樑與斗栱被重新繪製為重複的格網。
captions: 寺廟形式、營造方式與提取構架的繪圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The frame was rebuilt at installation scale from wooden sticks, a material that recalls ancient building techniques, and partly deconstructed so that it reads as fragments of a temple. Cellophane and lights were set inside to colour the frame, which measures 1100 by 1100 by 1300 mm.
captions: The production process and details of the frame.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 構架以木棒在裝置尺度重建，這種材料令人想起古老的營造技術，並被部分解構，讓它讀起來像是寺廟的片段。內部置入玻璃紙與燈光為構架上色，整體尺寸為1100×1100×1300毫米。
captions: 構架的製作過程與細部。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: Light and shadow on the timber create an ethereal atmosphere, while smoke from dry ice drifts through the grid. The play of the intangible and the visible becomes a metaphor for the fragility of heritage and the nostalgia for traditional temple building in the city.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 光影在木材上營造出空靈的氛圍，乾冰的煙霧在格網間飄移。無形與可見的交錯，成為文化遺產之脆弱，以及城市中對傳統寺廟營造之鄉愁的隱喻。

sections.heading: Smoke and Frame - Heritage Held Between Presence and Loss
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to approach heritage through structure rather than ornament. Temple drawings were made until the frame could stand on its own, stripped of roofs and colour, revealing a logic of posts, beams and repetition that carries the memory of a craft. Building it again in sticks became an act of study by the hand, and partial deconstruction kept the work honest and humble about what has already been lost. The decisive addition was atmosphere: dry-ice smoke and low light let the frame appear and dissolve in turn. The installation thus stages preservation as an experience of time, proposing that what we risk losing is not only an object but our very ability to see it clearly.

zh-Hant.heading: 煙與構架-在存在與消逝之間的遺產
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生透過結構而非裝飾來接近文化遺產。寺廟的繪圖反覆進行，直到構架能夠獨自站立：剝除屋頂與色彩之後，柱、樑與重複的邏輯被揭露出來，承載著一門工藝的記憶。以木棒重新搭建，成為一種用雙手進行的研究，而局部的解構則誠實地承認那些已經失去的部分。決定性的加入是氛圍：乾冰煙霧與低照度讓構架輪流顯現與消融。這件裝置因此把保存演繹為一種時間的經驗，提出我們可能失去的不只是一件物件，還有看見它的能力。

pins.title: Precipitation
pins.description:
A space model imitates trees, waves, waterfalls and caves to imagine architecture that reunites with nature and lets people draw emotional value from it.

Space model | Nature and senses study | Wooden sticks, stone powder clay, cellophane, PVC boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 沉澱
zh-Hant.description:
一件空間模型模仿樹、海浪、瀑布與洞穴，想像一種與自然重新結合、讓人從中獲得情感價值的建築。

空間模型｜自然與感官研究｜木棒、石粉黏土、玻璃紙、PVC板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: The final model of branches, waves and wooden houses.
由枝幹、海浪與木屋構成的最終模型。

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Architecture evolved from caves to skyscrapers, and after many social milestones most spaces were commercialised into square boxes. The project imagined a new evolution in which architecture reunites with nature and people regain an inner connection to space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 建築從洞穴演進到摩天大樓，經歷許多社會里程碑之後，多數空間被商品化為方盒子。專題想像一種新的演化：建築與自然重新結合，人們重新找回與空間的內在連結。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: A photo collage gathered four natural elements, the tree, the waves, the waterfall and the caves, and a drawing combined them into one composition. Each element was paired with a material and a way of making.
captions: The inspiration collage and the design drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 一張照片拼貼收集了四種自然元素：樹、海浪、瀑布與洞穴，一幅繪圖再把它們組合成一個構圖。每一種元素都對應一種材料與製作方式。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Laser-cut Y-shaped PVC pieces mimic branches and pass through the spaces as supports for wooden houses and hallways. Curled water-texture paper forms waves, a blue PVC cone becomes a waterfall and stone powder clay shapes curving caves.
captions: Shaping the clay and branches by hand.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 雷射切割的Y形PVC片模仿枝幹，穿過空間，成為木屋與廊道的支撐。捲曲的水紋紙形成海浪，藍色PVC圓錐成為瀑布，石粉黏土則塑造出彎曲的洞穴。
captions: 以雙手塑造黏土與枝幹。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The finished model lets each element awaken a different sense, so that people can create a resonance between nature and their hearts. Wooden houses perch among the branches above the waves and caves.
captions: Two views of the final model.
Details of the houses, branches and waves.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 完成的模型讓每一種元素喚醒不同的感官，使人在自然與內心之間產生共鳴。木屋棲息在海浪與洞穴上方的枝幹之間。
captions: 木屋、枝幹與海浪的細部。

sections.heading: After the Box - Four Elements Settling into a Dwelling
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to frame a large question in a small object: what comes after the commercial box that most buildings have become. Rather than answer with theory alone, nature was broken into four legible elements, each standing for a sensation, the shelter of a tree, the rhythm of waves, the energy of falling water, the enclosure of a cave. Every element was then assigned its own material logic, so that meaning was carried by technique, a cut branch, a curled sheet, a cone, a pressed hollow. The model became a manifesto in miniature, where tiny houses nest among these forces. It proposes that architecture may grow more humane by returning to the senses from which it first emerged.

zh-Hant.heading: 方盒之後-沉澱為居所的四種元素
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生用一件小物件框住一個大問題：在多數建築淪為商業方盒之後，接下來會是什麼。與其只以理論回答，自然被拆解為四種可被閱讀的元素，各自代表一種感受：樹的庇護、海浪的節奏、落水的能量、洞穴的包覆。每一種元素再被賦予自己的材料邏輯，讓意義由技術承載：一段切出的枝幹、一張捲曲的紙、一個圓錐、一處壓出的凹洞。模型成為一份縮小的宣言，小小的屋子棲身於這些力量之間。它提出：建築或許能透過回到它最初誕生的感官，而變得更有人性。

pins.title: The Pulse of Nature
pins.description:
A sculpture of clay, sticks and branches recalls imagined childhood spaces, intertwining valleys, sea spray, coral and branches like the vessels of a body.

Sculpture and drawing | Nature and memory study | Stone powder clay, sticks, plaster, branches | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 自然的脈搏
zh-Hant.description:
一件以黏土、木棒與樹枝構成的雕塑，喚回童年想像中的空間，讓山谷、浪花、珊瑚與枝幹如身體的血管般交織。

雕塑與繪圖｜自然與記憶研究｜石粉黏土、木棒、石膏、樹枝｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: As a child the student drew abstract sketches of spaces imagined every night before sleep, without the resources to explore them. Later reading, workshops and studios offered a way to give those memories form.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 學生童年時，每晚睡前都會畫下腦中想像的抽象空間，卻沒有資源去探索它們。後來的閱讀、工作坊與工作室經驗，提供了把這些記憶賦予形體的途徑。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Pen drawings studied the surfaces of the sculpture in detail, tracing how folds, pores and branches turn into one another. The drawings guided where each texture should grow.
captions: A pen drawing of a partial detail.
A second pen drawing of a partial detail.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 鋼筆繪圖細緻地研究雕塑的表面，描繪皺褶、孔洞與枝幹如何彼此轉化。這些繪圖決定了每一種質地應該在何處生長。
captions: 另一幅局部細節的鋼筆畫。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: Stone powder clay was laid over a structural support of sticks and plaster to depict mountain valleys, sea spray, blooming coral and growing branches. The clay was modelled by hand so that the parts merge without seams.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 石粉黏土覆蓋在木棒與石膏的支撐結構上，塑造出山谷、浪花、綻放的珊瑚與生長的枝幹。黏土以雙手塑形，讓各部分無縫地融合。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The elements intertwine like the blood vessels of a body, expressing the wonder of nature and the pulsing rhythm of life. The sculpture is shown both coloured and in white.
captions: The sculpture in white from two sides.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 這些元素如身體的血管般交織，表達自然的奇妙與生命脈動的節奏。雕塑同時以彩色與白色兩種狀態呈現。

sections.heading: Vessels of Memory - A Childhood Landscape Given Flesh
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to take an early, private imagination seriously as design material. The spaces once sketched before sleep were not treated as nostalgia but as the first evidence of a spatial instinct, and the task was to give them a body. Clay over a skeleton of sticks allowed growth to be modelled rather than assembled, so that valley, spray, coral and branch could merge without seams. Pen drawings then slowed the eye down, recording patiently how one texture passes into another. The finished sculpture thus becomes a portrait of continuity between memory and making, suggesting that the origin of architectural thinking often lies in the landscapes a child invents long before ever learning to draw a plan.

zh-Hant.heading: 記憶的血管-被賦予血肉的童年地景
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生把早年私密的想像，認真地視為設計的材料。那些睡前畫下的空間，不被當成懷舊，而是一種空間本能的最初證據，任務在於為它們賦予身體。黏土覆蓋在木棒骨架之上，讓生長可以被塑造而非組裝，使山谷、浪花、珊瑚與枝幹無縫地融合。鋼筆繪圖再讓目光慢下來，記錄一種質地如何過渡到另一種。這件雕塑成為記憶與製作之間連續性的肖像，提出建築思考的起源，往往藏在孩子學會畫平面圖之前就已悄悄發明的那些奇幻地景之中。

pins.title: Retro Lamp
pins.description:
A timber lamp blends retro motifs of the city, such as street lights, ferries, Chinese patterns and a landmark tower, with a geometric frame.

Product design | Retro lamp | Wooden boards, light bulb | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 復古燈
zh-Hant.description:
一盞木製燈具把城市的復古意象，如街燈、渡輪、中式紋樣與地標高塔，融入幾何框架之中。

產品設計｜復古燈具｜木板、燈泡｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: A design and technology course asked for a lamp with a retro theme. The project looked for a way to balance the preservation of traditional culture with the innovation of new expressions.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 一門設計與科技課程要求設計一盞復古主題的燈具。專題試圖在保存傳統文化與創新表現之間找到平衡。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Sketches explored many design ideas inspired by the yellow street light, the harbour ferry, classic Chinese patterns and an iconic bank tower, each combining traditional motifs with geometric forms. Notes beside each idea weighed its structure and light.
captions: Design ideas and details sketched with notes.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 草圖探索了多種設計構想，靈感來自黃色街燈、港口渡輪、經典中式紋樣與一座標誌性的銀行大樓，每一個都把傳統圖騰與幾何形式結合。每個構想旁的筆記衡量了它的結構與光線。
captions: 附註記的設計構想與細部草圖。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The chosen idea was built as a slender frame of wooden boards, with angular arms that hold the light source at the centre. The faceted outline recalls the stepped profile of the tower.
captions: The timber frame of the lamp from two angles.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 選定的構想以木板做成纖細的框架，以帶角度的支臂把光源托在中央。多面的輪廓令人想起那座高塔層層收分的剪影。
captions: 燈具木框架的兩個角度。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: When lit, the bulb glows within the faceted frame, casting a vintage charm that marries traditional and contemporary facets. Its shadows draw the frame again on the surrounding walls.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 點亮之後，燈泡在多面的框架中發光，散發出結合傳統與當代的復古韻味。它的影子在周圍的牆上再次描繪出框架。

sections.heading: Light of the Old City - Geometry Distilled from Street Memory
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to collect the city before designing an object for it. Familiar signs of an older urban life, a sodium street lamp, the silhouette of a ferry, a lattice pattern, a faceted tower, were drawn side by side until a shared geometry began to appear. The sketches worked as an archive and a laboratory at once, testing which memories could survive abstraction. The chosen frame keeps only angles and proportions, letting nostalgia be felt without being quoted. Building it in timber then tied the idea to the precision of making. The lamp proposes that heritage can enter everyday design not as decoration but as a distilled rhythm of lines that a city has long been drawing.

zh-Hant.heading: 老城之光-從街道記憶提煉的幾何
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生在為城市設計一件物件之前，先收集這座城市。舊日城市生活中熟悉的符號：一盞鈉燈街燈、一艘渡輪的剪影、一種窗花紋樣、一座多面的高塔，被並排描繪，直到共同的幾何開始浮現。草圖同時是一座檔案庫與一間實驗室，檢驗哪些記憶能夠在抽象之後存活。最後選定的框架只保留角度與比例，讓懷舊可以被感受，卻不被直接引用。以木材製作，再把概念綁定在製作的精準之上。這盞燈提出：文化遺產可以不以裝飾的姿態，而以一座城市長久以來描繪的線條節奏，進入日常的設計。

pins.title: Exercise Bike for the Elderly
pins.description:
A compact octagonal exercise device lets older people keep fit at home, combining pedalling, a hand crank and a screen holder in one wooden body.

Product design | Home exercise equipment | Wooden boards | Student Project | Design Mentor: Yu Chun Tsai

zh-Hant.title: 長者健身單車
zh-Hant.description:
一件精巧的八角形健身裝置，讓長者在家中保持健康，把踩踏、手搖曲柄與螢幕支架整合在同一個木製機身中。

產品設計｜居家健身器材｜木板｜學生作品｜Yu Chun Tsai 設計指導

captions: Rendered views of the exercise bike.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.body: Older people often have little space at home and few reminders to exercise. The project designed household sports equipment that encourages daily exercise in limited space.

zh-Hant.heading: 問題
zh-Hant.body: 長者在家中往往空間有限，也缺乏運動的提醒。專題設計了一件居家運動器材，鼓勵長者在有限的空間中每天運動。

sections.heading: Research
sections.body: Following a user-centred approach, sketches explored handles, pedals and a hoop-like track, with notes on simplicity, convenience, ergonomics and safety. One idea added a counter with lights to make exercise more playful.

zh-Hant.heading: 研究
zh-Hant.body: 依循以使用者為中心的設計方法，草圖探索了把手、踏板與環形軌道，並註記簡單、便利、人體工學與安全等考量。其中一個構想加入帶燈光的計數器，讓運動更有趣味。

sections.heading: Development
sections.body: The body was resolved as an octagon of wooden boards that combines several functions in one, with a holder on top for a tablet. Measured drawings fixed the dimensions of each part.
captions: A drawing of the octagonal body with the screen holder.

zh-Hant.heading: 推演
zh-Hant.body: 機身被確定為以木板構成的八角形，把多種機能整合為一，頂部設有平板支架。尺寸圖確定了每個部件的大小。
captions: 帶螢幕支架的八角機身繪圖。

sections.heading: Outcome
sections.body: The prototype was tested by pedalling while seated and by following a video on the screen, showing how exercise can fit into a small room at home. The device can be moved and stored in a corner after use.

zh-Hant.heading: 成果
zh-Hant.body: 原型以坐姿踩踏並跟隨螢幕上的影片進行測試，展示運動如何融入家中的小房間。使用後，裝置可以移動並收納在角落。

sections.heading: Small Room, Daily Motion - Designing Exercise Around an Ageing Body
sections.body: The guidance first led the student to begin with a person rather than a product. The limited reach, strength and patience of an ageing body, together with the narrow rooms of the city, were treated as the true brief, and every sketch was asked whether it would be simple, safe and inviting enough to be used every day. Functions were gathered into one compact octagon so that the device could stand quietly in a corner, and a screen holder turned solitary exercise into something shared. Testing the prototype in a real seat closed the loop between drawing and use. The project suggests that care can be expressed through form, and that good design for the elderly is measured by how naturally it enters a daily routine.

zh-Hant.heading: 小房間裡的日常運動-圍繞老去身體的設計
zh-Hant.body: 指導過程先引導學生從一個人而非一件產品開始。老去身體有限的伸展、力氣與耐性，加上城市中狹小的房間，被視為真正的設計任務書；每一張草圖都要回答：它是否簡單、安全，並且吸引人到足以每天使用。各種機能被收攏進一個精巧的八角形中，讓裝置能安靜地立於角落，而螢幕支架則讓獨自的運動變成可以分享的事。在真實的座位上測試原型，完成了從圖面到使用的循環。專題提出：關懷可以透過形式表達，為長者所做的好設計，取決於它能多自然地走進日常作息。
